- Hotline to report misconduct including sexual, verbal and bully
- Perm employee make up your talent base, if you treat TAP like babies please show respect to per employee with a genuine "hello" in the hallway
- Unproductive meetings waste tons of time with disjointed teams
- Figure out a better pay model to keep up with competition
pros:
- Good company reputation
- Strong balance sheet
- I actually think the Leadership at the top meant well
cons:
- Undisciplined mid level managers actually engage in office affairs, bully and belittle others
- Under industry average pay for Software Engs
- Frequent change of management impedes promotion
- Workers with common culture often engage conversations in mother tones (Spanish / Russian / Indians) in office common areas, unprofessionally shouting over shoulders in a Tech org
- TAP graduates get a preferential treatment over permanent employees while in the programme, well that is about how long it lasts
- Traders just shout and curse all the time, guess that is nothing new

summary: Decent Pay/Benefits,  But Caution Regarding Layoffs!
advice: People aren't just numbers, people have lives.  Treat people fairly.  When business needs change, make the people you are displacing a priority if you truly care about them.  Help them find positions elsewhere in the company.  Stop trying to manage people outside of work, they don't report to you 24x7.
pros: Decent base pay and benefits (paid time off, medical/dental)
cons:
Several times a year they do random layoffs. The sad part is they do nothing to help employees who are being displaced find employment elsewhere in the company. 
Bonus money tends to stay at the top levels. It should be fair across the board based on your grade level you should know what your expected bonus will be, not based on who are favorites. They will shave some of the money you are suppose to receive as part of your bonus to give it to someone else they want to promote or who is a favorite. Too much politics in most departments.

summary: Ok, but don't expect a lot out of management
advice: Do what other companies do - fire the folks who are underperforming at year-end.  Don't just keep them because they haven't done anything egregious.  Also, too focussed on cost-cutting.  Should be more focussed on the overall efficiency of the firm.
pros: If you want job stability, this is the company for you!  Work life balance is pretty decent too but mainly because no one cares a whole lot about whether you're in the office being productive.
cons: If you want intelligent people to work for, however, look elsewhere.  Management at JPM leaves much to be desired.  Part of the problem is that it's difficult to get rid of people here once they're hired.  So a lot of the good people end up leaving and all the bad ones are left behind.  Might be better in more senior front office roles but anything that's MO or Operational is not the best.  Good place to start out but once you've spent a few years here, move on.

advice: Each year, we were expected to do more with less.  Is there a tipping point?
pros: The company has their act together with processes and procedures. I found most of the people to be great to work with and very professional. There was flexibility since most salaried positions have a high degree of ownership - no one is looking over your shoulder, you are expected to know your job and do it. There are great opportunities for women. You get out what you put in.
cons: It is a large organization with constant change that can be hard to keep up with. You need to be there for a while to understand which system to request to get something done. If you have an issue of some sort, it could take a while finding the right ticket system or person to help. Most help is in a chat room or FAQ as self help. Expectations are that you will cultivate your career, constantly grow and give more. That can be both a pro or con.

advice: A more efficient and faster recruiting, screening and on boarding process. Floating employee from each job family available to assist those with a smaller staff in the event of an employee calling in sick, Leave of absence, termination.
pros: Leader in the financial industry. Forward thinking and constantly looking for ways to improve its technology to better serve the customer and the employees. The benefits (medical, dental, 401k, stock purchase...)are also pretty good and there are still a great variety of tools available to employees. Pay for performance and great growth opportunity.
cons: Recent employee reduction has added stress to current employees with the increase of work flow and responsibilities. You pray that your employees will show up to work on time and don't call in sick otherwise it makes it pretty difficult to run a branch. Branch managers have to fill in the gap in the branch functioning as tellers and bankers. Career mobility within different lines of business not facilitated to internal candidates.

advice: When there are HR complaints, someone other than the direct manager should do the investigating & limited information should be shared with them to avoid conflict of interest & to make sure that the "confidentiality" is not broken.
pros: The healthcare benefits were great and the amount of time off provided is pretty generous.
cons: Local management was very abusive and extremely unprofessional. This is where the "over promised, under delivered" comes into play. I was promised during my interview that I would be working with experts and professionals but my manager was nothing but unprofessional and lacked knowledge. She had no interest in her team and only cared about her metrics. She was verbally abusive to employees, cursed all the time in front of clients, and would only cared about sales and would get mad if we would only help clients without getting anything out of it. After several HR complaints, her boss (Market Director) would always cover for her & would give her confidential information about the complaints because they were friends and so they started transferring and coaching out anyone that they knew had complained to HR. Honestly, working here was one of my biggest regrets in my career and the most toxic working environment I've ever experienced.

summary: Good Place to Work - Lots of Red Tape
advice: Give employees a bit of breathing room. Stop creating such a stiff culture and stop favoring clients' children; some of which are spoiled and incompetent.
pros: JP Morgan is a pretty good place to work. The company is well run considering the size. Pay is decent, most people are nice, there is room to move up due to its large size.
cons:
A lot of red tape and bureaucracy. New rules and regulations every single day; JP Morgan goes overboard in complying. They do that to cover themselves, but it becomes a massive burden on employees who spend all their time trying to comply and less time doing actual work. 
Also, at least in the Private Bank, there are a lot of employees who are children of clients. You can tell they are treated more favorably than employees who got there on sweat and effort. I can't blame them for doing it because it helps the business, but it's just plain unfair.

summary: Big Brand spoiled with Cheap People Managers
advice: Its waste to give any advice as this company runs on the plank of un ethical policies under the supervision of crap people managers who can't even code.
pros:
Brand Name
New state of the art building
Pay
cons: Of all the companies I have worked for, JPMC is the most political and un ethical company.Since it is a big Bank with multiple LOBs, can't generalize but from my experience in CT LOB, I can say this is a company where your political inclination and favouritism plays a major role in your career progression. People with mediocre skills can become VPs and even EDs with some communication skills and political acumen. People with good technical skills and who work hard are often sidelined.There is no HR policy as such and waste Indian managers and some times onsite managers from QA background decides a developers fate. Strongly recommended to avoid this crap political company unless you are left with no offers other than service based companies. Because of some worst managers, people are moving to other companies (like Wells Fargo) in bulk and still this so called ethical company can't realise the ground reality and make necessary corrections to motivate employees from crap mid to senior level management.

summary: No Exit Interview. Not well functioning management survey.
advice: Hope those controls around managements could become really powerful tools.
pros: Big name. A big company with a lot opportunities. JPM offers a lot of diversified products, so if you able to learn quickly, it’s a good place to get feet in the finance.
cons:
One executive was really proud that JPM takes very serious about the exit interview. He also shared his view about the importance of exit interview during one of the town hall meeting. But actual he doesn’t realized there may be no exit interview at all. 

There’s also such a thing called management survey. The last team I worked with got low survey rate. But you can tell the managers don’t care about it at all. She /he knows this kind of survey won’t hurt her /him at all, even with way below average survey rate and about 80% of turn over rate in a year. 

One word keeps showing up in JPM’s reviews is bureaucracy. I also think so. You need some luck when picking up a team. If you have bad management, there’s really not much you can do. Because those control around effectively management is not really functioning.

summary: JPMorgan Chase your tail. Bullying and bureaucracy in the guilded prison.
advice: Threats and coercion will not earn you the loyalty of your employees. The whole 'escalation first ask questions later' game has to stop. Just because you remove all freedom from your employees does not mean that they will do what you expect.
pros: Compensation is good compared to similar jobs at other companies.
cons: Corporate culture is sh*t.  ZERO respect for personal time. ZERO work/life balance. You are expected to be available at any time whatsoever subject to the whims of management with little or no notice. 2 A.M. conference calls are commonplace. Although benefits are offered, they are not expected to be taken advantage of.  Bureaucracy is ridiculous. The entire modus operandi of this company is to find some hapless person to push your work onto by whatever means necessary.  Your refusal to accept more work, regardless of existing commitments will result in you being reported to your superiors regardless of the circumstances.

advice:
Treat the tenured employees with more respect.  Five years ago, I would need a paper and pen to write the names of people with more than 15 years. Now they can be counted on one hand. Have one of them speak to a new hire class-it may inspire the new people  to stick around.  

Raising the bar on performance standards to make it virtually impossible to meet, only to give reps a skimpy raise is just wrong.  It's one thing to "challenge" employees, it's another to create unattainable goals to prevent a large payout later when they exceed goals.  

Actually utilize the feedback in the electronic exit interview instead of ignoring the comments.
pros:
Name recognition-looks great on resume for outside opportunities

Great Benefits

Fellow tenured employees are still good friends to this day
cons:
Do not think for yourself-"follower" philosophy vs. "leading by example"

Micro-management-makes it impossible to "meet standards" due to changing goals/matrix

Managers that care more about how they appear to upper management than about the team

No respect for tenured employees

Poor Communication across the board

advice: Please work with upper management to allow the lower end of the workforce to have a nice quality of life. Or a good work-life balance, i have seen managers take advantage of people, and scare them with their jobs. Or the fact they will lose it, if they don't bend over backwards for them.
pros: You can make a lot of money, and they offer great training.
cons: Your work life balance will be off. When I started, the bank was called bank one. What a wonderful bank to work for. Once Chase bought the bank, things started changing. You have to adapt to change, which is fine. But they beat down a lot of employees, that is why they are always hiring. As many employees leave after being beat down so many years. One other thing, corporate politics are in play always. District Manager hold employees back, if it is going to mess with their district. Movement is allowed, but you have to jump through hoops to get there.

summary: Fast paced environment but very dense hierarchical structure
advice:
Open up the culture.
Hire smart talent that is on the cutting edge of information. Perhaps time to break from the legacy Ohio roots that simply don't have it.
Reward merit, not contacts
pros: Work moves fast and efficiently as one would expect at JPMC. Cross-functionality is well organized and most things run like a well oiled machine.
cons:
Despite the efficiency of the processes, I found a surprising lack of talent, particularly in the midwestern employees vs the NYC folks. Also there is a big cultural gap between the midwestern and the NYC folks - mostly in terms of depth of understanding of issues that are considered common knowledge in NYC but of which midwesterners seem to be totally ignorant. This leads to clannishness where the Midwestern folks protect their own and get into unprofessional favoritism.
Finally there is a total lack of visibility into upper rungs of management, even via quarterly conference calls or group notices. This makes it very difficult to know the general direction the group is moving towards.

summary: Lots of options, some of them good.
advice: Be prepared to pay for quality staff in the technology sector as you would in the business side.  The results of the offshoring are showing through in the tech space first, but pain is also apparent in the operations side.  Having regional teams is fine, but having a team beholden to another organization on the other side of the planet is a drag on the efficiency and capabilities of both.
pros: A fairly stable company with good training and benefits opportunities here - internal moves cover a wide array of options.
cons: Lags behind competitors in salary and bonuses for the industry, general management attitude seems to be stating that something is world class will provide adequate energy to make it so, without investing in the staff or infrastructure to the extent that this is an accurate statement.  Lots of offshoring going on.  One of the more politically fierce places to work on the street.  These vary by business sector, but is an overall theme.

advice: Be more open in communication and show some respect to the consultants. They are there to work and so dont treat them like vermin
pros:
Its great work life balance. They actually will be ok with people working upto 2 days a week from home. Many people take liberties with more than that and tend to work all week from home.

They are also pretty relaxed and make sure that no one person is over burdened with work. Work allocation is pretty fair.
cons:
Managers are partial to Employees and treat consultants badly. Unfair to consultants even though they do the same job if not more. Managers will openly in meeting remind employees that they are more important and will make consultants feel like outsiders

With the amount of work that is outsourced, and given to consultants one would think that the managers will be more appreciative, sply when the employees are slacking away when they should be working and the consultants are working they b*tt off....just to make sure they are not laid off.

advice:
Provide proper training to employees, be transparent about what the firm is doing.

I remember receiving an email about the firm with higher revenues, while masking the costs side of the equation.  Revenue growth doesn't mean anything if costs have increased as well.  Or if employees are dissatisfied.  Prime Brokerage is a shrinking business, don't tell us about how much better it's been doing.  With the turnover rate that high (I don't have official statistics, but I've seen 3-4 people leave in the span of 6 months), it can't be a sustainable business.  That's pretty much it, there's nothing else to say, good or bad about this position.  Perhaps it's different in ibanking, or sales and trading, as those are actual front office positions.
pros:
Honestly, not too many pros
The cafeteria was nice, and there were other people my age as well, which made social interaction less awkward
cons:
Long hours for a middle/back office job (8:30-6:30)
No upward mobility
High Turnover rate, even among the full time employees

summary: Stable company (for now) but very old school
advice: Go back to admins supporting execs directly and reporting to them as managers. Remove these inept and inexperienced admin managers who have a high need for control and are running the good EAs off.
pros: Very big company that is stable (for now)
cons: Benefits are not the best, they are very stuck in old world type bureaucracy and their technology is stuck in the 90s (which makes it hard to do your job efficiently); they frown on flexible work schedules, and the worst part is they have an admin management group who purportedly are supposed to be "advocates" but I have found the reverse - they are high control, poor managers and I have even had to get the executive I support to advocate for me in the relationship with my admin manager. Turnover in my group of admins since the inception of the admin mgmt system here about a year ago has been roughly 90%.

summary: Good people.  Pay ok.  Challenges available.  Frugal company.
advice: Sometimes, it is worthwhile to satisfy performing employees than to risk their departure and backfilling their positions.
pros: Random things to mention - The investment banking area offers plenty of opportunities to learn and grow.  Most of the people there were great.  They understand the importance of your support for them.  There are also plenty of perks such discounts to parks and free admission to cultural events.  The intranet is filled with information for the employee.  eTraining is also available.  The company also invests heavily in technology for smoother operations.  They promote work/life balance.  There are also town hall meetings where you can express your concerns with Senior Management and the CEO.
cons: Recognition is usually not followed with pay/promotion.  The company is extremely cost conscious.  Training/conference does not seem to be encouraged when cost is a factor.  They do not even have milk in the pantry.  Office supplies is in short supplies.

summary: 14 years at firm and opinion continues downward fall
pros: The Benefits are decent for employees
cons: Mortgage Banking - There isn't a life/work balance. Consistent 70+ hours per week. Salary is very low. Raises are minimal (2% if any) and bonus is extremely poor even with a meets+ performance rating. Exceeds performance rating is impossible because they will change your manager every few months so you can't prove your skills to anyone. New managers automatically give meets performance ratings so you have no chance to increase your performance rating. Work environment is very bad, culture is very bad-Sr Managers talk very badly about employees behind closed doors. Constant lawsuits and regulatory settlements (in the billions) give the firm an excuse for not staffing appropriately, causing extreme work hours and an excuse for not giving compensation increases to employees while the firm  announces billion dollar earnings for the quarter.  They have an "employee experience" campaign due to an extremely poor employee survey that gives employees ice cream, cookies, paper trophies, so if that's what you're after - you can get it once a year.  If you wan ya company that really cares about their employees, I suggest that you look somewhere else.

summary: Early responsibility and opportunity get ahead quickly but inefficient and toxic culture
pros:
- Unprecedented level of early responsibility: had my own book after 3 months and was co-managing a large one after just 6
- ability to travel to other global offices on trips where everything is paid for. For me that was Sao Paolo and London
- generally very intelligent & competent people
- highly competitive environment
- great pay and benefits
cons:
- all of the inefficiencies of a large company with the added restriction of heavy regulation. - the software is outdated and clunky
- all of my ideas for operational improvements were very quickly dismissed on the basis that a) there was no time to do it, or b) it simply wasn't necessary
- there are a few people at the bank who have your best interest and will go to bat for you. Everyone else will step on you if it lets them get ahead. Can be almost a toxic environment at times

advice: Ease up on the bureaucracy and the process of speaking with higher-ups. There's no point in encouraging networking with coworkers if we can't even go straight to someone a few levels above us. It stifles a lot of good ideas and discourages people from speaking up.
pros: Caliber/intelligence of coworkers, compensation (salary and bonuses), prestige of firm, challenging and impactful work. The company is very socially responsible (especially compared to other megabanks) and it's awesome to be a part of a company that follows through with so many great values. Jamie Dimon is also an incredible CEO.
cons: The hours are long and the work is very demanding. Very cut-throat with high standards for all work, even in the non-NYC locations. But that's the industry, and JPMC is the biggest (arguably the best) in the industry.

summary: kafka-esque beaurocracy and not dev friendly
advice: Extended the Firm’s commitment to fairness and integrity to contractors. Let them use the game rooms and pay them for the actual hours they work which is typically well over 40.
pros:
Salary and benefits
Diverse and high quality colleagues 
Easy to take vacation 
Strong job stability
Atmosphere of courtesy
Making some effort to give back and be socially aware
cons:
Firm doesnt treat contractors with integrity. I’m fulltime but the double standard really makes me lose respect for the firm. It bills them for forty hours but they always work more. It bars them from using the game rooms and  going to company events even though most of them have been with the company for years, and vast majority work tirelessly. 
50% or more effort goes to institutional beaurocracy/redtape 
Devs arent given access to ANYTHING, barely have permission to work on the command line of your own computer
Management/business very out of touch with difficulties and timelines of dev work

advice: Changing the commission structure and keeping a very low salary makes it very difficult for one to want to stay.  Families cannot live on bad commission months.  I know the saying is when you do it right then you will never have a bad commission month, but that is just not true.  I worked very hard and did very well most months, but when I did bad  a month or two I could barely get by.
pros: Top of the line industry when it comes to technology, lead generation, and training. Plenty of time to study for the tests. Paid training while gearing up for SIE, Series 6, Series 63, and Life.
cons: I feel the salary is low and they do give you a ramp up period to make some incentive, but it takes a good amount of time to develop relationships for people to invest. The time is a short period for the ramp up period.

summary: Line of Business will determine your happiness.
advice: Drop the military mentality where it exists.  People are not plug and play and need more than "that's your job, soldier".
pros: They're stable at the moment.  Within the banking industry, they are still holding steady while others are crashing and burning.  Of course, a lot of the stability is dependent upon which LOB (Line of Business) you work in.  The LOB I work in provides technology support to all other LOBs; however, we're in a horrible state when it comes to stability and compensation.
cons: At least in our LOB and group, poor recognition of work done, horrible pay packages, no incentive for professional growth.  The manager above my supervisor when asked about incentive and rankings and such said "Well, I don't know about you but just having a job right now is compensation enough."  Although it may be true, it's not something that will help morale and performance.

summary: Great place to learn with a fast paced mature cutting edge team
advice: Improve your on boarding and work facilities to compete with other IT companies in the area. Create an innovation team to keep good employees engaged when projects get cancelled.
pros:
My experience is specifically with the Mobile banking team:
- Learn with the best industry standard IT management tools in a process optimized environment
- Learn to work with dispersed teams using state of the art communication tools
- Be surrounded by brilliant project focused people who work at a relentless pace
- Learn form a delivery focused metrics driven schedule with tight releases
- Treated as professional with reasonable work from home allowances and flexible schedules
cons:
- Expect weekend work, and high pressure work environment
- Minimal on boarding where most people are too busy to train new employees
- Large offshore component and communications can make collaboration challenging
- Little interaction between teams, very segmented and narrow roles
- Little team building, cramped office in fringe SOMA location

advice: If you want more office space in midtown, tell all the ED to stop having multiple offices at midtown and at Whippany. Allow staff to work from home and use the application, See Me more effectively. We will then save some money in real estate to pay for all the fines!
pros: Not a lot to offer. Good backup child care facility.
cons: Recently jp Morgan have to move employees out of 1 Chase Manhattan Plaza. There are no more space at 383 Madison Ave, so they move employees out to 4 NY Plaza, Brooklyn and Whippany , NJ. In some cases, employees have no choice and they move them to Whippany NJ and the managers expect their employees to suddenly buy a car and drive out to NJ with no pay compensation. Some JP Morgan managers are control freak. They have to see their employees everyday even though we are all on conference call because most of the developers are offshore anyway.

advice: Stop the incentive programs and increase the wages. You will get better public relationships and give staff the opportunities to built the relationship with current customers. There are more that cheat the incentive system hunting the new and ignoring what you  already have just to make enough in their paychecks to pay their own bills.
pros: Insurance coverage is good and due to high number of employees, not as costly as any other employer. 3 weeks of vacation right out of the box is sweet as well.
cons: Competing to get your three weeks (or even one week) when you want the time off is almost impossible. Pay in the call centers is not much more than poverty level. As to their being in the news for paying incredibly high fines, well, they do not want to hear from an employee about any wrongdoing they will wait (and make money from) their wrongdoings until the Fed catches them at it.

advice: If you want millennials to stay, the work culture needs to change. Millenials want work life balance, meaningful work and to be treated as equals.
pros:
- Good name, having JP Morgan on your resume is a name everyone  recognizes
 - Decent work life balance
 - People are nice and do try to help, environment is not cut throat
 - You come in with an analyst class and people your age which is nice to have friends when you start
cons:
- Work culture can be apathetic or centered around blame
 - It can be demanding at times, you may be expected to work late or work through weekends
 - Work can require lots of approvals and will take time to get projects done. Things move 3x slower here
 - Extremely hierarchical. As a junior employee, you might get stuck with all the grunt work. 
 - Senior execs sometimes don't do ANYTHING - they just delegate yet they micromanage.

summary: Not Great. Good only for college students.
advice: My direct managers were great, but my marketing director is awful. She doesn't care about you or your goals unless they benefit her in some way. She was the reason I quit. You only get promoted so long as you play the game. Don't ever say your real opinion about anything. Keep your head down, do your job and management will work with you so long as you don't rock the boat.
pros: Good benefits, culture is okay and most management is professional. If you want to move into a new position you have to be aggressive about it, but they do have some movement in the company.
cons: Pay is awful, especially when compared to other banks. No bonuses anymore unless you get gold on your OSAT score (which is really hard depending on what kind of branch you're at). More job responsibilities and no increase in pay. Decent entry level position, but keep your expectations low.

summary: Very political company; you have to seek out your own success
advice: Listen to your management team and invest where there will be good payback.  Not everything is about cutting costs.  There will be positive outcomes for taking the long view and not solely worrying about quarterly results.
pros: As a huge company, there is opportunity for moving around if you search it out yourself.  The benefits, while not as good as in earlier years, are still fairly good: four weeks of vacation if you're an officer plus two personal days plus standard bank holidays.  The health insurance is expensive, but good.
cons: The culture is very much about cost cutting, to the detriment of investing intelligently in the business to foster growth.  Some of the senior managers are very political and while excellent at managing up, they are poor managers to those who report to them.  It's amazing how some of these managers continue to survive in their positions.

advice: Senior management appears to be navigating well during these these turbulent times. Continue to maintain a "fortress" balance sheet and keep up the good work!
pros: JPMC is a world-class organization and the corporate brand is highly respected.  Management "sets the bar high" and the executive leadership team is both competent and courageous.  The firm hires high caliber employees, and it's energizing to work with the best and brightest.  There are great career opportunities, and the rewards and recognition are excellent.
cons: It's can be challenging to work in such an enormous, hierarchical organization, and corporate politics can be tough to deal with. Sometimes the hours can seem endless, ie there are many required late nights and weekends.  There's constant pressure to improve performance and reduce expenses, resulting in lots of downsizing.  The fast pace and high degree of change create a level of intensity that can be exhausting and stressful for some people.

jobTitle: Vice President/Lead In One of the Many IT Groups
summary: JPMC puts the dys in dysfunction
advice: Become more involved in the day to day operations and truly understand what is going on at the lower levels.  There are millions of dollars being wasted, and no one at the top seems to know or care
pros: Very few pros, other than some of the very nice people I get to work with
cons:
Where do I begin?  
* Too many levels of management
* Too much kingdom building
* The people at the top are too interested in their bonuses to care about the daily work
* Analysis Paralysis is common
* Rushing to get things done even when they're being done wrong
* Never enough time to do things right the first time, but always time to do them again
* Repeating the mistakes of the past instead of improving upon the situation
* Duplication of duties
* No clear vision of Total cost of ownership, more emphasis on immediate cost savings (Total cost of Acquisition), which translates into bloated systems environments

summary: Last one turn out the lights
advice: Treat your employees with respect. A certain Sr VP i can think of needs to show people respect and not be so stuck up. Dont treat people like there stupid, and they'll pull more weight than you ask them to do. Dont lie to employees, JPM isnt treating this as a 'merger' were all hosed...
pros: If you want to show up at 10 and leave at 3, this is a great place for you.
cons: Everyone's lack of knowledge on anything but their own "specialization" Try to find someone that can actually solve your issue from start to finish is impossible. Everything is a fire drill, it's like the blind leading the blind. The person leading teh project always seems to be the one with the least experience. All teh smart people have virtually left, the rest are waiting to see what their package will consist of now that JPM is cleaning house.

summary: Reputable Company, but Few Opportunities for Advancement
advice: Improve ability to retain talent and show employee appreciation. Good talent is leaving left and right for much better paying jobs going on to perform the same role they had here.
pros:
It is a reputable company that is good for professional experience. I have worked hard here and have gained a lot of valuable experience that has better equipped me as a professional. 

Work/Life balance is good. Expectations to work extra hours vary

401k and Employee stock purchase program

Diverse and many great coworkers
cons:
Currently it is difficult to move up. Daily/weekly expectations for your role tend to consume all your working hours and is hard to pick up extra projects/tasks that could help you move forward without falling behind on the things you are primarily evaluated for.

No efforts to retain talent. Positions are vacated and not backfilled which results more work, raised expectations, and less flexibility.

Compensation/raises/bonuses not competitive

Work from home flexibility slowly being stripped away

summary: Standard Banking Job in A Standard Industry
advice: I don't know if they would even listen. With a hemorrhage of employees happening, I hope they understand and actually listen to their concerns.
pros: Like most jobs, the people that work her are earnest in their approach and they truly think they are making a difference in their clients life. The company has also made a concerted effort to include diversity in their customer facing positions.
cons: Management is terrible. From upper to lower, they do not care about you or your contribution. Some people have been working for years with no cost of living raise. Also, their approach during the pandemic was business as usual. Sales are what mattered, even if people were literally dying. They preferred to put their front line employees in danger to make a dollar. Also, nepotism is hot here. If you don't know the right people, do not expect to move ahead. Meritocracy is dead, even if they say different.

advice: The entire company culture needs to change.
pros: The pay.  Also if you are a technically adept person who likes a hectic work environment.
cons: I was warned that it was a sweat shop, and that is indeed true.  This is a very large company, so ymmv depending on what area you are in, but IT is not a pleasant place to be.  Culturally it was diseased to the core:  there was a no understanding of process, no understanding of roles, and basically they were just trying to do way too much too quickly and so it was a constant of environment of chickens running around with their heads cut off.  They really do not care about their employees. And that's their right, of course, but if you go there you might as well do so as a mercenary because that's all you are to them.  I didn't know anyone who was happy there, and yet there was an odd type of timidity (and maybe loyalty in some cases) which stopped most people from leaving.  I hated working there.

summary: Good Job but not a Meaty one!
advice: Please be more technology focussed and open towards open source technologies. There are challenging problems to be solved but there are few people with the vision. Please stop asking tech folks to wear fancy banker costumes to work!
pros:
* Was hired as a Recent Grad Applications Developer. The company as such is good, the pay package and benefits for the location was good. 
* Nice and friendly co-workers
* Management was understanding most of the times
cons:
* I personally didn't find the job meaty enough, that too for a recent grad who is hungry to go challenging work
* Too much bureaucracy and slow moving 
* Technology is not the Product, its just considered as IT. So working on the Tech side which is not considered as the product means low exposure to the company
* People are really nice but the problem is passion might be missing at times

summary: Daily Challenges Everyone Runs into....JPM AND 3rd Party Outsourcing
advice: Do BAU for one day.  Understand the challenges your people are going through.  Get down and dirty and just maybe you'll understand what your people are trying to tell you.  Stop micro managing.
pros: Decent pay. Relaxed environment. They just added more parking spaces so you no longer have to take the bus.  Free coffee.
cons: Senior management encourages transparency in communication but has a very hard time following through themselves.  Many jobs have been outsourced to third world countries and you have to learn to adapt to work with different people at different hours.  Communications is always challenging and therefore it seems like every team is always doing their own thing.  It's never a "we" but always Mumbai, Bournemouth, Manila, or Buenos Aires team.  Technology is very poor. Can take up to 6 months to gain the access you need to do your daily job

summary: Former Transaction Supervisor (the last to ever do it, they cant find anyone to take the position and rightfully so!)
advice: Dont lie to incoming candidates about this position. Its grueling. You think you are the warden in a prison that is creating model inmates but fail to see we all are prisoners in the same yard.
pros: Of course the people there (except managment) were great! It was close to home for me and this site typically hires people who live close.
cons: DO NOT BELEIVE WHAT THEY TELL YOU ABOUT THIS POSITION! I was the last supervisor they hired and this position has been open for over 2 years. They are looking for the right sucker to hire and then overwhelm you with administrative work with antique programs while telling you to watch the floor and baby sit 70 + 18 year olds and all your Team Leaders will be off because they are schizophrenic and take a sick leave. This by far was the worst job I have ever had. This is not a career folks, just a job. If you like 16 hour days then it's the job for you.

advice: Change the bonus approach.  Needs to be defined, not subjective.
pros: Good brand name.  Some people are smart and humble and great to work with.
cons: Bonuses are discretionary and determined by managers.  The clients are “covered” by bankers and given to bankers subjectively.  Many managers do not understand what a merit-based environment would mean.  Those in market manager or regional manager positions control a lot, such as who gets what clients, who gets referrals, who goes on what calls.  It is kind of bizarre how much control they have over large staffs.  Many managers have little professional or life experience outside of the silos at JP Morgan private bank and so the culture tends to persist.  Many of those considered top performers do not source their own business, and instead they “work on” big clients or deals that were handed to them.  Face-time is very important at JPM.

advice: Treat your clients the way you want to be treated. If you are going to the ATM for a quick deposit, do you really want to be sales pitched by a banker? This is why many people are moving to online banks. Excellent service and free accounts.
pros: Only pro is if you like low pay, new employees getting paid higher than you with less experience or even licensing. You like to be micromanaged and like working for a company that doesn’t support you when coworkers are sexually harassing you or bullying you. The only pro is that the branch manager got fired but was after I left.
cons: Low pay, low commissions, unreasonable expectations. All the training is about ethics and integrity but when you get into the branch they want you to open bank accounts and credit cards without the clients consent. It’s all about the numbers and nothing about customer service and building trust and relationships.

summary: Only work here if you are about to become homeless, find any other job and don't believe any of their empty promises
advice: Keep in mind that people are what makes a bank great, treating your employees with disrespect will get immediate results, but in the long run no one will want to do business with you. I would suggest trying to filter some of the messages a little better. Just because your supervisor just spent two hours ripping you a new one, does not mean you are going to achieve your goals by doing the same to your employees.
pros: Name recognition, this used to be a great bank before Bank One bought them. Cutting edge technology and great commercials make it easy to speak with prospects.
cons: You are only a number, the bank is only concerned with profits and the quickest way to show double digit growth (which as a stock owner is nice). Use this position as a stepping stone, unless you become friends with someone high up, you will not be able to advance. Be very careful about disagreeing with anyone, they hold a personal grudge forever.

summary: You get paid to cleanup people's crap, that is what I have been told by my direct manager and the one above.
advice:
- Don't bring up the subject of being paid a high salary to cleanup people's crap
- Don't be jealous of your subordinates just because they get paid more than you. You get the good position they get the good pay
- Demotivating your subordinates will not give you a raise
- Don't interrogate your subordinates to know how much retention bonus they are getting
- If you don't like your pay find another company that thinks that your skills worth anything
pros: If you're coming from a good IT company, you can easily negotiate a good salary because low IT quality people usually apply to work for that company.
cons:
- Managers tend to be intimidating if you speak up about your concerns
- Most managers have no managerial skills
- I have been assigned several times to projects that are completely outside my area of expertise 
- They do internal reviews to simply let managers use it against you
- Old technologies
- Very hostile environment
- Very strict unpleasant environment
- A very hierarchical organization

summary: Let's s Start Telling the Truth Here  . . . .
advice: Grow up and start treating people the way that you would like to be treated.  Adequately staff, and stop lying, cheating and promoting a culture of dishonesty and concealment.
pros: Benefit package is comparable to others in financial services.
cons:
Everything else - you have no value as an employee; everyone is expendible; you give up your life when you walk through the door. If you have a family, kiss them goodbye now because you will never see them again.   18 hour days are the norm.

Everyone is constantly afraid and terrified of making any little mistake.  You are expected to lie, and to tell the lies that senior management dictates.  If you don't, you're gone or banished. Senior management is clueless, manages by crisis to crisis, and is completely occupied with its own self-preservation.  

And, just try to find a clean and working restroom when you need one.  They'll tell you to go use the bathrooms in the hotel next door if you don't like it.

advice: Meritocracy - make it happen. Diversity is a joke and inclusion is required.  Very much an old boys network. Firm needs to stop being complacent with being the leading back and put focus on innovation to be a true leader in the industry.
pros: Supported going back to school and provided ample growth opportunities.  Promoted twice, travel internationally is possible.   IT is a utility here not a revenue generator so be ready for businesses to treat you like staff and not experts.
cons: Decision making is geographically centered on New York where the employees are not the leaders they just happen to have seniority and are physically located to the executives.  New York centric mentality as well as the American mentality that we push decisions down to all other country leaders.  Not a truly global mindset here.  Approaching 250,000 employees.

summary: Good company, some poor HR policies though
advice: Weed out the poor managers (faster) and make the hard decision to cut some of the VPs loose.  There are numerous entry/mid level managers who lack technical expertise and have poor social skills, they are causing the churn of your solid employees.
pros: Good strong company, good technology, good support, average to slightly better than normal paid time off policies, great reputation when looking for next role
cons: The rapid growth of the AML operation led to some exceptionally poor middle management decisions; and in turn those managers/VPs can make life miserable for lower level employees. Likewise, the promotion process is exceptionally rigid.  They had a tremendous amount of turnover, so hopefully upper management has noticed the issues with mid management.  Finally, the ranking system is archaic.  They rate everyone out in a bell curve shaped fashion, but largely political and the ranking influences year end bonus.

advice: Treat your employees better, promote from within and reward hard working rising stars!
pros:
-Negotiated a good salary during interview
-Good coworkers, but there was some disgruntlement from tenured employees who felt "stuck" and overworked
-Great benefits, ie 401k, health, dental, profit sharing, etc
-If you had worked there for a while, it could be pretty stable depending on your position and responsibilities
cons:
-No training or on-boarding program!!!
-Apparently my department went through LEAN a couple years ago, and they passed over internal promotions to hire externally
-Disgruntled and overworked employees
-Apathetic upper management
-Some internal strifes between certain teams and everyone looking out for themselves
-Came down harshly on "rookie" mistakes
-Constant layoffs and restructuring, at least with Custody Middle office Operations in Dallas, TX - the whole department was soon shuttered and relocated back to NY soon after I separated from the firm
-Disorganization in roles, titles and what team is actually supposed to handle certain tasks

summary: JPMorgan Chase: Once your in, your nuts if you leave...
advice: Offshore resources are not the answer management makes them out to be. Keeping knowledge experts inside the firm will produce a much better end product.
pros: The work/life balance at JPMorgan Chase is excellent. They are very flexible when it comes to work needs, life events, and other situations. For instance, I have been working from home for the last 18 months, and have found my productivity to be better than ever. This works for my situation because I can perform all my work tasks via telecommuting. This arrangement does not work for everyone, but JPMorgan Chase recognizes that everyone has a unique set of circumstances, and tries it’s best to do what’s best for everyone. They also have the best benefit packages I have seen. (vacation, health, retirement, etc...)
cons: It's a very large company, so there are many bureaucratic things you need to be able to deal with.

summary: Incredibly great CEO, seriously lacking in Mortgage sector. I undertsand the enviroment we are in however!
advice: In Regards the Lending: Regional VP's, their boss's and the additional Managing layers should be required to fill the shoes of the people doing the ground-work that are not paid very well, and it's reflected and  shows in their accountability.  It appears, they are just recruiting Manager's and lack experience. Leading with fear is not motivational, at least not in any business books I have read. That said they are Global company, and do a lot of things very well!!!
pros: Can do attitude, expanding in a difficult time and a real attempt to help the economy. The Best CEO, of a large banking institution.
cons: Clearly consistant mistakes, lack oversight and  good judgement from top to bottom in providing good quality products to clients. It's sad to see good harding working people get lost in the black hole.

advice: Quit your day job, lack of job skills on your part makes very unhappy employees
pros: It's a job is the only pro. It is by far one of the worse companies I have worked for. The supervisors and management are either too laid back and indifferent or strict and over your shoulder all the time. They micromanage everything with their time and processed items programs they have. It measures productivity which in hindsight is a bad idea for the people with several job functions throughout their shift. You will get laid off if you dont meet their standards of productivity no matter how hard you work and how much you lend yourself to other departments
cons:
High turn over
lack of management or managerial training
Non department specific training classes
Pick and choose what skills you learn for your department, you won't know everything if you needed to fill in for a member of your team

pros: I was lucky to get young, understanding Branch manager who tried to work around your school/personal schedule. There's always some company event going on that they invite you too (like funraisers, holidays etc.) so you can feel more like a family. Branch manager are good at making employees feel like a member, you get cakes for you birthday,  sometimes they invite us out for dinner (free on us they pay) if we funraiser extra money.
cons: Sometimes they baby you too much, they do more scolding and telling you what you do wrong than pat you on the back for keeping at the good work. They focus more on the negatives that you do. It can be a flip-flop situation, some good days, some bad. It can sometimes be stressfull and overwhelming because sometimes your mostly under staff because chase has staff turnover (employess fired, leave & constantly are hiring)

pros: Good medical benefits and Poor Training
cons:
Management from Executive Director through the individual he appointed as my manager was absolutely clueless
Management shows favoritism to the Indian culture and black people which I declare as discrimination considering I was the only white person on the team.  I can't say this is true across the company, but it did exist in the Line of Business I worked in.
Work - Life balance is stressed in the company, however the job was 24/7; I worked 60 hours a week at a minimum.  Management tried to cover their tracks by making sure you only logged 40 hours on your clarity time card which was clear deception.
Opportunities are not provided on a level playing field as the Indians and Blacks are given  preference.
Yearly reviews were not evaluated fairly in the Line of Business I worked.  It was stated that there was a 70%/20%/10% rating scale that dictated raises.  After talking with Employee relations this rating system has not been used in the company for over 2 years.  The management team was 100% corrupt.

summary: A good place for new employment opportunity
advice: Instead of putting so much emphasis on bringing in new talent perhaps you should work harder at valuing the talent that has been loyal to you for many years.  And the recognition is nice after 15-20 years of service it would be much nicer to see good salary increases rather than a little paper weight to sit on your desk.
pros: JPMorgan Chase is a very good company to work for.  They have a very good benefits program and for the most part they work hard to keep a good work-life balance.
cons: Unfortunately like any large company, they pay market value for new employees but for their loyal existing employees you are lucky if you are even keeping up with inflation.  it's very distressing to find the people just coming into the company with less experience and education than you are making more money than you.  And also like any other large company sometimes it's not what you know and the value you provide as much as who you know and how much you're willing to kiss up to them.

summary: Do not expect to advance or retire here
advice:
Be more thoughtful and understanding of the job we're being asked to do. Help people excel into different positions instead of being completely self serving.
If you work here and run out of sick time they will fire you. When people retire there is no goodbyes or a party, they just leave. This is essentially a large adult daycare. Every call is monitored and recorded. If your manager knows you want to advance they will do everything in their power to make sure that's not possible. It's a large company with NO advancement opportunities. Once they get you on the phone taking their back to back calls trying to keep up with your metrics... You're on a continual loop to nowwhereville and you won't get interviews for new positions. I've *never* had a good manager here. You will hate your life and get very fat here. Most people gain 50 pounds and some are morbidly obese. You can't go to the bathroom or get a drink. It's awful.
pros: Pay, benefits and that's it. But you can actually get the same benes at any company.
cons: Call volume, micro management, company culture, no advancement opportunities

summary: A place I wish to never work at again
advice: If someone is qualified and has outlived the position they're in, its not right to try to block them from advancement because of your own insecurities, Writing people up for mundane things just because they have expressed an interest in advancement is highly unprofessional and ridiculous
pros: Once you leave phones based position you will be exposed to a lot of interesting people in different departments located all over the world. You will acquire a lot of valuable experience and get to use new systems, software's and things like that . This company overall isn't bad but the corporate culture needs to chase especially at the call center locations
cons: The Chase Card politics are just ridiculous, once management determines that they dont you to advance in your career, the only choice you have from there is if they leave or you do. There's a lot of un-professionalism and jealousy from managers that will keep you moving up and advancing your career. Theres a lot of clicks and if you don't fit in with the cliques because you disapprove of their ways then your career there is doomed

advice: Be more communicative with your employee. Hold more one-on-one conversations and meetings to regularly check in, aside from & in addition to the usual Mid Year and Year End discussions.
pros: Extremely employee-focused with efforts on career growth & development. If you want to succeed and grow, there is no one stopping you. Tools, "Universities", and courses/trainings at employees' fingertips that we are all highly encouraged to use. Have personally seen plenty of people "start at the bottom" and rise to their full potential. The sky is the limit in this firm. Work/Life balance is stressed regularly and the firm offers many opportunities and actually encourages employees for an enriched home life and to utilize time off/lessening "overtime".
cons: The restrictions of the Corporate World hold true here. Things are very "by-the-book", and while I think this is a good (and necessary) thing, many people aren't cut out for the strict nature of the industry or the way this company works.

summary: Company has lost its soul and employees are leaving
advice: Get out of your ivory tower on Park Avenue and actually see what your mid-level leaders are doing.  They lie about what the true issues are.  Moral is horrible, but people are afraid to say it on the reviews because it is very clear there is retribution if you don't say things are good.  The company is dying from the inside out.
pros: Good Benefits.  Good location.  Pay is average.  The company name looks good on your resume, but there isn't much else going for it.
cons:
Mid-level management (MD's) are ruining the place.  New review/management system is a farce, because it isn't documented and not place for employees to provide commentary; in other words, the bad managers can hide how bad they are.

No strategy.  Run like a boiler room.  Bad mangers keep the bonuses.  The new office setup (high perf workspace) is a joke. Taking people and putting them at bench seating is despicable.  Treating all employees like they are offshore coders is short-sighted.  Why that is the new corporate standard, other than to squeeze more cost, makes no sense.

summary: really enjoyable experience for finance careers
advice: obviously Junior persons are here to learn and grow, but senior-level analyst a & Associates are still willing to learn and grow as well. Don't write them off. If you cannot attend to a junior person needs that is being able to teach them and help them grow in their professional style, don't take in a junior person on your team.
pros: I have had nothing but a good time being in this company. The individuals and managers that you meet are also helpful and willing to be flexible and teach.however this comes at a price of you being willing to work hard and put in the hours that are needed to get work done.
cons: this is not a place you want to be in it you are not particularly interested in the finance industry. First and foremost it is a bank and everything that you do will be Bank related, if you can grass that or don't want to be in that environment you do not need to be here. In certain parts of the bank atmospheres are in wOrk cultures are more intense than others, and there's no way around.

summary: Ups and Downs, Like any corporation
advice: Simplify management structure and hold management accountable for their relationships with employees.  Focus on providing opportunities to talent within the organization and optimizing their skills.  Annual review process needs massive update.  90% of the organization ends up in "meets" or "on track" and there are no opportunities for advancement or raises unless you happen to achieve the highest performance once a year.   Quarterly reviews would be nice, along with a more customizable review process.
pros: Structure, benefits, Pay on average.
cons: Management is disconnected from the average employee.  Too many levels of management dilutes the communication from top to bottom.  Employees have to basically riot for the smallest concessions.  Recruiting system is abysmal.  Poor forecasting results in massive layoffs and poor transparency about the future.  After two layoffs of almost the entire department, I realized that moving up in the organization would be impossible and it's time to look elsewhere for employment.

summary: This is where careers go to die
advice: Right your own ship and stop giving condescending and contradictory "advice" to your employees about mobility.   It doesn't exist.  Own up to that and have a frank and honest discussion about how to move forward.
pros: It is a big name on your resume, assuming you do two years maximum and leave
cons:
Absolutely no mobility whatsoever.   Top 1% performance and a glowing review will net you a salary increase which barely keeps pace with inflation.   Promotions do not happen within your line of business, however you are not eligible for cross platform increases either.   The firms stated solution to this is that you should basically hop from department to department, remaining at each for 2-3 years and maybe after three or four cycles of this your direct supervisor will get hit by a bus and you will be one of 20 people considered for promotion.  Even if this occurs, the firm has a history of increasing your title, giving you more direct reports and then later cutting the position before you ever see a pay or title increase.   

TL:DR,
As a clear top 1% performer, I can confidently say that death or retirement of a direct supervisor is your only chance at advancement.   Avoid this trash heap like the plague.

summary: Great company to work for- very corporate environment
advice: Fix your public image.
pros: I have worked with people that have turned a part-time job in a bank into a career. Maybe it's just my manager, but the bank has a very strong code of ethics enforcement. Great Benefits, good pay for college students with school flexibility, and the company is all over the US. The uniforms are not bad, the company gives it's employees allowances to purchase any style uniforms they like. Their operating systems are a lot better. I prefer it a lot more than Wells'.
cons: The company changes the incentive packages every year. It sounds like they try everything to keep them from paying your incentive, but this is probably just to make sure that the banker made a quality sale. Gaming is a rampant in the banking industry. Sometimes, wearing the uniform everyday gets boring and robotic. The company has a very corporate feel to it- definitely feels different than WaMu. WaMu was more people-friendly.

summary: Lowest base salary in the field
advice: Focus on your employees
pros: Great benefits, it used to have a decent incentive plan.
cons: Too many changes. They expect private client bankers to pick up the slack when they layoff other positions. They are so demanding with productivity and calls. Expect you to do your job and cover for other roles and manager when they’re not there. They also made most bankers managers on duty to cover when manager is absent. Without any pay or bonus for the much added responsibility which will distract you from doing your actual job that makes you money to compensate for the embarrassing low base, even when you make good commission you are heavily taxed on it which at the end of the day you are better off have a high guaranteed salary. Because they change the incentive plan on you with just 1 week notice. Also no flexibility to work from home or have access to at least an email. Chase have changes a lot it’s all about the big bosses pockets and not their employees that are the ones that doing all the hard core job and hustling to bring new clients and new money.

summary: Run. Run as far away from Chase as possible...
advice: My advice to management is NSFW.
pros:
My last day working at Chase was the best day I had in 2 years while working for this miserable company. This place is so evil, that birds actually fly around the building backwards. The day I left, food starting tasting better again, I noticed the birds singing again (and flying properly), the sun shined brighter, the air was fresher, and there was an actual beacon of hope in my career path because I was moving on from this toxic environment. A toxic environment that included nepotism, sexual harassment, and gender double standards - all ignored by incompetent management. 

Chase could offer me a blank check as a salary and conjugal visits at lunch everyday and I still would never go back to that wretched, bottom layer of hell.
cons:
I wasted two years of my professional career in this poor excuse for a company. Underpaid, underappreciated, and overworked. It is no surprise Chase always finishes last amongst the Big 4 Banks when it comes to the JD Power rankings. 

I would not recommend my worst enemy for a job at Chase.

summary: Good company to work for, excellent pay
advice: I have a health condition that causes me to drop off for a moment or two, especially when I am stressed. I am under treatment for this condition, but I still have occasional issues.  I advised my managers of this when I was hired.  I was terminated because of this issue.  The manager reported my work was great and even volunteered to give me a positive reference.  Please don't release people from employment for a health issue that they are attempting to control.
pros: As a contractor, I found it was a great place to work.  They had great pay and they definitely made sure you got a full 40 hour week (they didn't do OT much).  The people I worked with were friendly and were happy to explain anything you needed to know.
cons: There seemed to be a lot of issues with account setup and permissions for new hires.  It took almost 6 weeks before I could log into any of the software needed to do my job.  Even afterward, there were still issues with passwords ongoing.

pros: Great company brand; looks good on your resume and easier to get job interviews when it is time to move on. People here are in general very nice and cooperative. Work/life balance is achievable depending on the team. I have seen people living a 9/5 life in JPMorgan.
cons: Very political environment especially in back office; unfair performance rating; lack of transparency; terrible compensation. Constantly changing organizational structure and leadership. (I have had 4 direct managers in past two years.) It depends on the team but some managers are just mean people and all they ever care about is to take the credit and promote themselves in front of senior management. I have seen people moving around internally but it is VERY DIFFICULT to get a promotion or a raise through internal transfer. HR is not as helpful as they should be. 1) First of all they are hard to be approached, you just cannot find the right people to talk to. The internal hotline "accessHR" is a joke because you will never get through; 2) I have seen people report their manager to HR but they did NOT do ANYTHING to protect the employees.

pros: Work with bright, hard working people
cons: Senior management is taking away regularly scheduled WFH days unless you can prove a hardship or special circumstances. Corporate hubs are moving to "choice seating" which essentially means you no longer have an assigned desk. Each morning you are required to come in and find a seat by logging into a system. You have an extremely small locker where you must go to pick up any personal items you'd like to bring to your desk for the day.  At the end of the day, you log out and put your belongings back in your little locker. Teams are no longer guaranteed to sit together. You may not even be guaranteed a seat when you come in, in which case you have to work with an Admin to help you find a seat somewhere. By the time you actually sit down, it can be a half hour later.  There is a general feeling of frustration and discontent in the office with these changes. There are extremely intelligent and seasoned employees working in this type of environment and quite frankly insulting how we are being treated.

advice: To much of personal connection . Should be fair to the personal who is determined long term and proven result, how ever never get a chance for pay increase or the promotion without competion from personal preferences in middle management . They are having filled position without concern on existing employees . Must leave to have  better pay or at lest to meet market price with other financial institution .
pros: Great benefits , but I think after 5+ years you get this in most of the big banks .
cons: Used to be great place to make good monthly incentive pay,  since pay is bottom in the industry . New hires are making more due to market or to who hired them , and long term bankers are stuck on low pay but with the experience working for multiple people and expected to fill in every empty spot a day with same pay for years . Incentive is cut in every way possible in last 4 years. No rewards monetary and if you say something you can get sent to different branch or loose job .

summary: Good Place to Work, Technology and Culture can be Stifling. Tech salaries low.
advice: Invest more in technology salaries. Time and again people leave because technology is an afterthought. For a company that stresses that they are technology first company, you still have the old-timey mindset that front office should get all the money and technology should get the scraps.
pros: Amazing, Very Bright People. Decent benefits and pension if you stay that long. Tech salaries lag behind as you become more senior.
cons: The technology can lag behind industry standards by a large margin due to getting approvals and the scale of the system. The salary on the tech side can be uncompetitive. Technology teams tend to be the thing that they are always trying to make run leaner and always where they go when they need to reduce costs. They try to get people out of good programs by offering a very competitive intro salary, however salary growth quickly flatters, while front office skyrockets.

advice: The blatant nepotism is a turnoff. Try actually vetting people before promoting them to management positions. Cut the bureaucracy and let us do our jobs.
pros: Pays well, ample time off, great name on resume.
cons: Work life balance sucks. It’s not uncommon for people try to put meetings on your calendars after hours. Also there’s a ton of bureaucracy. Political landmines everywhere. Zero process management in DCE. Every single team does everything differently and people are turned into managers based off of nepotism (blatant at that) instead of actual merit. Also Chase is handling COVID extremely irresponsibly. Senior management basically threatened us with full time return to the office if we don’t comply with this hybrid schedule. Folks are exiting at a high rate and it’s very telling. Not a diverse culture at all and I’m in the NY office.

pros: No pro for this company.
cons: Really really really busy !!!

summary: Good place to work, though HR kind of annoying
advice: Allow employees to negotiate pay or to even discuss pay as telling us not to is technically illegal. Also listen to employees about complaints and about broken equipment instead of constantly getting them “serviced” to save money
pros:
“Part time” is minimum 30 but you always get to around 40 hours a week if that’s your goal. 
Plenty of ways and opportunities to go up in career if wanting to
Good pay and good amount of days off (equals about 3-4 weeks of paid time off.
cons:
HR can be annoying and doesn’t really help. Though they are just doing their job, you get the sense they are aggressive in only protecting chase.
Benefits take a minute to kick in, try to get hired around November because January benefits signed up for during this time kick in on New Years
Getting time off consecutively for a long vacation even if saved up time can be annoying as there is a shortage of staff.

advice: My advice would be to take "Talent Mobility" more serious.  There are so many opportunities within the company.  There is always someone to fill the need and someone who can excel at the opportunity.  I've seen plenty of good people past up for positions because someone else made friends and negotiated something in the background.  Lastly, be open to take more risk on accepting change.
pros: JPMC is a good company overall.  There is a diverse workplace, flexible wok schedules, lots of opportunity to expand your knowledge base and definitely great people. pros: Surrounded by smart, capable people, including bosses.  Almost everyone is friendly and easy to get on with.  Some cool tech to play with if you're on the right team/project, though some products are old and stale.  Solid pay and benefits, though not amazing.  Work-life balance good in my team - work from home pretty much whenever I need to, take holidays pretty much when I like, some late nights but not all the time.
cons: It's a big corp, so there's some fairly heavy bureaucracy pretty much everywhere you turn.  While you're piloting an application, you get plenty of freedom, but once you go live, there's no escaping the red tape.  Impossible to really be agile at that point.  Also, I gather salaries and benefits aren't top in the industry, which is surprising considering JP's position.

advice: Don't forget to be human...empathy goes a long way and culture will improve.  Make sure to reward the right people and watch out for folks who only manage up, kick down and/or play favoritism.
pros: Great global brand with diversified lines of business.  Many opportunities to move around and learn/develop but only for some.  Senior management changes every couple of years...some for good reasons and others for bad.  If you don't like your manager, most likely he/she will change - just ride it out.
cons: Company is too big to manage effectively and culture has suffered.  Not the place for you if you want work/life balance.  Pay is not competitive with market nor equitable for same roles...the longer you stay, compensation will suffer.  Management changes too often.  Nepotism is allowed - so be careful not to work for some senior officer's family or friends.

advice: Ops users need to be able to understand technology in order to properly work with developers. Applications are not created by a push of a button. Woke life balance is important in any industry, but technology seems to forget that.
pros: Really good benefits and plenty of vacation that they basically require you to use. Health insurance is decent. Tech stack isn't bad but a lot can be outdated quickly. Salary is about mid level. They will try to low ball you, but if you initially ask for higher they will most likely honor it. Does feel like a tech company within a bank for sure.
cons: Lots of red tape. Not really agile or devops though they claim that they are. The business users are not good at their jobs, and tech has to to basically do their jobs as well. You will be overworked, especially during covid-19.

jobTitle: Assistant Vice President Financial Planning & Analysis
advice: Always work to understand your staff beyond the typical day to day operations. They're real people too that are dealing with real life situations outside of work. Continue to promote work life balance from the top and ensure that it flows down through every level of the organization. It's important to know that the support is there.
pros: It was a great company to work for. I'd go back if the opportunity presents itself. We worked in a team setting within the finance team. The paid vacation is by far the best and the compensation is great too. I love the fact that it's a global company and the opportunities for advancement are endless.
cons: I wouldn't necessarily consider it a downside, but the fact that it's in the financial industry means that the overall market behavior has a direct result on the fate of companies in the industry. When the banking world took huge market plunges a lot of us were laid off at the time.

advice: Ensure that senior management has the proper credentials and experience. Reduce the highly politicized internal movements. Management has to be more transparent. Invest in human capital, which would reduce turnover. Continue to offer great benefits, but focus on a better work/life balance.
pros: The benefits the company has is one of the best in the industry. Multiple locations across the U.S. allows for unique opportunities. Generally, employees have diverse backgrounds, which increases knowledge and exposure to different mindsets. The pay is competitive, at least initially. The company is strong and will continue to be a cornerstone of the financial community.
cons: Senior management leadership took a massive step back in 2013-2014. This resulted in droves of departures by mid to entry level employees. This created a very high stress environment, and generally, the company culture shifted to more rigorous procedures with a very NY/NJ focus. There is not a strong emphasis on human capital. While the salary is competitive initially, don't expect that to change in continuing years without a battle.

summary: Excellent place to work. Excellent benefits as well!!!
advice: Management is awesome and I have no recommendations. They always do their best to help you if you are struggling or will find someone who can help you if they are unable to. Everything is done precisely and everyone follows the same practice as well. It is nice to finally work at a company where there are not lazy people and we are all treated equal!!!
pros:
When I say I Love my
Job, I mean it!!! Management is awesome!!! Excellent insurance, Ira, time off and more. Discounts on many things in life just for working there. Everyone is so nice and always does the right thing!!!
cons: There’s are not any. You do need to be licensed with many licenses which takes time snd the company they chose to use is very hard but worth it if you want to succeed in your career

jobTitle: App Support & Development/Database Administrator: Level2 Support Technician
summary: Why I would never work for JP Morgan Chase again
advice: How can you expect to maintain a low turn over rate of employees when the best they can hope for is they stay in long enough to burn out.  Give your employees a level playing field, instead of shifting sand, for them to build a foundation upon and you will see better results all arounf
pros: Several of my immediate co-workers were very nice.  My immediate supervisors were too.
cons: I came in at a lower hourly rate to get the job,  Forty-five days later they cut all contractors by 15% (ie they already knew the cut was coming before I got there, but made no mention of it, before hand ).  About he same time they moved me off of the position that I was hired for to a new team where they needed a warm body (I had zero skills for this position).  One month before my contract to hire was to transpire they told me they were going to upgrade my position and that I could still apply for it but as I would be under qualified for this position, I would not be qualified for that job.

summary: Pretty good place to work but difficult to move up
advice: Make sure you quickly and effectively address behavioral problems on your teams because it erodes team morale and drives people off eventually. You have a LOT of really excellent people who work for you at JPMC but allowing non-performers to kill your organizational morale is going to drive away all of your really good employees. It happened to me and 6 other people that I know of in the same location.
pros: Good working conditions, good pay, great benefits, great people, lots of lateral opportunity if you want to move around and learn new areas, Lots of on-campus perks if you like working in an office, mentor programs for younger workers
cons: Lots of pressure to be upwardly mobile with very few opportunities for upward mobility, Management often doesn't adequately address behavioral problems which negatively impacts the team, not flexible about hybrid/remote work

advice: Push for the leaders to conduct a market analysis every few years and adjust salaries accordingly. I have seen many top talent folks leave the organization (myself included) for a salary that is aligned with the market demands and job functions. When I left I made 47,000 with an annual bonus of 1,500. Now I earn 85,000 with an annual bonus of 15% of my salary; doing the same work as before.
