JP Morgan has been consistent, and there has still been a substantial amount of deal flow that has come in. In addition, the people here -- the culture, is generally nice, friendly and very open. There exists a bit of a superstar culture, but definitely nothing to the scale of another prominent i bank. Everyone here is here to help you succeed, because their own success depends on the back of yours.
cons: Hours, lack of flexibility, not as prestigious as other i banks

summary: Good industry...hard to predict long term success
advice: LISTEN to your employees
pros: Great industry...hard to not make money in banking.  There are good people who work here who care about what they do and want to win.  The industry is solid, regardless of what it is going through right now.  The industry will be back and when it is, there managers at JP Morgan Chase are smart enough to have the organization poised to do good things.  The atmosphere of the organization is congenial and is pleasant enough to work in, which obviously is a very big plus.
cons: Culture not focused on long term improvements.  Doesn't get how to develop people to enable success of the company.

summary: Used to be great company that went belly up because took too much risk
advice: Less risk taking, more risk control
pros: Good pay, good work life balance. Love living and working in the Seattle area. Wonderful offices, nice people. Was definitely one of the best banks out there until the financial crisis hit. Really a shame for things to have happened as they did, I have been really happy with my job there.
cons: Will probably loss my job in the acquisition, Bad office politics. Need to take fewer risks, be better stewards of capital. The integration with JP Morgan will be an interesting exercise. It will be interesting to see who all is kept and if they will have jobs going forward.

summary: JPMorgan ... the best brand on the street
advice: Senior management should considering hiring from a broader school base.  Group think will eventually cause problems
pros: JP Morgan is one of the best brands of the Street.  Considering the the whole street is moving toward the JPM models why not be with the best player.  They have slowly taken over most IB league tables and will continue the dominance.  Further, the AM business is thriving.
cons: Sometimes the environment can get a little too arrogant.  Some of the people who should not be in a position to lead are in said position.  One of the other downsides is that they don't actively hire MBAs into Invetment Management, only the Private bank.

advice: The best thing they could do is spend their time and effort in finding ways to simplify processes and reduce reporting (things that they expect employees to fill out). I find that I spend more time each day on these things.
pros: JPMorgan is such a large organizaton that there are many different ways you can grow within the company. Depending on the line of business you're in they may or may not encourage you to explore. I've found that the Retail Bank is much more open to this than the Commercial Bank.
cons: Large company. Lot of reporting and process. They are pushing more and more things to call centers which tend to make problems worse.

advice: Keep focusing on the customer experience. Fully staff branches. Recognize and appreciate employee performance and development.
pros: A brand people recognize, good benefits/perks program for employees. Platform continuously being enhanced, very good data sources. Good integration between branch channels; providing clients with a somewhat seamless transition between banking, investments, business, and lending.
cons: Incentive program was cut every year. Higher production required to make the same or less than previous year. Employee expectations and responsibilities continuously increase; salaries rarely increase. Top performers typically get "meets expectations" in performance reviews. Very hard to move up in within the organization based on performance alone. Communication between departments is not seamless. Advisor/Banker support could be more efficient.

advice: Care more for your employees you are losing good people for the lack of acknowledgement. As well do not give promotions base of politics of who you know. It will always be denied that that is done but it is the Truth.
pros: Benefits and co workers is what makes you get through the day.
cons: Promotions are given by who you know not the work you give. Management expects you to go above and been to be notice but basically your stuck doing their dirty work and you get no credit and get stuck with the same pay. Training was horrible you get basic knowledge but everything you learn is really once you hit production floor. Many get depressed and stress due to management and drama that is going on.

summary: Good for starters, not for the long run
advice: Be more transparent and fair with the people doing the ground work (analysts and associates).  Many are smart and with great potential, really great assets, but you underpay them and overwork them.
pros: Some really nice and smart people. The glamor of working for a recognizable brand.
cons: Little internal mobility. Promotions not based on meritocracy. If you started at a low salary because they recruited you out of college, you will always be hugely underpaid. They would rather have people quit and lose talent than give salary increases. In the long run they lose because they end up hiring someone for a higher salary than the person who quit.

advice: During times of trials and tribunes, it is always smart to remember the most critical segment of the successful business JPMorgan has grown to be, and that is the lower of the totem pole at the consumer banking level. These are the employees that day after day meet with clients and earn their trust.
pros: Loved working with a team based environment.  Working within a consumer branch has given me the opportunity to be able to work with different colleagues at all different levels all shooting and trying to achieve the same goal.
cons: Had been going through some rough waters as a company as a whole. The lower level of consumer banking was not compensated enough for the job  and effort they put in.

summary: Corporate environment with interesting software challenges to solve and tons of bureaucracy.
advice: Listen to your employees better, promote people who actually have technical ability instead of "Yes men".
pros:
There are some good people to work with at this company in Digital, the team in Seattle is filled with experienced people. 
In my situation, I am enabled to work autonomously at my own pace and I have input on my assignments. This will depend on your manager.
Very stable employer from a financials standpoint.
cons:
This place does not operate like a technology company, management is very much top down in a typical bank, large corporate institution setting. 
Most of the managers are extremely risk weary, they would rather leave a problem unsolved than risk breaking something.

advice: Many bankers are talented and have potential to move in other areas in the company not just in banking. If you do this, you'll have more loyalty. If something happens in the company the bankers are the first to feel the cuts in the company. We are the bottom barrell.
pros: The staff I worked with was amazing and became family to me. The branch I worked in became home and I felt part of the community. The programs and training are better than I've seen with other banks.
cons: As a woman you will get paid less, negotiate well. Managers were like revolving doors. You will be pushed like a car salesmen to meet that branch's goal. Rare salary increases and promotions.

advice: No advice- they don't listen or care anyway.
pros: Endless opportunities (work) and mobility. If you are lazy, they wont fire you.
cons:
Your salary does not keep up with the cost of living. The company claims they are 'manage through these challenging times' however they have increased their dividend payout and stock is now an all time high after the pandemic. 

Hard working professionals that allowed them to weather the pandemic storm were rewarded with coffee mug and a cake pop when they returned to office- seriously.

When JPMorgan received stimulus money from government on a Saturday and then waited until Wednesday to distribute- it proved to me they only care about stock price and investors.

I have values and empathy- therefore this company is no longer a fit for me.

advice: Learn what management is by looking at successful companies with happy employees. (Hint: Look at top 100  and 1000 lists of companies to work for which JPMorganChase is never on. Look at best companies for minorities and employee preferred companies list.) Employees are better off working for Bank of America, Wells Fargo, any other bank, or McDonalds.
pros: Stable company so far, diverse, pays on time, benefits, global, now allows full 1 hour lunches, now allows you to develop your own career path
cons: Discriminates against blacks by saying, after years of employment, your credit is not perfect, so you're fired. Worst management ever. Poor training or barely any and constantly finding ways of saing no matter how good you are doing, its never good enough. Unrealistic goals and no cooperation amongst peers or other teams since you compete against each other with the same title (crab mentality).

summary: Good work environment but not highest quality
advice: Management needs to focus on giving more time to learn new skills and improve systems that exist instead of continuing to add more and more work when they know the teams are already over worked. Need to stop committing  to work hoping they can higher the people to do it since they have had a hard time finding the right people.
pros:
Lots of mobility in with different tools, tech, and locations
Level of skill required before working here not too high. They are willing to train on the job.
Full benefits
cons:
High demand on time depending on team. 
Hard to get a team using cutting edge tech. Lots of old tech
Lots of maintaining systems jobs, fewer creating new things jobs.
High level of bureaucracy

summary: Overall it's a decent company to work for.
advice: Certain senior managers could use some serious improvements as to how they treat their subordinate managers and their employees.
pros: Excellent paid and unpaid benefits and company discounts.
cons: "Change is constant" and constant change is an understatement.   Too much change is not stable but chaotic and negatively impacts customer values.  Employees are continually being degraded and devalued.  Countless co-workers hired within the same time frame have left due to the mistreatment of employees, while the ones that remain, maintain a silent discontent for fear of termination.  It's a high-stress, high-deadline demand work environment with intense regulations.

summary: C.H.A.S.E. = Cheat, Hose And Screw, Everyone
advice: Inpedentant thouths and ideas sould be encouraged and not punishied. People should be advanced because of there qualifications and abilities, not by their gender, ethniciity, and sexual orientation, and not by the ability to kiss butt.
pros: Benefits. Good health insurance and 401K plans. Generous time off ,sick leave and vacation time.
cons: Unless you are a YES person, and you are a minority advancement is just a dream. Extreamly high attrition rate. First level and mid-level management are rarely on the same page. Information for policy and procedures changes is constantly and is indiscriminitly applied. The human rescouces department will have different answers to ones questions and concerns dependining on who you talk with. Constant change in policy and procedures.

advice: Accept the desired agile transformation by being a part of the solution and not part of the problem.
pros: 1) Jobs usually pay higher but in hindsight it is generally not worth it having to suffer through the politics of such a large org.
cons:
1) IT Teams have no structure and seem to reinvent the wheel every step of the way
2) Turnover is so high that all system domain knowledge is non-existent 
3) The culture is toxic and seems to be driven by how many direct employees you manage
4) Most technology stacks are beyond maintainable and there is a heavy focus on rebuilding (Opportunity)
5) Agile transformation is in the very early stages causing conflict as middle mgmt. fights to stay relevant

summary: Jp Morgan, if you can get in stay in.
advice: n/a
pros: It was a very good company to work for.  Until I was laid off I was pleased with the moves of the company.  Senior management helps in allowing you to move forward in the company.
cons: getting laid off is not easy.  A little more detailed when it comes to helping you find a clear direction within the fold of the company.  Needs a lot more minority integration on the trading floors.  you can pick minorities out with ONE hand.  give more opportunities and spread around the major amount of money being given to the employees.  you have to claw to stay.. and force your way in the door if you are a minority.. trust me

advice: Clean up your act literally. Have the custodial/cleaning staff do a better job and maybe less people will get sick and show up to work.
pros: Benefits and pay depending what you do.
cons: I have been with the firm 2 years and in those 2 years, I've seen the cleaning crew vacuum only twice. We walk in every morning and our desks are covered in black soot from the vents. Every 3 hours we have to wipe down our desks. The carpets are so filthy, that I dropped something and it laid there for 3 weeks before it was picked up. Our office in Tampa, FL the Fountain Square hub has a lot of people with allergies and bad asthma. These are horrible conditions to have employees working under. When employees get sick and continue to get sick then they have to take the penalty for missing a day.

summary: Too corporate, too large, and too political! Good pay, good marketing/software system
advice: There is not enough local decision making and too many things come from middle level management without the lower level knowledge. Not enough separation between power/authority that Retail Banking has over Business Banking. I think its great to work together, but Retail Management does NOT understand Business Banking, so they should not have any power, control, or authority over Business Bankings Management or roles of the Business Bankers.
pros: There marketing software computer system for doing sales as a Banker is top notch. The salary and commission structure was good 7 years ago, not sure for today.
cons: There is not enough local decision making and too many things come from middle level management without the lower level knowledge.

pros: Very stable environment. The company truly understands work/life balance. Competitive salary and great benefits/time off etc. Jamie Dimon (CEO) is taking the company down the right path year after year. As long as he's in office, the company will flourish.
cons: While the company does appreciate work/life balance, they have no problems tipping the scale to the work side but in all fairness, they only asked me to work long hours only if it was absolutely necessary and they would make it up to me later but during those long hours, it was very stressful. I don't really approve of the company's off-shoring tactics. I hate to see all the good local talent going to waste just to save money.

advice:
Hiring technical experts that don’t like people, into management jobs makes for a bad employee experience.  Bad people managers are sometimes weeded out, only to be rehired in another area.   
Too much emphasis on new college grads, who consume scant promotional opportunities  and then leave the bank within 5-7 years.
pros: Top notch Competitor, incredibly stable firm, with powerhouse CEO. Well funded marketing and customer experience teams. Room to move into different lines of business, or possibly different locations.
cons: It’s a big machine, for sure. We used to joke that the writer of the cartoon Dilbert must be a Chase employee. They recently have turned a corner and are making great strides to Improve the employee experience. Kudos.

summary: My Life in the Big League
advice: My advice would be to treat your staff with respect. The better you treat them the harder they will work for you. At Chase whenever our targets were met we would be rewarded with a special lunch and/or company gifts.
pros: Working in the Legal Dept at Chase was a very memorable experience. It gave me a chance to work in an area that I had no prior knowledge of. It was a very hectic environment and we had targets to meet every quarter but the people that I worked with made it tolerable, and eventually, enjoyable.
cons: There were no real down sides, the long hours were tiring on the brain sometimes, but the work needed to be done so we never complained.

summary: Great to get your foot in the door, no future in this department however
advice: Fire Client Service middle and upper management because no actual leadership is happening.
pros: Very visible role, exposure to lots of senior executives and high-profile clients. If you can do a good job and get the ear of the right people, you can go far.
cons: No upward mobility, management is a sham - they only promote “friends” and seems to have no basis on actual performance. In fact, performance metrics (when brought up in meetings) are never considered and so lots of people just don’t do their job and in order to keep clients happy you have to do it or your team suffers. Lots of attrition because of this.

pros: Jamie runs a great company.  All the people i work with and for are extremely smart and motivated.  If you are active in managing your career, the opportunities are there - but they do not come to you.  There is a lot of mobility as well.  I much prefer working for a US based bank, having worked for others.
cons: It is a BIG company, and with it comes some groups that are better managed than others.  It is not a place to work hard and hope good things come.  End of year reviews can be brutal and you need to ensure you understand the rules upfront.  And that you have a manager that has your best interest at heart.

summary: Solid company with name recognition and decent work life balance
advice: Treat the employees that have more experience better via salary increases. Too much of a push for high salaries for new hires make the people with experience feel they are being vastly underpaid
pros:
For college new hires they start you a pretty high salary with good increases year to year
Can get up to 4 weeks of paid vacation relatively quickly, 5 weeks if you stick around for a long time or are upper management
Depending on team can have a very easy going work environment
cons:
Experience will differ greatly based on Manager
Salary can stagnate if you are not part of the college hire program or are not aggressive about asking for raises
Prefer you to work longer than 8-5 but some teams more than others

summary: Good project experience, but bad work-life balance and career mobility
advice: Promote employees to VP, ED, and MD roles early instead of provoking them to leave the firm for a competitor out of frustration. Provide more generous raises and bonuses to teams that were stretched beyond capacity. Do a better job of prioritizing projects in terms of value-add and provide better work-life balance
pros:
Opportunities to work on projects involving high-profile partners and high-scale business impact
Good vacation benefits
cons:
High employee burnout- many managers aren't respectful of employees' time and pressure them to waste time on low-value projects
Low career mobility- experienced employees get promised they'll have opportunities for promotions which don't materialize after years of waiting
Low employee morale- many employees' desire to remain with the firm is running out because of the lack of genuine employee appreciation by upper management

summary: Wamu was a great company to work for - Chase . . .not so much!
advice: since it is now Chase, I don't have any advice for them, because they are clearly NOT Wamu.  Some may see this as good, but there are lot of us out there who only see this as sad and very wrong.
pros: my experience with Wamu was great.  I had a good manager who believed in me and the work I did, and who was also a very dedicted and hard working manager.  Benefits were excellent and pay was comparable.
cons: the obvious is that the high level execs were doing things that were not in the best interest of the company.  I would say that lack of communication was the most frustrating thing about the place.

advice: Continue to invest in technology as a competitive advantage.  Try to build a more meritocratic culture for development of projects that have business value.  Kill projects that don't and reallocate those resources to the ones that do, providing challenging, rewarding opportunities for all.
pros:
Top of almost every league table
Cutting edge finanical products
Wide range of business lines
Good technology mix
Some effort to create best practice and architecture across all organizations.
cons: Corporate environment tends to encourage managers to build little empires and the politics of these are problematic.  Projects that have no point survive because the person in charge has some pull with higher-ups, while projects that have a clear business value die for the opposite reason.  There is an upper limit to how high an individual technical contributor can rise.

advice: Many more options are presented to new grads than ever before that are offering challenging, well-paid jobs with a much better work/life balance, thanks to the booming technology industry. If the same kind of talent is expected to be attracted to firms such as JP Morgan, there needs to be a critical review of the number of hours that analysts are expected to work. It's just not productive and is detrimental to both the quality of work and health of the analyst.
pros:
- Decent pay for junior level job
- Dinner and cab service is provided when long hours
cons:
- As a junior employee, the amount of hours that you put in largely determines the perception of your performance (not the quality of your work)
- Work/life balance is abysmal
- Type of work is not interesting

summary: A company full of empty vessels
advice:
Wake up. If Mr Morgan had been here today he would have hanged you continuously for 108 days.
Please run analytics on your own wasteful business practices and correct yourself
pros:
(i) Large company with many products, so opportunity to learn about different types of businesses
(ii) People think, you work for a great company!
cons:
(i) This is a place full of empty vessels, who can only talk well but have little depth
(ii) Most likely you will be in the company of greedy arrogant people who always think about their bonus
(iii) No one cares about how your work could be used for the benefit of the company. They are always worried about saving their own skin and putting up a great show to impress  bosses.
(iv) Remain busy in the thick of thin things of little substance
(v) It has a very unproductive hierarchy based culture. So if you are not that high up, your voice / views / emails will carry little value.

advice: Let IT groups specialize and deliver better applications, platforms, and service that fits the specific needs of individual lines of business and departments.
pros: Strong commitment to diversity, ethics, regulatory compliance, and security, casual Fridays, good feedback from management, employee banking discounts, major investments in philanthropy and volunteering opportunities.
cons: Only branch in Delaware is the employee-only branch in the office, very dated desktop platforms, incompetent Global IT help desk whose primary function is to force you to use self-service intranet sites, salary growth over time is limited even when getting promoted, benefits used to be good but have gotten progressively worse over time, ongoing push to centralize IT groups that always results in more bureaucracy, less expertise, lousy service, slower response times, and limited accountability.

advice: Rather than trying to enforce a uniform policy for motivation, try to determine what it is that motivates each individual.  If a person is not performing well as a salesman, but shows great signs of responsibility and attention to detail, find a place for them.
pros: Great sales and leadership training. If you work hard at achieving your sales goals, you can often push for further advancement or career path changes.
cons: Very political - management can tend to favor.  You have to maintain your numbers constantly, as the sales cycle is monthly, which can get redundant.  There is a LOT of bending of the rules, which is promoted by management... until it isn't.  Management is hardly ever up front with their employees when it comes to anything other than sales.

advice: Try not to tie compensation and benefits to what the "typical" and similar institution might do, consider trying to be best in class in this area as well.
pros:
Focus on employee career development
Well run organization with tight controls and a focus on integrity
Many areas for growth, IT, Business, Operations
Locations all over the world, with opportunities to work abroad even in entry level positions
cons:
Focus is clearly on hiring younger workers, and eliminating the positions for those who've been around perhaps a bit too long
Easy to become involved to the point of "My Life for You", especially as you climb the ladder
Inertia is strong here, will take quite some time effect change, especially at the rank and file level
When they are "through with you", expect to be encouraged to move on.

advice: Better salaries for existing employees, I started with 31 k yearly , with a MBA and three bachelor degrees over 10 years management and banking experience , I have 4 years with the company and I still on the low Household income level, very sad
pros: Benefits, opportunities, long term career, great experience and good partners
cons:
The salaries are very low, they offer commissions with a bunch of if’s (gaps and conditions ) Wages are too low $13/15? For a licensed banker it’s not a good hourly /rate it’s sad 😞 employment contracts conditional to stay with the company.
matching 401k is low and conditional until feb every year , 3 years with the company to get pension vested -hours of operations at branches until late hours , no room to life balance-

advice: People are the key... balance the "easy to do" talent cherry-picking from outside the firm,  with the development of  internal talent
pros: Opportunities - worldwide... fast paced environment loaded with smart people.. if you love being in the vortex of the tornado, then you will love this place... opportunities to take on more than you'd normally expect... 3 years here can be like 5-6 elsewhere, in terms of visability, exposure and learnings
cons: if you are looking for stability, balance and to "just do your job", then you may well fit in here... but expect others around you to be aggressive and assertive and to be left standing there while others are moving on

advice: offer more feedback to junior employees, communicate the company's direction
pros: The company offers a lot of opportunities for new workers. New hires are able to work in a variety of different fields. There is strong senior leadership and managers are frequently giving feeback about the job performance. J P Morgan Chase has many different areas to work in, in the investment bank, commercial bank, private bank, and asset management. The company is continuing to increase with its acqusitions of Bear Stearns and Companies and Washington Mutual. These acquisitions will definetly position J P Morgan Chase for future growth. The company is well positioned for high sustainability even in the present market environment.
cons: long hours, low pay, job insecurity

advice: Management goes too far.  Leave the employees be so they can work.  Stop stressing employees out with new rules and when letting people go, don't call them out on the floor.  Please, if you are going to praise an employee, let them enjoy it.  Stop coming back later in the day and coach them on a possible error.
pros: Coworkers are great, always looking out for each other, for the most part.
cons: Cult like atmosphere.  It's a call center for collections.  They monitor everything and set up new policy and procedures constantly.  Nearly impossible to get incentive.  Low pay.  Chase doesn't like the older population and finds ways to get rid of them.  If I could find a better a job, like I had in the better days, I wouldn't walk I would run.

summary: Great place to work if in a great team and function
advice:
Reduce layers of bureaucracy. Make processes more efficient. Provide competitive salary increase to keep valuable employees.  Too many layers of red-tape kills creativity and innovation. 

Need to include Sabbatical in benefits to compete with other companies in same industry.
pros:
Hires from within. 

Encourages mobility within the company but needs full actionable support from your manager to make it happen. Difficult if you are a critical member of the team.
cons:
Salary increase is minimal (0-2%>) once you are in doesn't cut it.. So make sure to negotiate the max up front. 

Lots of red-tape when you work with IT...too many sheeps. Probably the worst in my experience.

advice: Allow the talent that joins the organization be part of the change process and foster an environment to share ideas within the team.
pros: Chase is a great company to work for with a lot of benefits and opportunity.  It is a large organization and you get all the perks.  Great co-workers, very loyal employees.
cons: The struggle was with the workload and the lack of autonomy.  Individual contributors don't have a voice as everything is pushed down from the top.  Your job is very specific and there isn't room for working outside your specific job responsibilities unless you are promoted or transfer, which you have to be in your role for 1 year.

summary: Benefits are good, but the workload became unsustainable with no compensation
pros: I was in an IT line of business the whole time I was there and found it to be immensely rewarding for a long time. There were daily challenges and opportunities to learn and grow. For the most part management was supportive. Benefits were very good, when compared to other jobs.
cons: For the line of business that I was employed in the demands and expectations on workload became unsustainable. A lot of the flexibility and autonomy that made this job great for me in the past was being chipped away with constant re-organizations and management being more concerned with their own personal needs than bringing people together to get more done for the business.

summary: Good to work for not for career advancement
advice: Diversify middle to senior management positions. Give employees a chance advance by promoting someone up the chian whith the team/Org Chart. Stop giving the jobs to the same circle of people.
pros: Competitive salary, excellent work life balance , 4 weeks vacation for officer and above. Excellent place to start your career to get the experience you need. If you're looking for career advancment, there is little to none. I see people who work here for 10, 15 years and still can't make VP needless to say a management position.
cons: Not diverse at management level. If you are minority, prepare to work at a dead end job with little to no chance to advance. In addition, management positions are often given to friends and buddies of the person in charge and not by individual performance.

summary: Great work life balance. Not micromanaged as long as you are performing. Revenue Grid is low.
advice: Remember what it was like to be an advisor who is not based in New York or California.
pros: Great client base because you have people walking into the branch every day. Normal amount of pressure in a sales job. Bonus for Net New Money is great. Can offer several fund families and products.
cons: Compensation changes every year and it is never for the better. Resistant to bringing in new products that may be offered by a competitor because of the size of the company and massive due diligence it would take. Middle management is great but the upper management seem out of touch.

summary: Decent place to get a start
advice: Be proactive in developing your workforce on the retail side. Don't be "cheap" with time or money. Invest in stronger training programs that last longer than 3 days. Live your values, help clients with difficult situations. The rule book shouldn't be the only answer, being flexible when necessary can make a world of difference.
pros: Largest Bank. Great Benefits. Great Culture (Very dependent on branch). Great opportunity to grow personally and professionally. Ability to build very strong relationships with clients and co-workers.
cons: Some managers are very old fashioned. Favoritism is evident. For a "financial institution" there are too many unprofessional employees AND not enough employees that care about the financial well being of clients.

summary: Great Company too bad they dont like to pay their people
advice: Find ways to reward branch employees for their work. Alot of turnover and new employees should not come in making same money as experienced bankers. No annual salary increase is degrating to staff and lowers moral. No Branch managers have too much control. Also open company up to advancement internally.
pros: great training, good people with strong work ethic, excellent benefits, diversity key, strong management
cons: Branch level employees are grossly underpaid and overworked. Alot of pressure to find ways to make money outside of salary for bankers. Salary extremely low and highly incentive based. Issue is bankers are bogged down with playing door greeter instread being able to focus on task to make them money for liveable wage.

advice: Save the company millions by firing yourself.
pros:
Money is paid to you in exchange for the work you do.
Highly recognizable name looks nice on your CV.
Company is surprisingly functional given its size and complexity.
Employees using direct deposit are eligible for a free checking account, and up to a quarter of a percent discount on a qualifying mortgage loan.
cons:
Salaries are low and do not increase, though bonuses can be large enough to offset inflation.
Performance evaluation for non-traders is based purely on whether you can get a trader to say something nice about you.  
Reviews are provided solely to give you a sense of justification for the long hours you have worked and do not affect compensation.

summary: Solid, strong company, but can be bureaucratic.
advice:
Stop "busy bragging" about how awful and stressful your life is, it takes some of the appeal out of getting promoted for us peons.
Don't be so risk averse around change management, hire skilled professionals and trust their judgment.
pros:
Many mangers are OK with working from home.
Managers trust employees to solve problems.
Time off is very generous.
Company earns billions - little worry about indiscriminate layoffs (if you are a good performer).
cons:
Company has to cross all t's and dot all i's due to intense regulatory scrutiny. 
Formalized change management processes can substantially slow efforts.
Many projects are butt-covering rather than innovative in nature, due to the regulatory clampdown.

advice: please stop overlooking the talent in house!
pros: JP Morgan Chase is a great place to work. The pay scale is competitive and the job is extremely professional and highly respected. The company provided adequate training to ensure the employees are knowledgable. The benefits are great and the flexibility is great.
cons: The only complaint I have about the company is the the lack to promote from with. I can not understand why a company would choose a person with no banking experience and place them as a Branch Manager as opposed to someone who know the systems and has been with the company for a while. This blows my mind. I often see management doing the carrot on a string to the employees and this bothers me. I wish there were more advancement from within with out haveing to jump through hoops!

advice: Top executives should listen to mid-tier managers. They're the direct connections to the employees and those employees are usually first in line to work with clients.
pros: JP Morgan is a huge company with offices around the world. There are plenty of opportunities across various lines of business. The bank is constantly seeking new talent.
cons: JP Morgan is the largest bank in the US and one of the largest financial institutions in the entire world. Because of this, top level executives are often out of touch with locations outside of its headquarters in New York City. Major decisions, even made under positive intentions, are made in NYC and their effects could have negative consequences toward non-US markets.

summary: I spent 10 years at JPM Chase where I worked in 5 different roles. Department head and Program/Project Manager
advice: Focus on long term planning and staff development
pros: I personally had a great deal of mobility. On the flip side, I had no choice because my position was eliminated, or I had completed a large project. I enjoyed working with very smart co-workers. Hard work and a focus on meeting your commitments will go a long way.
cons: Some managers like to micro-manage their teams. Reviews and inter rankings are very political. Global departments tend to be the worse offenders (New York vs. London).  Work life balance is mostly negative, but it all depends on your role and your manager. Projects and initiatives tend to managed by crisis.

summary: Great place to get sales experience
advice: Help customers! Don't make them wait when you can help them yourself. DMs tell us you're supposed to be the one "saving" relationships when they come to close their accounts, but all of you pass them off to a banker and then drill us on why we couldn't get them to stay.
pros: Health benefits, cell phone plan discounts, paid holidays, above average paid vacation, the ability to transfer, top of the line tools and resources to perform job well.
cons: The push towards technology is going to cause a lot of job loss. Older clientele is becoming angry because they are being pushed to use technology and don't want their human interactions to go away.

advice: Stop the micro management/favoritism/nepotism, hire supervisors/mangers that knows the ins/outs of the  work of the department they are running or train them first about the work of the department until they do, also, practice what you preach about  how to have a pleasant corporate environment for employees.
pros: Worked with lots of good people with the same excellent work ethics from all ethnicities which I felt was great cause we got things done correctly by working together as a team.
cons: There was a lot of micro managing from supervisors/mangers, a LOT of favoritism from the top down, couldn't get answers from management for the correct procedures that have been changed many times, at department meetings - told to ask questions & give ideas that will improve work flow during the meeting, but then chastised by the facilitators of the meeting when a person does ask a question he/she doesn't like & the underlings ideas aren't good enough to be tried, also, its not what you know - its who you know for advancement.

summary: Old School Management Practices Reduces Appeal to Younger Generations
advice: I get it, you got to where you are by working long hard hours and personal sacrifice.However, newer generations are able to create far more productivity than you ever could, using technology and less time.  There is a rightful expectation to reap the rewards of this innovation and create a culture of a better work life balance.  Accept this or let your company gradually deflate due to a drain of the best talent.
pros: Great name brand. Global. Internal Mobility. Brilliant colleagues.
cons: Worst pay on the street. Old School management (work long = hard work): this discourages gains in productivity and innovation through technology and encourages creating the illusion of being busy.

summary: Just be careful which department you fall into
advice: Don't treat employees like children. Some were very respectful, and seemed to genuinly care about their employees. Others...not so much.
pros: Excellent benefits, great opportunities for medical savings, employee discounts to local and chain stores/restaraunts, matching 401k and pension
cons: I've been a part of two departments within JPMC. The first one was run terribly. The employees were treated like 10 year olds. You could go for weeks without having an independant thought in your head. Then my second department was run completely different. Lenient arrival, lunch, and departure times. Occasional free lunch. Managers would ask how your day is going (you don't appreciate this unless you've experienced the opposite).

advice: Keep it up, just when you guys are advertising or selling the job, please do not lie and say that there is so much technical exposure you are basically a technical analyst . Tell them what the job actually entails.
pros:
Decent Pay
Great Work life balance
Work is interesting but not too hard
Great atmosphere
Management Is fantastic and supportive
cons: No technology exposure. Especially someone graduating and coming from a technical background you will not grow in audit. I am currently facing a challenge where I need to go out because of lack of technological exposure. If you are from a technical background.. CS/IT/IS GET OUT! do not come because you will fall into the same trap I did.

advice: Things has already gone to far - not sure if any advise can be shared.  A positive cooperation among managing personnel would be desired.
pros: Benefits such as vacation, personal days, good medical, dental, vision.  Have some options considering 'carier' mobility inside 300k employee company. Good welcoming package including overview for company, meeting people and higher management, sharing thoughts on ways in regards to advancement.
cons: Lack of fairness in HR, lots of things going on behind the scenes. Management seems to lack direction , have peculiar evaluation practices  give bad ratings to the group when group is supposed to be dismissed (one way or another).  Favoritism, cronyism , lack of diversity.

advice: Get back to taking care of your middle/lower income customers.  They are the ones that got you to where you are now.  Don't just concentrate on Chase Private Client Services.
pros: I worked for Chase for 8 years in the mortgage loan department.  They gave me great opportunities for advancement.  The company terminated our position and they gave us a severance package and contracted a 3rd party agency to assist us in finding another job within the company or outside of the company.
cons: I believe the company is getting a little too big and losing sight of good customer service.  Looks like they are concentrating more on the high end customers and forgetting about the middle/low income customers.

advice: Chase has a hard time sticking to the rules.
pros: Full time, set hours, holidays off with seniority.
cons: Department was dissolved when it had been created only a year before I was hired. I worked there 5 years. Apparently this happens frequently with Chase, a few people in my department had said this was their second or third time they were forced to find another position due to department being dissolved. Also, Myself and several others in dept were not being paid sift differential that by law we should have been receiving. A fairly new supervisor realized what they were doing and demanded they back pay everyone. I still don't think they paid me everything they owed, but at least I received some of it back.

summary: Not bad, but not that good either
advice:
Stop the nepotism and cronyism.  Promote qualified individuals into positions of more responsibility.
Follow the established procedures to be successful.  
Get away from the "Never time to do it correctly, but always time to do it twice" mentality
pros:
Large company with established procedures.
Coworkers friendly and knowledgable.
Most peers professional and really cared about the quality of product they were producing.
Good benefits and vacation time
cons:
"Kingdom building" - managers moved around and brought in their own people to an organization cutting out advancement for others.
Having to interface with other technology groups that often didn't have the same work ethic and sense of urgency.
Setting hard delivery dates for a project before scoping or even understanding technical aspects of the project.

summary: Good, structured environment with open opportunities
advice: Constant reorganizing means those at the bottom are busy renaming/reworking things instead of moving forward with important projects.
pros: I found working at JP Morgan to be *very* dependent on what team you're on - some teams are great, some are awful, most are somewhere in between.  BUT I the amount of mobility that was possible (especially within IT) was enough to ensure that you could find a great situation with a little bit of effort.  Great pay, too.
cons: The company is so huge that you can get lost sometimes.  You might have to be shrewd or do a little political positioning to get to where you want to go.

advice: Keep up the good work, continue to foster an environment that your employees want to work for.  Maintain the values that have placed J.P. Morgan at the top of the list of firms worldwide.
pros: Great pay, culture, opportunities for growth and success.  Excellent training structure and ability to obtain the skills necessary to succeed.  Supportive management that foster and environment you want to work in.
cons: No real cons that I can think of.  The only thing is J.P. Morgan is so big that the ladder if very high to climb.  You have plenty of intelligent colleagues to compete with when climbing, but that's not really a bad thing because they challenge you and you can learn from everyone.

advice: Stop micromanaging and learn to actually care about your staff and recognize the good they do instead of spitting constant negative unappreciative comments to create a negative work environment.
pros: there are an unbelievable amount of opportunities to make money commission wise, but forget about raises unless you suck up to management who micromanages you beyond belief.
cons: Very stressful work environment. Management is always snooping on you trying to find something you're doing wrong while there's no time to go on your 30min lunch (which used to be an hour) or even go to the bathroom. If you do not suck up forget about a raise or a chance to move up within the company. You also have to learn how to fake doing your work being that there is not enough time to get things done...goodluck working at Chase...ha!

pros: Jp Morgan Chase is a conservative bank when it comes to lending, and very compliant. great place to learn the industry, and lots of opportunity to move within retail banking. Sky is the limit with commissions, and branch partners are key to making money at this company.
cons: difficult to move from retail to corporate unless you are well connected. Too many titles in banker roles now which confuses the customers and gives the banker too much to focus on. Other banks are more competitive with salaries, and Chase does not come up the difference. Salary increases are almost comical if you stay in the role,. Only opportunity for salary increase is with a role change.

advice: Try to foster a healthier working environment, bosses were very tough and cut throat but we got done what was needed to succeed. Also, there seemed to be lots of lone wolfs, I feel that if we worked better together it would have made a better work place
pros: High pay, great benefits I really liked working there because I made a lot of money and those around me were being paid highly as well
cons: long hours, stressful. It is tough to work such a stressful job for so long but once you get into the hang of things, the long hours do not seem too bad, but they do get to you from time to time.

summary: Large company with many layers of management.
advice: There is a large void between mid-management and upper management.   Mid management is still aware of the actual work being completed and people involved,  but have very little support from upper management.   Upper management is too focused on managing up only.
pros: They offer quality training opportunities,  as long as you are pro-active and use the resources available on their intranet.   Decent annual bonuses.
cons: Difficult to navigate between the different business units.  While they promote mobility you really need the support of your direct manager which is not readily available and the HR department does not help.  Basic benefits but they don't provide annual raises, even for cost of living increases.

jobTitle: Vice President and Senior Asset Manager Global Real Estate
advice: If you are going to hire military veterans, it may make more sense to have their managers undergo training to better understand the mindset and culture that the veterans are coming from.
pros: Well organized work environment with excellent technology and HR support systems.  The entire team I worked with are industry professionals bringing best practices to the table.  JPMC does a great job attempting to hold its employees by providing cross training and encouraging individuals to apply for various lines of business to increase their understanding of the banking and finance industry.
cons: People are commodities, and as the organization changes its focus it is not uncommon to see large groups of employees reduced from the rolls.

summary: The Brand is not extended to employees
advice: Current employees who receive mid-year promotions should not have to wait to year end to have their level changed. And there is no guarantee the level higher level will be granted. If you hired from the outside that person would have been brought in at the new level. This policy disadvantages existing employees.
pros: Working for a highly respected company - looks good on a resume. The division where I work is more customer focused. A strong advancement from several years ago.
cons: Always the swirl of layoffs. Not an employee focused company. Treat current employees poorly. They ask every year how they can improve employee morale. Simple become an employee NOT cost cutting focused company. Do things that show you care about your people. Too focused on the bottom vs. doing things to build a positive work environment.

summary: If you enjoy working with smart people to solve challenging problems, this is the place.
advice: Keep challenging us to be better, and keep supporting us with the resources to deliver on the challenge!
pros: Global leader in the financial space that is not willing to rest on its laurels.  The talent and leadership is unmatched.  Immense amount of resources available to bring to bear on solving important problems.  Clear focus on providing the best service for the client.
cons: Scale of the organization means you need to have an ability to develop strong relationships to get things done.  Geographical dispersion often prevents face to face meetings so you need to be comfortable using collaborative technologies.

advice: Suggest to Top management a work/ life balance program. It would make everyone happier, people may choose to stay with the company longer and you as a Management won't have to frequently hire new people as might do now.We all know how long that could be.
pros: Its a great company to work for, high expectations of customer service, professionalism, and accuracy. Also, offered a good variety of benefits including insurance and 401k.
cons: There is low work/ life balance. Expect your whole life to revolve around the branch. I advise you pick a location that is close to home/ school/ children's daycare etc. If you intend to make a career in banking especially sales, choose a location that has high volume clients no matter the commute.

advice: Sorry for your life, but stay at least until you find another rock to crawl under...smile!
pros: Receiving a check every two weeks, weekends, days that there was a state of emergency due to snow fall...
cons: Life sucking cubicle environment. Finger pointing central, smh. Everyone was ruled by fear! The buck stopped nowhere and people were constantly in fear of their jobs. They don't negotiate for entry level positions. There will be "no" paid happy hours! Record profits every year, but no pay raises... This is back office operations and your gonna feel it immediately (meaning your the dude shoveling coal into this "Titanic" of a Company). Workloads so heavy and depressing that you'll fear your own "vacation time"!

advice: You have to stop the bleeding. You have really smart, loyal employees, managers, and VPs with years of expertise,  who have done all they can to support and back your play. Please don't let them go.  Retain the talent.  PLEASE Help the US economy to be STRONG again by keeping the jobs among Americans and not outsourcing to foreign countries.
pros: Prestigious worldwide organization. Great people to work with.  Competitive compensation and benefits for their employees.
cons: Bad work life balance in some areas of the company.  Closing positions in the US and replacing them by outsourcing overseas to cut cost. It is very challenging for contractors to be "considered and hired" as a JPMorgan employee due to the constant layoffs and downsizing.

advice: You should respect and hold on to those that built your foundation and not follow Peter's Principle. Old School. Seasoned employees have the knowledge who can communicate and respect and know what it is like live the values and mission statement of a corporation. That cannot be learned from a book.
pros: Benefits, collaborative employee engagement, social events.
cons: Very difficult with constant management change and seeing thousands of your co-workers and business partners downsized after spending their entire career there after 30 yrs. Heartbreaking people just became a number and everyone was just working for a paycheck. Bringing in all the new young grads to take the seasoned employee's positions for less than half the salary knowing they will job jump and not be dedicated and use JPM as a stepping stone to their career.

advice: I have a great manager, and a great team.  Keep up the great work!
pros: Coworkers fell like family members, great benefits, especially for part time tellers.  Love that they match up to 5% in 401K.
cons: Would like to see more 30 hour tellers, not asking for much.  Base pay now is $12, which isn't the greatest but better than other places to work.  Wish that they would ask us the tellers questions prior to rolling out policies like no cash payments/deposits if not the signer on the account.  I'm tired of getting yelled/swore at for something that I didn't impose.  Understand the reason, but would have liked a little more information.

advice: Explore new management styles to motivate those people who are not motivated solely by money.  Happy employees are good employees.
pros: The vacation policy is generous with 4 weeks after just 5 years in addition to sick and personal time.  They pay for university and match your contributions to your 401K. Enormous company with potential of room for growth.
cons: Layoffs are common due to offshoring, moving departments and automation though they do try to reassign you even if it's only temporary. The company does not care about its employees as evidenced by the constant layoffs, mediocre bonuses and meager raises to good employees.  I despise the company, but I have too much going on in my life right now to begin a new career.

advice: Treat people well and they will want to do well for you.
pros: Good, affordable benefits, great 401K match, extremely generous PTO package,work/life balance, good initial salary offer
cons: Very large company and has lost sight of the importance of the worker bee, poor raises and bonuses (average 1% raise/yr) Evaluations for promotions and increases  are done by panel of tower management. If you are not known or favored by a member of the panel, you will not be promoted or receive an adequate increase, no matter how hard your immediate manager fights. You cannot jump levels. You must move up one level at a time

pros: Decent benefits, people on the immediate teams within the DCE structure are very supportive of one another but the company as a whole isn't set up to ship strong products. Really liked the people I worked with during my time there.
cons: It's a bank.... it also feels impossible to actually make an impact on a process or change something about a project. You spend a lot less time actually doing design work than you do navigating the bureaucracy. Career growth is tempered by HR processes, regardless of how well you perform, you are mandated to wait at least 2 years before any kind of promotion which isn't the most motivating structure.

summary: Find something else more meaningful unless you enjoy Call center Jobs
advice: Too many to even bother writing down because management says it listens to their employees but do whatever they want. So call employees have a say is just an illusion
pros: benefits such medical, dental, 401k matching up to 5%, vested after 3 years, cafeteria (depending on your location) is pretty decent
cons: Having to deal with agitated customers, policies that doesn't really benefit the customers at all (still wonder why people bank here), too many back to back calls, micromanaged to the very last detail and no sort of help from management when it comes to people suffering with mental health. If you want to move up, be prepared to be kissing some butts and say yes ma'am yes sir all the time. I'm not into that corporate lingo. And may I add that they base your performance on what they call a scorecard that summarizes your monthly goals either that you met or failed at

summary: Code of Conduct is not honored
advice: When numerous employees report verbal and psychological abuse from their direct manager, don't tell the employee to "work it out" or "discuss it directly" with the abusive person. Instead, follow the firm's so-called Code of Conduct, by taking swift and appropriate action up to and including HR involvement.
pros: Large corporation with lots of low-profile cubes to sit in
cons: Little to no opportunity for advancement, with exception to management's fraternity-like mentality. No training whatsoever, outside of mandatory CBT to satisfy corp liability. Abusive management (verbal and psychological attacks against employees AND clients) is permitted to persist, despite employees and clients reporting such behavior to senior management.

advice: Continue to focus on the development of your employees, hone in on their specialties/skills and provide them with opportunities where they can use them.
pros: I had one of my best work experiences in the JPMC offices in the Philippines. I appreciate that this company embraces diversity, making the workplace vibrant with culture. You can see some people are very passionate about working for JPMC because of the people they work with. It's easy to say that if you like the people you work with, it makes work seem a lot less like work.
cons: Job advancement is quite slow. You'll learn that you need to work smart if you want to move up, sometimes working hard does not get you the recognition you deserve.

summary: High performers should not want to leave
advice: If you have to pay new hires more money and you have to train them, why not give your current employees a raise greater than inflation before they leave? At least consider giving a true increase to your high performers.
pros: If you want to move around, there is ample opportunity to find new roles throughout the company.  You can find interesting projects and build experience by trying out new gigs. People are friendly, helpful, and senior management is accessible.
cons: Many employees are tired of waiting years for a salary increase, getting shuffled around due to org changes, and so much red tape that makes it impossible to get anything done. Many people are leaving.

advice: All good ideas do not always come from Management.  Take the time to listen to your employees they may actually offer some good ideas.  When you have employees running out of your department you should be concerned.
pros: Pay for performance.  Mentorship promoted.  Ease of mobility within different areas.
cons: Absolutely no work life balance.  You will be stretched until every ounce of you is depleted and then you will be viewed as not productive if you dare take a day off or lunch break.  After 18 months you can post for other positions but be ready to move laterally.  Sr. Management reacts instead of working with employees and be more proactive.

advice: If you value your high performing employees, treat them in a way that shows this.
pros: JPMC is a historically impressive company and a name everyone recognizes. There are enormous opportunities for growth and development within the company. It is a great place to start a career and with enough work you truly can make whatever you want of it once you're in. The face pace can be exciting and we have some excellent leaders within top levels of the company.
cons: The company places little to no focus on valuing its employees, most are just seen as replaceable pegs in holes. Work life balance is something that senior leaders love to talk about but is rarely actually supported. It's all about getting to the top and being the best, running over whoever you need to in the process.

advice: Please get rid of this internship program as it has no value to the students from the University of Delaware (except the name on your resume).
pros:
Money, as a part time worker the money was the only reason you work in Newark Delaware doing Operations.
Other departments actually look interesting and not completely full of derelicts.
cons:
Everything, you may think this dramatic but it literally was the worst internship experience you could ever ask for. They take away your human instincts by forcing you to work on holidays as an intern (Christmas eve, pre-Thanksgiving, post-Thanksgiving, New Years eve, ect and not caring about your current educational status. Specifically, the management is full of incompetent individuals that prey on weak minded micro-manageable individuals. 
Finally, It was amazing to see that college students were being trained by only individuals without college degrees in a company that thrives on "leading the market".
**If you like felling like a prisoner everyday and having someone breathing over your shoulder every day about your performance numbers, this is the place for you....**

pros: The pros are good benefits and great salary.We have very good co works, we are like a big family, Helping each other is the only way you will survive at Chase . Very good people .
cons: The Cons are the job is extremely stressful,everything you do is very tedious,you have errors for little things that don't affect the decision of the file.Some of the management are very lazy ,but you do have those that will help. You have to be quick .Chase doesn't play about quality and quantity.They will let you go in a heartbeat.I see so many people come in and leave out.No one is safe ,everyday we feel like our jobs are on the line which is  not a good thing.

summary: Great company, but be ready to work hard
advice: Focus more on making sure that adequate training is provided to managers. Just because individuals have deep subject matter knowledge, they may not be the best manager.
pros: Great visibility for career advancement, if you want it. Good training and mentorship is available, if the right mentors ad managers are found. Fast paced work environment with a lot of driven people. Open debate and discussion of ideas is appreciated. Hard work and long hours are the norm and expected, but there is respect for personal time off when communicated to management.
cons: Managers can be hit or miss, either very good or very bad. Because the company prides itself on being very agile and responsive, deadlines for projects and implementations can be extremely intense and sometimes unreasonable.

summary: Underpaid, overworked and 2/2 in layoffs per year
advice: Put down the glass and stop aspiring to be middle class.
pros: If willing to accept subpar pay and unprofessional HR experience you may enjoy 401k matching after a year, and slightly expensive benefits for the few years you make it through entire department shutdowns
cons:
Recruiters have no self respect, no room for negotiation and know just as much about their job as they do yours. Goldbricks, rude, and barely competent enough to read a script and paste an email, HR should be your first red flag.
If you are able to interview on site and have a look, do it. It's one thing to be screened by minimum wage thinkers, but to endure daily unprofessionalism across the firm is probably what sets this place apart from real Fortune companies.
A harder look at the Logo could explain the mentality of management and ruthless world you are about play a part in.

jobTitle: Assistant Vice President - QA Analyst III
advice: Stop taking away things that motivate employees, offer more flexible works hours and being able to work from home(I get a laptop but I can't work from home during business hours), take a small percentage of the billions of dollars in net profit and give back to the people that got you there.
pros: Great benefits, large company, 4 weeks vacation, a lot of job openings and opportunities for advancement.
cons: Long hours (once you go salary they don’t care how many hours you are here every day), for a company that makes as much money as JPMC does they have taken away everything that motivates their employees, little to no bonuses, no ability to work from home, no clue how some of the upper management got the positions they are in currently.

advice: Pay more attention to the relationships the FA makes, rather than making assumptions about the clients. Support in times of personal trauma is a great consideration. You are going backwards in terms of service.  Everything is moving toward self-service as the more tech savvy boomers become your main focus.  You will lose those people to firms who have Advisors that still write thank you notes and make birthday calls.
pros: Benefits are good. Working Saturdays until 2:00 and evenings until 6:30 is totally awesome!.
cons: VERY high partner turnover. The firm encourages higher priced recommendations, rather than what is in the best interest of the client at all times. My Compliance Manager reversed some of my trades in a low-cost fund family and put the clients in JP Morgan funds while I was on vacation, although the clients distinctly said they wanted to save on internal fees.  Clients called me very concerned that this Manager had contacted them in light of the length of time and decision input by the client.

advice: Do some UX work on your own systems!
pros:
Everyone in the Digital Consumer Experience department was great: kind, talented, supportive, interesting, etc. Almost everyone really cared about creating good products.

Great work/life balance, with an emphasis on life.
cons: Lots of bureaucracy, lots of technical issues with the equipment and getting things authorized. As a contractor, I filled in three timesheets (two for Chase, one of which was named Clarity. It must have been named ironically because it was one of the most frustrating interfaces I've ever encountered). Politics and the size of the organization meant some decisions filtered down to us with little to no explanation of their rationale. Also, salaries offered were significantly lower than salaries in tech in San Francisco in general.

summary: Good for the Resume, but that's about it!
advice: More should be done other than lip-service to help mid-level women advance to senior positions in the Fixed Income Dept of IB.  Each sub-dept managers should be evaluated for what they are doing to increase inclusion and value of diversity.  Parts of the group are a complete frat house!
pros: Good for the resume as the largest US national bank.
cons: If you are a senior woman in an income-producing role in the fixed income dept, good luck making it past Vice President.  Senior women in non-admin/revenue driven roles are almost non-existent (limited to a few tokens), which was very depressing and crippled morale among many women.  Horrible for working mothers.  Team environment is almost non-existent too.

summary: Great Company but hard to leave your Line of Business
advice: Make job movement more fluid by considering applicants from other lines of business.
pros:
Pay was ok
Benefits Great
My location had a drop in daycare
cons: Really hard to move out of the Line of Business where you started.  If you start in Mortgage expect to stay in mortgage for years to come or until you get some specialized training for another LOB.  The raises each year are laughable, even if you receive an exceed on your review every year.  I was also asked in an interview whether I thought I could handle the position because I had children! No one would have ever asked a man the same question!

advice: Keep doing what you're doing and like Jamie once said, some people may move up just because they know someone, but eventually the people that bust their chops are the ones that get noticed.
pros: I loved the benefits. They did a lot of coaching which was awesome because it shows you what you can improve on. Hours were good. Best EAP program I've ever had to deal with. I used them for legal services, medical, and financial services. Overall a great company. Oh and employee stock was a plus.
cons: Sometimes it feels like your the little guy in a big company. Long way up to the top. Depending on what type of manager you get, it can go good or bad.

summary: Learned a ton, would like more internal opportunities
advice: Listen to the desires of your top performers.
pros: Professional development, networking, and a fairly friendly environment. Great place to join if you are at one of two stages in your career. If you are just starting your career & want to learn valuable skills, join. If you are over the mid-level manager manager hump (you are at the executive level), join and run team filled with very smart people.
cons: Mobility is unnecessarily difficult, office politics can become annoying. Sometimes too much value is placed on who you know and appearances instead of doing a great job. If you are joining from anywhere in between the 2 career stages I mentioned in the "Pros" section, think twice… It may be tough to move up the ladder.

summary: Great place to work, fantastic benefits package including monthly, quarterly and annual bonuses.
advice: Keep the flexibility you offer the employees of something comes up.  All managers I have had have helped make changes in schedules if something comes up.
pros: Stock options, pension, 401k and healthcare are great.  Depending on your manager, they enable you to learn multiple things to make your life easier when having clients in front of you meaning you do not have to tell them to see someone else within the bank.
cons: Some days you work 8-6:30 and Saturdays are 8:30-2:30.  Makes it difficult if you have kids to have family time on many nights of the week including dinner before 8pm.

advice: I have offered many constructive criticisms in the yearly employee polls.  At no time were any of these addressed or acknowledged.  Why both with those polls if there is no real interest in listening to your employees concerns and insights?
pros: Great benefits, ample vacation time, sick time and holidays.
cons:
The management tends to be 'micro-managers' and do not understand the concept of how an exempt employee situation works.

The only way to get a raise is to move from one department to another and that's no guarantee.

The company will hire someone from outside at a higher pay than someone working they way up within the organization.

The company is moving most operations to two central locations in the DFW area in the fall of 2017.  This is creating horrible commuting situations for many people and is causing many to leave the company.

advice: Do more to protect your employees in the branches. With not wanting to hire for appropriate staffing, you force the branch employees to be without team support or a manager. As a women who basically ran a branch for herself for almost a year (for free), it is not safe and you know that.
pros: Good benefits, PTO, quality training & user-friendly resources.
cons: Difficult customers who will verbally abuse you and threaten you. Management and security do not seem to care unless you are being robbed. I've seen a grown man threaten to punch a young girl in the face and nothing was done to the man and the young girl quit to work from home at another bank.

summary: Job interviewed and hired for was not what it was in reality.  Management very impersonal and just part of a huge machin
advice: Put leaders in place that appreciate employees' achievements and contribution to the Team's success. There seems to be a pervasive atmosphere of "Big Brother" is watching your every move and squelching employees' individuality. CHASE seems to want to have their employees all be alike and does not recognize individuals for giving superior client service either verbally or financially.
pros: Good Benefits, Clean and Secure Working Environment
cons: Mgmt did not make employee feel valued as a member of the team. Probably because the team had been together for years and did not want a new member to compete with to reach sales goals. Overall, the worst employer and environment in my career

summary: Difficult Environment, but Management tries to make the best of it
advice: Keep going.  The effort provided to constantly improve the environment for the employees is appreciated
pros: Benefits are fantastic.  I would complain about the healthcare, but I suspect across the US everyone's healthcare costs continue to rise. Management is engaged to provide the best employee experience.  There is ample training available to everyone.  Rewards go to those that demonstrate hard work, innovation, cost reduction--type thinking and doing.
cons: Regulatory environment prevents associates from being free to quickly react to change.  Being the largest bank by assets in the US makes JP Morgan a prime target for cyber attacks which results in more work for all associates to secure the computer environment.

advice: Focus on employee development in terms of skills and career-path rather than tons of projects every week to cover your a**es that proved to be useless in the end.
pros: Very good benefits. Addition of work from home was great to help boost the work/life balance dilemma. Knowledgeable coworkers and managers for the most part.
cons: Absolute terrible paths to advance into new roles. Upper management and VP's want people to kiss their a** and that environment is toxic. The North Dallas location off of Spring Valley is being all moved to Boston by the end of 2015. At least they gave a decent amount of time for current employees to look for jobs if you didn't want to move to Beantown with the same pay and no cost of living adjustment.

advice: Be more consistent, be fair and don't pretend to know what you do not. Let your employee know you will find out for them if you do not know the answer. Back your employee up and let them know they can trust you to do the right thing. Follow the company policies and do not make local rules
pros: Monthly Incentives are good depending on the area. Wellness and health benefits as discounts are good quality
cons: Management often lacks knowledge to actually run the branches adequately and treatment can be based on emotion. Most things are based on who you know not what you know. It is difficult to move internally and they don't give feedback after interviews.

advice: Senior managers need to stop being impressed by the immoral and unethical tactics of the local level managers. Too many people were scheming and getting away with too much but as long as the AVP got their bonus they would look the other way.
pros: Lots of potential for growth and development if you're in a large hub such as New York or Chicago. Senior Managers know what they are doing and there are amazing benefits.
cons: The worst excuse for management at the local Tampa level in OMC. They do not care about the individual employees, they care about their bonuses and how they can make themselves look good to their AVP. This company has perfected the art of laying people off so beware of that.

summary: Boundless opportunities if you know how to spot them.
advice: Do a better job spotting poor managers.  They harm the environment.
pros: There really are a lot of opportunities if you are able to spot them.  Make sure to read up on how financial institutions work before you join or early after you join and take advantage of all the available training.  Make sure you focus on a spot where things are happening and don't get lured into a dead-end spot of which there are many.  Where you sit in these huge institutions makes all the difference
cons: Very large corporation.  Risk for people to get boxed into certain roles.

advice: When bringing transfer employees, please make sure to have all systems accessibility available! It’s so discouraging to be new to the line of business and in top of it not have the proper systematic access!
pros: I’ve been an employee for 10 1/2 years and all this time have love working for it, GREAT benefits and good work mobility.
cons: Recently transfer roles and line of business which is allowing to see a different perspective and side of the company; moved from mortgage to merchant services. The downside from this move it’s the lack of smoothness of the transition system access wise. They have terminated all my access after being an employee of this company for almost 11 years and started me over as a brand new employee! Systematically speacking.

pros: Great pay, cheap health insurance, automatic 401k, vacation, sick time, and personal time given at start date for most departments, lots of resources for work and personal needs, yearly raises.
cons: Working at the bottom of the chain in a bank at a corporate office reminds you that you're not really cared about and that you are replaceable. It's all about numbers and meeting quota. It gets overwhelming. Occurrences are also annoying. The end of the year comes and you're out of time, it's a quick and the easiest way to get fired. Also, if you start in the bottom (consumer banking) then it's nearly impossible to get a great job out of consumer banking, even with a degree and already being at the bank.

advice: Stop the public floggings when things don't go well. Quit complaining that you can't fill security jobs when you don't have a program to help those interested in joining. I spent hundreds of hours upskilling and never even had the opportunity to interview. If you're going to mandate training, make it WORTH SOMETHING.
