The new job offer was not very good and I do not recommend working here if you do not already make a lot of money.

advice: Should pay their retail bank employees highest base salary amongst their peers or at least on the high end salary ranges in that geography, hire managers that truly care about helping people and employees, make employee satisfaction their #1 priority over profit; make career mobility more transparent, consistent; fair based on experience, education, ability, skills; not just today's sales performance when considering career mobility
pros: Great company for entry level
cons: For mid-career or graduate degrees working in retail banking non-management, under pay, under value; under utilize, and too much politics in career mobility

advice: Everyone gets busy, take time to come around and hear any inputs from your manager and the workers underneath who are right there dealing with the problems that would help workflow more efficiently.
pros: Depending on your manager (like every company), my department was not ran by Type A managers. The job was still done efficiently with down-to-earth managers. Senior managers were great to work with as they helped you to understand the process rather tell you to just 'do.'
cons: More 'personal' cubicle space needs to be added so workers for a sense of individual space.

pros: To use a sports metaphor, there are only a handful of financial services firms that would be considered the "The Show" and JPMorgan is definitely one of them.  Very smart colleagues, very competitive, good compensation.  There are many executives to learn from and grow.
cons: Work life balance is an after thought.  Famous quotes from managers, "there is some else right behind you if you don't want to do the hours and make the commitment";  "that's what Saturday is for, to see your family"

summary: Providing great Customer service with less '"selling"
advice: Taking timeout to coach employees. Give out positive feedback and encouragement .
pros: Vacation and sick time.401k.  Building special bonds with customers and meeting new people. Having a hour lunch to relax from the busy work day.
cons: Working 6 days a week. Not getting out of the branch until 6:30pm everyday.  working almost every Saturday. Always short staffed. Get the cold shoulder from management for not wanting to work extra hours or needing a day off for doc appt. Health care for family expensive.

advice: Become better organized, care more for your employees and acknowledge their work ethic and skills. Do not look out only for yourselves only.
pros: training, good starting point for those looking to get their foot in the door. looks good on a resume. Generally flexible if you are a student and need a part time job.
cons: no advancement opportunities. They use you for what you are worth to them, then fill you with empty promises to keep you "happy". Horrible management in my opinion and for those i worked for up till now.

summary: Good experience though lots of red tape
advice: You're facing a talent exodus in your investment banking division. You need to implement work life balance improvements or young professionals will continue to prefer buy-side or tech-sector jobs.
pros: There are a lot of institutional resources that help employees learn skills on the job. Having a global platform also gives opportunities to move around.
cons:
Work life balance is of no concern to managers
Getting things done or having systems changed is hard with so much red tape

pros: Working for J.P. Morgan wasn't as bad as I expected it to be, I was going to school at the time and they were flexible with hours and since I was pretty accurate with my typing I never got yelled at. Others were yelled at weekly for being under the accuracy mark.
cons: Production based environment where you are constantly working, not much time to talk to coworkers when you are typing the entire shift.

advice: Be honest with people and don't use them as a number and when not needed after they turned down other job offers based on your lies. Treat people how u want to be treated..
pros: I like the fact that you have teams that work well together and build relationships amongst yourselves.
cons: If you are a contractor, they will lie and tell you that they will hire you by the end of your contract. May end your contract before the actual end date and leave you hanging...

advice: Pay attention to the truly devoted workers, instead of those that look busy only when you're looking. Truly reward them financially, or with work/life balance. Not pointless annual publishings about the company they work for.
pros: Great family feel with regard to direct reports. I enjoyed coming to work for those faces daily. That's is what I miss most
cons: The company could learn to pay and compensate better for the employees that work themselves tirelessly instead of rewarding those who wear the right designer labels, and know somebody that knows somebody.

summary: Too much Stress not enough Salary
advice: Pay attention to the amount of people that voluntarily leave a team. when no one has been there for longer than 2 years that is a very bad sign.
pros: code of conduct strictly enforced, very open about all cultures and backgrounds
cons: The company is so big that it is run like the military. When you work for a "drill sergeant bully" manager, there's not a lot you can do about it but look for something different. There are a LOT of drill sergeant bully bosses.

summary: Client Service Associate JPMorgan Private Bank
advice: Better training and more experience is needed for the front office as well as client service associates in order to successfully serve clients.
pros: Very challenging, great clients, great people to work with. Company provides good benefits. Private Bank is growing very fast so there is a lot of opportunity to add to development.
cons: Structure of JPMorgan Private Bank is not designed to support service role so we did not have the resources we needed to do our job which put a lot of us at risk.

advice: Put more thought into LOB placement by having people rank their preferences or something of the like. Also, don't make the events mandatory, as some people are commuting from far away and had to arrive an hour or more earlier to attend.
pros: During the summer there are quite a few intern events including a speaker series with the company's leaders and social outings.
cons: The placement for the summer is completely random, and your experience is really based on which line of business you are in.

pros: Overtime is available and the people you'll work with on a day-to-day basis honestly want the best for you.
cons: The program kind of fell apart and left a lot of analysts in jobs that they didn't get to choose in the first place. Basically managers picked your resume out of a hat and decided what team you were placed on. The HR representatives that hired you in the first place are not helpful and trap you into the role until you stick it out throughout the two year program or gain the strength to quit.

summary: Large Financial Services Firm with significant opportunities for movement
advice: Your salary and promotion practices encourage  associates and vice presidents to leave after several years and return to promotions and salary adjustments to the market.
pros: The size of the organization allows you to change jobs every few years to gain broad experience.  The company encourages movement especially at the officer levels.
cons: It is difficult to affect real change in such a large organization.  Some of the senior managers have not adapted to current trends in employment such as flexible work arrangements and remote work arrangements.

advice: Continue creating opportunities for new employees.  Train (give feedback, perhaps even only once or twice a year) to managers/bankers about how to best utilize/train their subordinates.  Will be a win/win as subordinates and superiors experience better working relationships and improved deliverables leading to better business outcomes.
pros: Broad experience across many facets of wealth management. No matter what we do in life, we are selling something. There are many talented salespeople within the JPM organization.
cons: Can be a political environment. Some bankers/managers care very little about their subordinates while "managing up" with significantly different behaviors.

advice: At the risk of sounding salty... none. Well-intentioned feedback was routinely ignored/never addressed. Even in rare instances when it was solicited.
pros: Pay is good. 4 weeks vacation.
cons: Bureaucracy slows down all. A revolving door of management only exacerbates this. Competing initiatives and silos between business divisions create staggering inefficiencies, spinning, and wasted resources. Management ignores employee emails and frequently ignores best practices and strategic advice. No KPIs. No talent development, only importing from outside... so no employee growth except through soft skill. Soft skill has its own value... but is often the culprit for chaos when heavily weighted higher up in companies. The culture is unfortunately stale, bc everyone is confused and frustrated. And it doesn't help when cronyism has brought grown people to tears in the office.

summary: Awesome program to be involved with
pros: This rotational program allows you to see many different parts of the firm. Great way to start your network and the program gives many opportunities to get more involved and grow. Also overtime opportunity for many of the roles but in my roles it was never required
cons: You don't get to choose your first role and the roles after you can preference but there's no guarantee that you'll get your first choice. Most analysts are happy with the roles they've been placed in and it's only 8 months per role.

advice: I have a great team and a great manager. We've actually worked together at previous Banks and it was really great that we all ended up getting hired on at Chase.
pros: Great benefits! Great people! Chase is a company that actually stands by their values. Not only do they provide exceptional service to the customers but they take care of their employees as well.
cons: Honestly I don't have any at this time. I'm new to the company so I could be speaking too soon but I have nothing to complain about.

summary: Great firm, but don't stay long.
pros: Great brand and good people
cons: I think compensation is terrible for people who wants to build a career. Ive been with the firm for 6 years and tried to work my way up. Depending on the organization you work for there's a quota system where there can only be "x" amount of associate / VP etc. Which makes it hard to move up. Annual raise are average 3% YoY so you might be better to leave after 2 years for better compensation at least in the middle to back office type roles.

pros: I really enjoyed my time at Chase Bank as Part time teller. We were given plenty of training, a clothing amount to pick out our own shirts, and before I had to quit to move out of state we got a great pay bump. Paid days off were nice as well if you get sick.
cons:
Customers aren't as nice as I thought they'd be when you're there to help them. 
Having to change my password CONSTANLY to something I've never used and having to remember it haha.
I HATED having to write my own annual review!

advice: Don't make it so difficult for branch employees to enjoy their time outside of the office.  Morale would improve if our time was also respected.
pros:
- Affordable benefits
- PTO
- Stock purchase option
- Networking
cons: - PTO highly questionable. Must compete w/ coworkers in completely different job families. If a teller has requested time off at the same time as a relationship banker, the manager has to choose whose time to approve based on basically nothing. These employees have different job duties. It sometimes feel like they get to decide when you use the time you've earned.

summary: Hard to get compensated fairly internally
advice: Listen more to your employees, run new metrics in terms of compensation against the current market similar to how their competitor Capital One does, and retention of talent will go up.
pros: Job security is very good at the firm, some much so that senior developers can get away with doing minimum effort.
cons: As an employee of the company, most of the time effort is not adequately compensated, they value more external hires and pay them close to what the market demands given negotiations, it is not the same for internal progression

summary: great experience with a global company for it tech minded people
advice: Try to balance everyones homelige and work, and not always about the stockholders. I am all for customer first, but think of your people sometimes.
pros: Diversity with all types of people and lifecycle testing and product techniques both in the mainframe and distributed areas. level playing field for promotions and a very good timeoff policy trying to balance work and homelife;
cons: Working with a global company means at times taking meetings in the middle of the nite,,,, LOL.

advice: Be honest about changes that will happen to the company
pros: I worked for JP Morgan for 5 1/2 years and had a really great time working for the company. I like the people I worked with best because everyone was like family to each other. They also provide training often to make sure everyone is at par witb company policies and procedures.
cons: The not so good part was that we had to be transferred to another process/department because my account has been dissolved

advice: Pay attention to the talent pool.
pros: career opportunity is excellent. Due to the vastness of the company it is easy to move to a different every few years which keeps things fresh without having to re-invent the wheel. Had some of the best leadership that supported the employees by keeping them honest.
cons: In-efficiencies, work life balance is a just a wishy washy statement but not adhered to. Had also encountered huge gaps in ownership within management and quality of management. Found some of the best and worst in management.

summary: Very production oriented with very little incentive for the supervisors.
advice: Change the treatment of your front line supervisors. They like recognition too and desire some kind of incentive.
pros: It's a very clean and secure place to work. Company does care about input from employees and tries to make it a good place for the employees to work.
cons: Company is all about the developing of employees but lacks any kind of incentives for the ones they want to drive this type of culture, the supervisors. Low pay for what is expected.

advice: create options for employees to move within the company. don't lock them into a position for one year.
pros:
Great pay
hours
vacation time
benefits
work life balance
cons: I honestly loved working for chase until they closed my branch. The new branch I was placed in made it obvious that they didn't want me there. There is to much pressure from the partners to pitch chase private client. If your sales style doesn't match with the branch you are placed at you are stuck there. Unfortunately, there is almost no moveability between branches

advice: Hire people who are actually good people instead of focusing solely on credentials
pros: Top firm which makes it easy to get a job after
cons: Very bad culture at the firm. My managers were extremely disrespectful to the analysts. I could not even step away from the desk for 10 minutes without fear. The people I worked for did not care about my growth at all. I did not learn any useful job skills during my time there. Although the role made it easy to get other jobs after I don't think it was worth the stress and anxiety I experienced working there. The grad training program is very difficult with challenging exams once or twice a week.

advice: Recent emphasis to measure and improve employee satisfaction was articulated with positive actions and not just merely words. This initiative has had a measurable impact on overall morale.
pros: A great place to gain broad experience in residential real estate. Nationwide exposure and the opportunity to network with internal and external professionals. Actively promotes work life balance. Top notch benefits package.
cons: Due to the size of this organization, process changes to improve efficiencies require an extended timeline. Recent decision to severely restrict remote workers was disappointing.

summary: Not a Good Career Decision for Software Engineers
advice: Need new management, problem starts from the top down.
pros:
Good Health and 401k Benefits
Decent time off
cons:
Old technology.
Politics, extreme posturing, people wasting your time and showboating so they can get ahead.
Recruiters lie about how much of a bonus you get.
Not a good move for young technologists, don't learn much. They just want you for the young people numbers.
Houston building is terrible, maybe other locations are better. Dim and depressing.
Working from home strongly discouraged.

summary: Good job for young person or someone near retirement
advice: Listen to employee suggestions. Allow employees to work independently and treat employees with respect.
pros: Good benefits and opportunities for charitable organization involvement
cons: Treated like a number, no individuality is wanted or respected. Payscale is lower then the national average in most positions and when trying to advance to the another role, often times the level is changed so no pay increase is given. Terrible experience, do not recommend this company to work for, too big with no feelings or respect for individuals.

advice: stop micro managing.  raise salaries..give raises annually.
pros: No product minimum sales required.  Make commision off of any combo of products.   Not forced to fill buckets.
cons: Extremely low base salary.  Capped commisions.   MICRO-MANAGED.  Over worked and under staffed.  Not Appreciated.  Scrutinized for everything.  Will make you hate being a banker.  NO RAISES.  Raises dont exist.  I haven't gotten a raise in 6 years.

advice: Spend more time with employees or even passing by and saying hi can make a huge difference on a telephone banker as days can get very lonely isolated away on the phones.
pros: Great benefits and pay. the culture that the sky is the limit was actually very inspiring.
cons: The calls in the bilingual brackets were overwhelming. Customers can be very vocal and would say anything to hurt your feelings; if you have thin skin or are an emotional person this can get to you.

advice: Continue to value and appreciate staff.  Provide more avenues for development and advancement.   During transition of center functions take the time to analyze staff and their abilities and qualifications before placing them in a position, otherwise you are setting up good employees to fail.
pros: Great staff, support, training, and HR department.  Benefits and compensation are very competitive.
cons: Annual review process is unorganized and unsystematic.  No actual formalized process and rushed.

summary: Good work life balance, but often not enough drive to excel among colleagues
advice:
Incentivize senior VPs

Higher standards for UX/design/content
pros:
Good work life balance
Good opportunities to switch careers
Ability to work on products that have massive scale
cons:
Difficult to own your own outcomes/KPIs. There are some talented VPs , but we often do the bulk of the strategic and tactical work and the credit goes to Executive Directors. The culture needs to be more outcomes oriented and less political.

Senior leadership on the digital team needs to provide a cohesive strategy and vision.

summary: The hands on training is good at first but goes away rather quickly.
advice: Ask for a shorter commitment off the back the large number of years. Preach development and guide younger employees in new directions.
pros: Good base salary to start with the opportunity to network and find different areas of interest within the bank. The issue is getting out of your roll is very difficult.
cons: Transitioning to a new roll or department is frowned upon unless you finish your overly long "verbal commitment". Managers tend to block your moves internally.

summary: Not all that glitters is gold....
advice: Don’t make employees participate in diversity book clubs when JPM has a well- documented history of predatory lending in minority communities. Hypocritical!
pros: Firm won’t ever go out of business or need a bailout, decent healthcare benefits
cons: Highly toxic culture, many employees are lifelong JPMers and blindly follow the cult (referring to the CEO by first name as if they know him, etc), under market pay compared to other bulge bracket banks. It cannot be overstated how rotten the culture is at this place.

advice: If you don't pay competitively, start giving actual benefits/incentives, let people work from home, relax your completely archaic dress-code requirements... you will lose many people.
pros: VERY good health care benefits. Usually flexible schedules. Liberal ideologies (if you're into that)
cons: Raises, Promotions are very difficult and rarely given out. Appreciation, bonuses, and other perks (besides healthcare) are rare or non-existent. Archaic thinking in regards to uniforms, in-office mandates when the job can be done at home, very cliquey and without butt-kissing you won't get anywhere.

advice: Ask for help, don't try to be a hero. Help your employees with every ounce of energy you have.  Don't celebrate other's failures.
pros: Vacation time was terrific!  You learn a lot working at JPM. You learn how to deal with red tape, layoffs, learning how to stretch your paycheck, how to deal with difficult people, how not to manage people and know that not everyone is treated equally. Working there teaches you a different life lesson everyday.
cons: People stay there so long because they get comfortable.

advice: Talk to your employees and directly ask them what their concerns are and what they would like to see moving forward. Communication solves everything but you also have to be willing to listen.
pros: Overall lots of opportunities for growth.
cons: You can get lucky and have a great team as well as a manager or your manager can be tough to work with but, you can always tell during the interview whether or not this would be a person you want to work with long term.

advice: Stop understaffing! It is obvious that your company has enough resources to treat your people properly and staff branches enough to be functional.
pros: 20 hour tellers get full benefits (medical, vision, dental, PTO, and sick time.) They hire diverse people, and there is room to move up.
cons: All branches are understaffed. I work at a branch in a small town that has 5 employees running the entire branch. Days where someone calls out sick, employees don't get proper breaks, which is disappointing for such a large company.

pros: could learn a lot about global finance infrastructure and policies. great mobility opportunities, great work life balance, very collaborative. the risk management culture and "fortress balance sheet " mindset is very real across the firm.
cons: big company and too much separation of duties across team as a result you lack visibility to many different element impacting your business and full understanding of the desk strategy. Low pay as management still want to rely on the company name and reputation as incentive instead of matching industry average.

summary: Good place to work until you can get to a better company.
pros: Some nice people, very nice cafeteria, nice amenities. Looks good on your resume if you can stay there for a couple of years since everyone seems to understand how bad it can be.
cons: Stressful, management is not supportive, focus is on form over content, how you say something is more important than what you are saying, perception IS everything, lots of back stabbing. There is always a law suit in progress so makes you wonder about the overall integrity of this bank.

advice: break it up and spin off businesses to creat value exec management is probably most competent of all big money center banks the firm is too big to be nimble
pros:
great people to work with , challenging and family needs are understandably accommodated especially with young children and a single parent 
but upward mobility seems tough and org changes cripple divisions for a time period
cons: health care costs are high, benefits are ok but not very competitive. a few people make the concentrated wealth but I guess it's the same in other companies

pros: Being a teller. One of the easiest financial jobs there is. JP Morgan & Chase's three day training classes repeatedly pounds the basics into new hires heads. Everyone is friendly, and the perks a admirable.
cons: Very strict on their hours. If you sign up to work 32 hours, you will work 32 hours one way or another. If you're taking time off without Vacation, they like to pack your hours to accommodate your time off. While this isn't explicitly a con, it is a downside when you're a full time student as well.

summary: Good company depending on the department
advice: Train first line managers to be true people managers.   My managers are usually forced into spending all their time jumping through the hoops that their managers impose.
pros: Good benefits and competitive salary.   Good citizen on the world.
cons: If you are in certain department or locations, there can be a lot of job insecurity.   The company has a lot of talk about job opportunities but does not put an emphasis on finding talent or developing skills that may be transferable to new positions

summary: There's lots to do at JPM
advice: Stop participating in this race to the bottom. Do you want to be the Walmart of financial services?
pros: There's many different opportunities. It's easy to move up since there is so much turnover. Generally the people who work here are a step above those at other financial services companies I've worked for.
cons: Raises and bonuses are terrible. They don't care how many hours you put in so long as you aren't paid hourly, the product is still acceptable and the client is still paying.

summary: Great company to make it a long term career.
advice: Don't expect employees to be perfect or robots.
pros: Chase has awesome benefits when it comes to health, paid time off and maternity leave. Definitely made it easier for me when I had my kids. Back up child care was a big help.
cons: I've been with the company over 15 years so after being there over 5 years it became harder to earn a decent pay raise. There has been a few years where I didn't get a pay raise because I am considered caped out.

advice:
If you want to be a tech company- you need to have tech that works for your employees.

If you want to be modern , attract & retain talent, and be innovative - you need to strip down the bureaucracy and empower your staff across all levels
pros:
-great brand
-opportunity to work with some really great and really smart people
-depending on the team, can craft your own work/life balance
-encourage internal mobility
cons:
-so bureaucratic. Driven by procedures and processes rather than practicality and rationality
-minimal perks. no firm holiday party. minimal, if any budget for team events.
-slow moving

advice: Assist with having your well educated employees advance. Nothing sucks more than being at a dead end job.
pros: The benefits are great. The team I work with are social-able.
cons: No room for growth. Even if you have a degree in work in auto, I have been told by not only HR, but from other departments it is hard to move around. I was advised by current and former in employees in order to see an increase I would have to leave and reapply for a position I would be qualified for.

summary: Do your research to find where you can thrive
advice: Racial bias in some organizations is unchecked. Do not allow known transgressors to move to new roles before demonstrating behavior change and without taking corrective action.
pros: Firm size and global footprint lends to abundance of mobility opportunities and the benefits are good. Significant investments to improve racial inequality within the firm and the communities it serves are going to move the needle.
cons: Size of firm allows bad managers to move around and maintain good reputation while taking bad management practices to other parts of the firm.

advice: Only current benefit of this role is the job experience it provides. If you want to find better talent then start creating career path opportunities, right now this role is a dead end job, and the longer you stay in it the more it hurts your career. Job is looked down upon within the organization.
pros: Job experience, exposure to ultra high net worth banking.
cons:
Low pay
Long hours 
Stressful work, with tight deadlines and high pressure
Lack of partnership with front office
Treated like assistants, and generally looked down upon within the organization.

advice: With the focus on cost savings, make sure to reward your top performers in order to ensure you don't loose them when the economy turns
pros: One of the best, if not the best, financial institution in the world today.  Size of the organization enables each employee to own their own career development and growth.  Each area of the bank is its own small corporation.  Enabling employees to move into a different tower and experience a new professional culture.
cons: Large organization that moves slowly due to the oversight necessary at times.

advice: Recognize employee capacity, cutting budget without cutting workload will only take you so far.  Having seen the large project failures over the past few years it's surprising to see that this behavior continues.
pros: Challenging, fast paced, Chaoctic IT environment that consistantly challenges you to be invovative to be successful.  Occasional solid partnering with other departments.
cons: Lack of Sr Leadership, priority decitsicions are pushed to lower level managment rather than making the difficult decisions of what projects to cut.  End result is failed projects and significant overtime by lower level employees

advice: Listen to feedback just as well as you give it. Organize more outside of work activities for the firm to give employees and management a chance to bond.
pros: Compensation was great. The diversity of the firm exposed me to alot of different people and ways of thinking which was excellent. I was given a large amount of responsibility from early on. My manager and team were friendly and very easy to get along with.
cons: Overtime was often required. Technology is a bit outdated. You are often the scapegoat and blamed when something goes wrong

advice:
The biggest challenge is figuring out how to navigate through the functional and bureaucratic channels of the organization even to get the most petty jobs done - that needs to be change absolutely and swiftly before it becomes another gse!
The favoritism towards revenue generating businesses is visible and incremental, which is detrimental for the intrinsic growth of the company!
pros: Internal mobility is real and not a myth
cons:
HR sucks
Very hierarchical 
Career development is only offered if you are a from revenue contributing line of business/department otherwise no body really cares

jobTitle: Home Equity Payoff Processor/Invoice Processing Analyst
summary: I learned so much from the departments I worked in and will carry that knowledge with me in my future career choice.
pros: great opportunity to cross train in other jobs within your current department or the ability to transfer to another department, good benefits, some offices offer daycare for the new mother to return to work quicker
cons: I can't think of anything that I really disliked with the company for me to list as cons.  Everyone's opinions are going to vary, but I can say that I really enjoyed working for the company.

advice: There should be more focus on diversity within the company in upper level management positions.
pros: This company has a strong sense of direction, with exceptional benefits, and amazing technology. Great place to learn the ropes of how to run a efficient business and it has tons of growth opportunities.
cons: Very poor work life balance, extreme goals, and aggressive tactics. Either you are the best at what you do or you are nothing at all in this company. Great work environment for a aggressive career orientated individual but this can be challenging for someone with family priorities.

summary: This company is literally a game of musical chairs, inexcusable ineptitude is rewarded with constant reorgs.
advice: You could cut staff by 50% if you eliminated people whose terrible work product actually creates work in lieu of getting things done.
pros: The money would be good for a person working 40 hours a week.  Those people are generally part of the problem.  The rest of us work 60+ to compensate for all the dead weight.
cons: Rampant unethical business practices and terrible work ethic, the lowest common denominators are moved around and promoted in lieu of managing out.

summary: Opportunity exists, but you have to fight for it.
advice: Realize who is bringing in the money to support the business unit and treat them accordingly.
pros: If you are a sharp quick learner that can become efficient, then you can make pretty good money originating mortgages... if you're in a good market.
cons: You can be placed in a crappy location with can significantly limit your opportunity. The backoffice support can be almost non-existant for non-Chase Private Client customers. The backoffice processing often can treat you like you're bothering them although their job exists because of your sales.

summary: Good company to work for and grow with
advice: Upper management in the Credit Department was a little unprofessional.  The environment was good.  The management was friendly and inviting - they made me feel like they cared about me as an employee.
pros: The work was good and easy.  I initially interviewed with them as an Analyst, but they moved me up to an Approval Officer based on my knowledge and experience.  It made me feel like they cared.  Big thumbs up!
cons: The schedule and answering the phone constantly while working.

summary: Nice company to work for, and great people.
advice: I suggest to HR to discuss with the leadership and plan the steps to introduce work life balancing work culture.
pros: Worked in IB and Card services. I came across with many good people and helped to progress well in my roles. Lot of challenges and a good place to gain a good financial domain expertise.
cons: Lot of work pressure and technology is always a bit old. But for sure JPMC is far ahead in comparison to other banking institutions.

advice: Talk to the guys in the trenches more they know a lot of stuff that is going on that are yet to reach your ears or that you would not normally get to hear.
pros:
Reward scheme is quite motivating so in pushes you to give 100%
Great mentors who you can bounce off ideas and thoughts in terms of your current task or work in general.
cons:
Long hours, hardly any time for social life.
Long meetings, hardly leaves any time for actual work
Poor management relations with junior staff

advice: Look for more better ways to have your employees find fulfillment in their current positions. Promotions should be based on body of work since an employee is hired not what was accomplished in one calendar year.
pros: Opportunity to work with intelligent individuals. Organization promotes internal mobility and offers ample opportunities to network outside of your current group.
cons: Current group has been in the middle of a relocation strategy for the past 2 years. Morale is low and compensation has been flat across the past two years.

summary: Great benefits but difficult to move laterally
advice: Find more constructive ways to help employees move laterally within company.
pros: Pay, bonuses & benefits were very good (at retail level). Most of my managers we're great people who were supportive in my career goals. Good work-life balance. Excellent PTO allocation.
cons: I found it very difficult to move out of the retail side of the bank to a position that would not in essence be taking "a step down", even with over 4 years with the company & a masters degree.

advice: Train managers how to be effective leaders for all lines of business better equipping them to make intelligent choices for the organization. Learn to listen and pay attention to employees who may have something valuable to contribute.
pros: As a whole, my experience at JP Morgan Chase was positive.
cons: A lot of "Group Think" occuring across different departments at the detriment of the company and other employees. Upper management is frequently disconected from what's really going on within the ranks.

advice: Not much. I don't think the IB culture is easily changed. Within those constraints, JPM is pretty well run.
pros: The training program is very good. Working in the analyst program at a place like JPM does look good on the resume and also helps a person build solid financial modeling and analysis skills.
cons: This is not specific to JPM, but the culture of investment banking leaves a lot to be desired. The people aren't nice, and most people are pretty stressed most of the time.

advice: Management should spread focus evenly and give attention to the Tellers as they do the personal bankers. Management should also train bankers to help tellers during times when they are busy.
pros: The biggest pro is working bank hours. I also enjoyed receiving extra money for passing mystery shops and referral incentives. The company tries to help its employees grow within the company.
cons: Tuition Reimbursement never happened. When I was hired they told me that I could get tuition reimbursement. However when I tried the process there were b.s reasons that always seemed to keep me from receiving those funds.

advice: Do not use cookie-cutter management practices and employee standards between departments. Grow employee numbers with client base.  Listen to employee and client/customer feedback and take it seriously.
pros: Excellent health care, vacation time that you are encouraged to use, pension and other financial benefits.
cons: Below industry average compensation for non-executives.  You are treated as a number, not an individual. Reactive, not proactive management and crisis resolution.  Company does not care about any clients except a select few high profile ones.

advice: Higher more qualified bankers with a finance background and BAs in finance and less bankers that do have a background in selling cars and shoes
pros: Platform opputunity to uncover outside assets and grow balance s is tremendous given the right personality and work ethic you will be successful
cons: Based on the amount of bank related tasks that are not sales specific the base salary should be much higher especially for bankers who are manager on duty and hold other titles serving as a banker with many functionality within the day to day operations

advice: Don't nit pick your employees
pros: Great Benefits including employee discounted stock, 4 weeks paid vacation plus PTO days and bank holidays, great volunteer network and opportunities to get involved in the community.
cons: Aggressive employee reviews cause unnecessary stress. Training is not that great. I basically taught myself how to do the job on the job. Thankfully I had very supportive team members who were very knowledgeable and offered some great tips I still use to this day. Unfortunately those folks didn't stick around and once management changes over I knew it was time for me to leave.

advice: Please be engaged with your employees. Micromanaging is not necessary but there should be a connection with your employees for the overall success of the team and company.
pros: There are great opportunities for advancement, benefits, collaboration with other associates, management and department, facilities and excellent time off allotment work/life balance.
cons: Some of the upper management can be hands off to point that they seem disengaged, career development should be more a focus, better forms of acknowledgement need to be implemented.

advice: The system promotes mediocrity. Bait and switch is never a good way to retain good people.
pros: Steady flow of prospects walking in if you are in the right location; assigned a 'book of business' to manage; straight forward work, great for workers who don't need to make money.
cons: Entry level roles; management claims during the hiring process advancement is swift but the goal changes often and no one can move for first 12 mos; pay is anemic; commissions are equally low; not a career company if you are looking for fast tracking or earning six figures

summary: Its a great company to work for if you willing to work for it.
advice: Some are good and some are bad but its life.
pros: Money great and the company is expecting you to do what you get paid for, and I love the people they want you to be great.
cons: The management to be was very bad since I relocated from California to Texas the management in Texas only care about there job not think if they train you to be great they would be great also.

advice: Make education a forefront of their requirements, have a more brokerage look and feel as far as investment options, cut some of the red tape, provide better incentives and higher pay for those that are highly educaated
pros: Great Global Brand Name Recognition, Vast Array of Affluent Clientele, Phenomenal Intellectual Capital from a Capital Markets and Research prospective
cons: Huge difference of Chase and JP Morgan ( like comparing Walmart to Costco), no level of education for employees at Chase, Huge Firm so a lot of Bureaucracy, Not a Huge selection of investment options for clients just mainly proprietary

summary: Big Brand - not so big on values and culture
advice: Try to practice what you preach. There is a huge disconnect between what is said in the townhalls and what is the reality on the floor. Also it doesnt help when you consistently lay people off without trying to work with them and whatever problem they have. The moral on the floors is pretty low and you need to act now.
pros:
> Good pay (not the best) but if you can negotiate and come in with a good package it will most likely be higher than what other similar sized institutions will pay.  However, there is hardly any percent yearly raise. 
> Not so bad Bonus: In Technology they don't pay as much bonus as they do for the business guys who bring in the money. Give or take 10%.
> Decent medical coverage. Not a big fan, but works.
> Lot of technology focus. Wide range of things to work on. From legacy tech to Cloud computing.
> Has a cafeteria in my location with subsidized food. Decent choices available.
> Good work life balance. Unless you are in a very specific role that requires you to take off hours calls or something, you can generally do 8-4 / 9-5 job here.
cons:
> There has been 6-7 changes in management in the last 3 years. There is no stability.
> A new lead comes in, spends a year criticizing the previous lead and planning the next big thing, and then there is a management change. He leaves (or is asked to leave) and the cycle repeats.
> No value for people. Everyone is replaceable. 
> They will talk all sweet in townhalls, but on the ground reality is different.
> Not easy for folks on work visa, waiting for GC etc,
> Lot of politics
> hard to achieve anything. People will first be non supportive of what you are trying to do, and then if you somehow still manage to do well - will finally try to steal your thunder and claim credit for the task you did.
> Incompetent people are promoted over smart ones, just on the basis of personal rapport.
> Lay off culture (for whatever reasons. Mostly personal.
> (there could be many more - I am just tired of typing)
(The above points are obviously generalized, there are good people and good projects too. Might be rare, but there are)

pros: Company has some good teams if you are lucky enough to be on one.  The TAP(now SEP) program has some stellar individuals who really go above and beyond to help those hired into the program (at least in Brooklyn).
cons: The TAP/SEP program as a whole has gone down hill since I started in 2017. A combination of what seems to be funding and effort cuts from upper management have taken the program from something I would suggest to others to something I'm very indifferent about.

advice: There's a reason successful teams/companies have gotten where they are today, and it's not by brushing issues under the rug and pretending to care about team culture. For a company that prides itself for being supportive of employee satisfaction it's extremely disappointing to discover this is not fully the case here. Care more about your team and its culture, and actually take appropriate action on negative, insulting people. This group has high aspirations - it's a shame it's being stifled by parasites and oblivious management.
pros:
- Exposure to financial markets and the operations of an index business
- Opportunity to learn the value propositions of an index business and its implications on the overall strategy for the firm
- Competitive compensation
- Great feedback from people on other teams within the firm regarding their culture, work life and motivation to be an employee.
cons:
- High turnover due to terribly negative work environment. Don't expect to get along with your coworkers; selfishness is the name of the game and all they care about is advancement.
- Local + Remote management made it very confusing in regards to performance/expectations for the role. Also made it extremely difficult to have concerns be addressed (specifically regarding the negative work environment and poor behavior of team members)
- Not much opportunity for additional learning/exposure to the business unless you are a full-time employee; expect to conduct daily/monthly tasks throughout training, and if you're not perfect afterwards don't expect anything more than that.
- Contract position ("try before you buy" seemed quite prevalent in this group in particular). This also leaves little to no room for mobility within the firm unless you become a full-time JPMC employee.
- In addition, contract position means there's no guarantee you'll have a job tomorrow. If you make too much of a big deal about this teams negative environment and team members you'll get let go without any notice. (This is what happened to me.)

pros:
Competitive pay
Ample pto
Big brand 
401k
Healthcare coverage
On site clinic
Some great coworkers
Stable company
cons:
I joined despite the warnings from friends noting that this place is a "shift" environment. I didn't know what that meant and ultimately felt it wouldn't be a big deal. I just thought it would be like any typical dba job. What they don't tell you is that this place tracks your entire activity. You have virtually no privacy. The standards are very high here and this place is highly competitive. You  are measured through a lot of dimensions such as number of tickets closed, how you closed them, what you create, how others rate you, how your manager rates you, and you have to seek feedback to essentially justify your existence. I felt my manager never had an idea what the team was doing. It didn't help that he wasn't even in the same office. There was always a disconnect. 

The workload was just highly stressful and sometimes over bearing. What I hated the most was I felt the work was very unfulfilling. You are very limited in the scope of work you do here compared to other places. A lot of people come here with a broad set of skills and essentially lose them because they don't get to use them. As you can imagine, the environment is very locked down and things, even internally, take forever to get done because there's so many approvals needed. The on call rotation here is just awful. What they don't tell you is that being on call here is basically you working a full 8 hour shift the entire weekend. You're logged in remotely and the whole activity tracking still applies because the desktop environment is completely virtual. The team is burnt out and usually leave for other internal teams as soon they are eligible. Depending on the amount of coverage, expect to lose several of your weekends.

summary: Great bank to work at, but it is a bank
advice: invest in your existing employees
pros: have had great experience working at JPM overall and really learned a lot from my coworkers
cons:
my positive experience is not consistent across the bank -- many others i know (mostly in more front-office roles) have had terrible experiences because of the senior management
JPM does not give a lot of perk and perks are not consistent across lines of business (e.g., some teams got refunds for work from home equipment, and others did not)

summary: Good for Graduates but not long term
advice: Salary raise or people will just take the brand name and leave.
pros:
Depending on team, can work from home.
Great Software Engineer program for 2 years to learn.
My manager is fantastic but horror stories for others.
Free coffee and tea.
cons:
Pay for software engineers way below average. (I know money isn't everything but they are way below average.)
Old technologies and very boring.
Looks like a bunch of old people where everyone hates their life.
Very cheap company when it comes to snacks, etc...

advice: Hire someone to lead who has a balance between people skills, leadership courage, and respect for others. Leadership by fear, intimidation, and micro-management can cause employees to think that Chase isn't a good company! It ruins the Chase brand! Also, don't make promises to several people if you have no intention of keeping your word. It creates mistrust in leadership. I'm so glad that I just accepted a different role within Chase to rebuild my core beliefs in the company that I know is great!
pros: Benefits, time off, pension, peers, FMLA policy
cons: Letting the wrong people into management.

summary: Ride the wave of constant layoff and rehire and company inconsistancy
advice: Chase IS the reason employees are disgruntled and unions were formed.  This company SCREAMS for a union due to misuse and abuse of internal policy.
pros: Decent health insurance and benefits
cons: Remove all accountability and reason and what you have left is middle management and lower/direct supervisory abuse.  Nepotism is alive and well.  Reviews are manipulated and fixed and brown nose employees are still favored over independent quality employees.

pros: Great training programs. Great cafeteria. It is nice to network within a big firm. You have a lot of opportunities to meet people outside of your group. A lot of perks and discounts for their employees. I learned a lot about excel, valuation, and serving clients.
cons: Office attire for my group was very casual. No one wore a suit on my floor. Common to have "jean days" before 3 day weekends. Pro or Con depending on how yo look at it. I don't like to look like a slacker.

summary: Wrong Place at the Wrong Time
advice: Don't grow too fast and compromise values that made you beloved by your customers.  Thanks for pushing me, though, to realize what I could do.
pros: Team was great; still maintaining meaningful relationships years after the Chase takeover.  Bonds were made during many long hours of shared project work.  Compensation was good.
cons: Very demanding schedule.  Felt like much of the time we were racing against time.  Thought we had made it through when things got pulled out from underneath us.

summary: If you have to be at a bank, not too bad
advice: more career development for entry level talent
pros: Great senior leadership in Jamie and his board, lots of vacation time. Good benefits for healthcare, stock options, 401k. If you can find the right people and network, there are a lot of interesting opportunities throughout the bank.
cons: Like any large company, key is finding the right people to work with. Can be hard to move up quickly, culture is still very old fashioned. A lot of legacy technology and increasing restrictions.

summary: The most respectful company culture of the big banks.
advice: Nothing that the finance opinion pages aren't saying.
pros: Works like an extremely efficient machine, if you're in the right part of the bank. Treats its employees well, and at least on a worker level tries to adhere to the "don't be evil" principle. People are generally nice.
cons: You're working for a bulge bracket bank, and everything that comes with that is true. When your manager is being nice, it's because she's making sure you're going to be in on a Saturday.

advice: Go to bat for your employees, even though senior management doesn't allow you to make final decisions, let your people know they are appreciated and that you did all you could for them.
pros: Great company benefits, i.e. health care, dental, EAP, matching 401K, employer matching contributions to lots of charities.
cons: This is such a large company to really hone in on the cons,  but the management was my biggest hurdle.  Very unfair performance reviews, year after year, 6 different managers in the 6 years I was there.

advice: Invest in cultivating solid branch teams that foster cooperation. De-incentivize greed, value customer service instead of paying lip service to it. Pay staff more instead of selling them on the incentive plan. Low salaries breed desperation and erode personal integrity.
pros: Everyone recognizes the brand so you never have to explain what you do. Decent benefits with generous domestic partner coverage.
cons: It's a mega bank that tries to make bankers feel like they don't work in retail but Saturday shifts, abusive customers and apathetic management will remind you of that fact.

advice: Work to be more open to innovation from all levels. Sometimes being in a satellite office you do not have the chance to have your voice heard as if you were in NYC.
pros:
Great training ground for technical skills at a bulge-bracket firm. 

Extremely smart leaders and very passionate about their business.

Great ability to move around the firm.
cons:
Sometimes their can be a lot of politics one must play into in order to succeed.

Work life balance as an analyst isn't great but that's a given.

summary: Company supports internal mobility and career progression
advice: Raise the bar when it comes to more competitive salaries. Place more loyalties to your employees rather than cutting cost by laying off performing employees
pros: Internal mobility and career growth encouraged. Culture better than most banking institution its size. Branding is excellent compared to its immediate competitors like Wells Fargo or Bank of America.
cons: Less than most salary range compared to peers. Cutthroat management style when it comes to cost cutting which could lead to employees unsure of security of employment.

summary: Great benefits, buttoned up corporate culture
pros:
- Awesome benefits & compensation
- Some teams are fantastic - it really depends on the part of the bank you are in!
- Great mobility opportunities
- Chase bank has a better culture than JPMorgan in my opinion!
cons:
- Buttoned up, corporate culture; very stiff 
- Company is huge - you can start to feel like 1 out of 260k
- Your experience will really vary depending on the team you're at - some are awesome, some are terrible
- Hours can be very long depending on the team

summary: Not a good place to work
advice: I know is hard to manage a slow heavy organization but make use of the talent of your people. There are plenty of us willing o steer the company on the right direction.
pros: Big company with established organization with procedures and lot of learning opportunities. Good location close to home. In site cafeteria.
cons: They were always scaring people about loosing their jobs and having layoffs. They promoted child care site when I was offer a job and they had it closed a month right after I left my previous job and was hired.

advice: Hire from internal if you want a cookie cutter approach to a boring industry.  Times are changing and some people don't take well to the pushy wealth management CPC being forced down there throat when they come in for a debit card.
pros: The company was established but guidance was minimal for industry newbie.  Opportunity was ample but environment seemed non collaborative and political.
cons: Merit based advancement seemed less frequent than tenure. Not a corporate feel to the branch level consumer banking role.

advice: Keep killing the tail.
pros: Many changes for the good going on in Tech, lots of new management from outside the firm bringing new ideas and approaches also skills relevant to new technologies (e.g. cloud).  Good benefits. After many RIFs a lot of the dead wood is gone in GT.
cons: Still a long way to go to catch up to other tech dependent companies; still remaining a lot of the legacy baggage from so many mergers. Never ending org changes.

advice: It's a hard pill to swallow when you state the most common talked about theme in employee surveys is pay compensation versus competitors and your response is "we'll look at everything except compensation."
pros: Benefits are pretty good, 4 weeks off if you are management but starting is 3 weeks.  Additional personal days are a perk too.  401k match, pension match, and lucrative sick time give you probably more time off than you need.
cons: Unless you are in a revenue generating platform, i.e. sales, the pay is considerably lower than competitors.

advice: Keep valuing contributions made by employees.  Being empowered, listened to, and given the opportunity to make decisions and execute on those decisions goes a long way in making someone feel important.
pros: Great company.  The management team of different departments has invested in young talent and let's them flourish with the proper tutelage.  Great learning environment.
cons: It is easy to get lost in the fray while you are working for a company of this size.  If you don't look out for yourself you can get forgotten about in the scheme of things.

advice: You can't put every department under a metric to determine its success.  Find the value that they are providing and measure them on that as well as to the impact they provide the company.
pros: Senior Management and Leadership are aware of the risk related to the business and take strides to ensure that the company is protected
cons: The environment is too open and does not allow people to do their work properly and in conformance to their function/service they provide the company.  Executives treat departments as cogs in a wheel rather than of their real value.

summary: Middle of the Road Experience - Employee for 2 Years
advice: Outsourcing jobs to cheap place like India may save costs dollar wise, but payment is still made when it comes to the quality of work being done, terrible communication, and poor business processes.
pros:
Prestigious name on your resume.
Can learn a lot if you try.
cons:
Lots of talk about career mobility at senior level but direct managers are likely to oppose.
People get screwed on compensation and management will pay the piper.
Lack of rewards for people who do good work and lack of punishment for people who do bad work.

advice: Raise the salary of the associates in order to keep turnover down and motivate analyst level workers so they try harder to get promoted.
pros:
Great place to work at to boost your resume and to gain some basic skills working with Excel and managing books and records. 

Friendly co-workers and higher ups. 

Average age of the floor was about 25. 

Paid overtime really adds up
cons:
401k doesn't match till 3 years.

High turnover because of it being a great entry-level job and the lack of higher pay at the next level.

summary: Some days it doesn't seem worth it
pros: Great benefits: 401k, 4 weeks vacy, 16 week maternity leave!
cons: As others have said, a decrease in the number of employees at the branch level is causing a lot of frustration and stress on customers and employees. A lot of operational aspects are hard to take care of when you are constantly being pulled away to help run the tellerline. The branch manager is also the person that can make or break the team, and unfortunately it seems like it is very hard to find these great managers....

advice: Check your lower  level (Executive Director) management styles.  Reduce use of profanity within Corporate technology.  Upper management needs to bypass MD/ED level and listen to the technologists.
pros: Leading (not Bleeding) edge technology.  Decent benefits.  C-suite acceptance of Investments in technology resulting in very large IT organization but gets bureaucratic in every stage.
cons: Management & Organizational structure changes every 9 to 12 months for past 5 years in Global Technology.  High turnover rate for individual contributors.  Dictatorial management style and use of profanity by management in Corporate Technology.

summary: Middle Management ignores top company culture
advice: Pay can't stay flat if the company has a killer year. Your messaging is out of touch with reality. Saying take a break and prioritize your mental health come across as insincere when your middle management sets goals that will not allow that.
pros: Able to work from home for now. At the most senior level management is empathetic in addressing social issues.
cons: Constantly shifting priorities as middle layer leadership doesn't have a clear vision on how to meet top leadership goals.

summary: Very Bureaucratic old school kind of culture. Managers do not communicate across the board.
advice: Please teach your managers to communicate effectively with their direct reports. I notice managers ( company wide) just keep quiet and fail to give honest and truthful feedback. So looks like managers lack training on how to implement a good feedback mechanism.  Was very surprised how deep rooted this culture was.
pros: You may get false sense of belief that you are working for worlds largest financial institution.
cons: Very Bureaucratic old school kind of culture. Managers do not communicate across the board. I initially thought it was an issue with one specific manager. Over the years realized this was more of a company culture.

advice: Bankers need to get raises instead of telling them to make their own raise by performing more. It shows no respect for the other things they must do that doesn’t increase performance like being an Adapter or a Manager on Duty. Also, many times managers will make the schedule around their own regardless of the needs of the staff.
pros:
Good Vacation Benefits
Decent 401k
Access to Higher Tier Banking Products
cons:
Unachievable Performance Goals for some markets.
Supervisors are often inflexible regarding scheduling.
Health Benefits not great.

summary: Great company if youre content with being stagnant
advice: none. worked for 5 years with promises of raises and promotions and never received any besides a .25 raise which was nationwide 6 months into the job.
pros: Great environment and mostly good people. But be careful who you trust, Get ti know them strictly professionally.
cons: Promise of advancement and never follow through. Constantly changing programs used for "betterment of company" and most times old programs were better. Phasing out certain positions clearly to reduce the workforce and save $$$

advice: Stop being so political, as advisors it effects our business in a negative that is through no fault of our own.
pros: Good starting salary, great systems in place to build a book and generate revenue. No need to buy leads or prospect outside the bank, you have a team who provides warm referrals, investment portfolios are top notch so closing is easy if you learn them and can explain them.
cons: Too political at times, incentive structures can be a little confusing.

summary: Long term career growth and professional development
advice: I enjoy working here. Lately management has taken a focused approach to develop and incorporate new technologies into existing bank products. I’m grateful for the opportunity to be working at JPMC during this transformation/modernization time period!
pros: Many growth opportunities. Competent leaders and mentors. State of the art technology. Emerging leader in FinTech. Best campus location in Plano TX!
cons: Driving change can be difficult. Slow to adopt or incorporate new technologies. Acquisition and expansion create inconsistent company culture. System and process improvements can be slow to incorporate.

summary: Good company but very leftist and too many recent woke policies
advice: Too many managers that only care about their own careers at the expense of their employees. Company has leaned too far left and bought into the woke-ness too much.
pros: Benefits and opportunities to do different jobs if you're not happy with current role.
cons: Very progressive policies and crazy amount of requirements in order to do daily job functions. You have to constantly fight to make sure system credits you with the correct commissions (PVC's) each month.

advice: Investing in your employees equally across the board will show that you care about them, as they're the reasons why you can make the money that you do.
pros: Work is very easy to pick up on and learn and team leads/supervisors are very eager in helping to expand your tools in whatever area of work or career it is you'd like to pursue.
cons: Not very transparent with reasons as to the lack of pay differentials between experienced workers and new-hires, with new-hires making more than the tenure workers.

summary: Corporate office was a great place to work.
advice: What to say.....I think they have learned their mistakes (hopefully)
pros:
Given a lot of opportunities to grow and try other roles
Management was very understanding when time was needed off or personal reasons and many in my department worked flexible schedules or were allowed to work from home part time.
cons:
Upper management was clueless a lot of times
Continual lay offs during my entire 5 year span there
Raises were always minimal. 3% was "great"
Could have had better career paths so that employees had something to work towards

summary: I used to love working for this company
advice: Be open and honest with your direct reports and stop treating them like children that don't know how the world works.
pros: The benefits, time off, and sometimes the schedules were great
cons: This company has made it clear they are more concerned with profits over their employees. They became dictators regarding vaccine mandates and returning to the office. I left one day after my 20 year anniversary because it became very apparent their  priorities had changed.

advice: All areas of management need to focus on the big picture in every initiative. Open communication is vital to the success of the business.
pros: While working with JP Morgan Chase, I had an extensive array of training opportunities available to me. This is a great company if you are seeking a supportive environment for career growth.
cons: Can be difficult to unite management to achieve one goal as a team. Many processes are not streamlined, and departments have a tendency to work in a silo.

summary: If you can handle the politics, it's a pretty good place to work.
advice: It has become clear how little you value your employees during this recession. You are taking every advantage of the situation that if people leave, they'll have difficulties finding another position, so you might as well force as much work out of as few as possible, with no raises or overtime.
pros: Good pay. For technology people, it's a great place to experience really large scale stuff.
cons: The politics are terrible. Death by process!!!

summary: Smart people, highly structured place to work.
advice: Despite everything that has happened at WaMu, there were some highly capable, inelligent people who worked there who did everything in their power to make the customer happy.  It is a shame that it will be remembered otherwise.
pros: Good compensation and benefits, Professionalism of co-workers was outstanding, Lots of opportunity for visibility and opportunities to work with executives, Good Community support
cons: Being in the finance industry at this time is very difficult.  WaMu is being held up as a "how not to do business".

summary: Give exceptional service and sell company products.
advice: I filed a complaint on my manager for harassment and was fired 3 days later. It was not investigated by HR as an independent review. Chase allowed my manager for personal reasons to ruin my career in the financial industry by lying about the reason I was terminated and noted my U4.
pros: I met and worked with a lot of great customers and employees. There is an ability to make good money, have great benefits and is a career over "just" a job.
cons: I believe Chase as a company literally does NOT care about any employee enough to look into anything happening within their branches. HR IS NOT ON THE EMPLOYEES SIDE.

advice: Reduce the corporate politics and promote greater meritocracy based on true performance and contribution and not on simply expectations and perception.
pros: Some very talented and smart people.  Newer people(past 7 years) are of high caliber.  Company is very socially conscience such as being green and humanitarian.  Jamie Dimon is a great CEO and businessman.
cons: Pay is not as competitive amongst the top ranked financial firms.  Too many people so lots of bureaucracy.  Corporate politics can sometime screw up a good team / environment.

summary: decent environment but under market pay
advice: management need to think a way to motivate people and increase the salary in general. try to have as more as possible town hall meetings
pros: nice colleague plus good environment and convenient commute and working load is not that high，but is pay is under market pay
cons: you do not have much opportunity to move up if you do not talk to people a lot. you hace to work long hours sometime. not many people care about what others are doing

advice: Management should move back to a more customer centric focus.  This is going to require more initiatives and focus around employee satisfaction.
pros: he company has Good Benifits. It is a training ground to develop your professional skills and resume especially for those just out of college. It is recognized as Top rated institution.
cons: It is a very large company who's culture has changed and is primarily focused on maximizing share holder value and has lost some of the customer, relationship and employee focus

summary: Unhappy place to spend half of your day.
advice: Everyone has a different situation in life and it would help if they tried to work around it. One time, I had an end of semester exam final and the manager wouldn't let me take it during that time. You can't help it if the university schedules it a certain time at a different time and day.
pros: Great health benefits, dental, and eye benefits. 401k is pretty good.
cons: A pain to come into work. Difficult to work with your personal schedule even if it's outside your hours.

advice: the managing directors often did not get the more junior people involved in many aspects of projects so it often did not feel like you were part of the team
pros: they have a very good training program and you definitely learn a lot.  most of the people are very smart and willing to help you succeed
cons: the hours can often be pretty long and you occasionally have to work weekends, not much flexibility when it comes to having your own personal time

advice: Better employee communication and team spirit in the hierarchy. More attention paid to employee development and review process. More hands on visibility.
pros: If you bring a constant entrepreneurial effort, shrewdly play the politics, power and authority and have senior management like you, then it can be a good day-to-day experience.
cons: Employee review process is more so than not perfunctory. When the dust settles it's more who you know and how they like you than a stellar functional performance of the job.

summary: Nice company to work for - great perks
advice: I thought management was very helpful and available. I wish I would have gotten feedback more often on my performance. Also, my direct supervisor was changed 4 times within a 2 year period.
pros:
-Friendly atmosphere
-Accept diversity, GLBT friendly
-Company culture
-Good pay
-Good management
-Clear communication regarding performance
-Great perks: fitness center, health insurance, bonus, discounts at local stores, etc.
cons:
-Asked to sell things to customers in a way they wouldn't notice, borderline unethical. 
-Schedule not flexible. 
-Office politics: it is not what you know it is who you know.

summary: One of the better places to work at
advice: Don't stop the work you are doing to improve the employee experience and work morale. It is not perfect but progress no matter how small is more important to overall satisfaction.
pros: Most banks tend to not care about their employees, I was fortunate enough to work for a division where management tended to most of our concerns and worked with us to address any issues.
cons: It still is a very large organization and it is easy to feel like a drone at your day to day job.

advice: Reward your employees for their longevity of service and hard work by promoting within.
