advice: management can be a little more democratic.
pros: Unlimited Commission earning structure, learn something new almost everyday. 3 weeks paid vacation, 5 sick and 4 personal. Room for advancement.
cons: can become very busy during periodic rush hrs, but that can turn into a pro since you make commission. May have to work alternate saturdays if your location is open on Saturdays.  Can be more open to new ideas  without breaking the policies.

pros: Some good people working on the team, friendly colleagues.
cons:
The managers in this team are terrible. Low technical competence, they don't involve in the team; they feel superior to his subordinates.
The managers give orders and don't lead by example; they also blame their subordinates if the projects don't succeed. 
The managers never share any technical know-how (maybe for lack of hands-on experience).
Also, some colleagues described the ambient in the team as "toxic."
Summing-up, not the place if you want to learn and develop your career further.

summary: Benefits are good but the atmosphere is toxic
advice: Really recognize the lack of diversity in the ranks and the value of the women that are in the office. Women are so disparaged and discouraged and truly made to feel worthless. I've seen so many wonderful women leave because they were passed over for the regular white men that they knew would automatically get the next ED or MD role.
pros: benefits, female coworkers, working from home
cons: only promote white men who know each other and work together to make sure they help each other

summary: Passed on promotion due to being pregnant.
advice: Treat women equally to men.  A woman should not have to choose between a job she loves and is good at and having children.
pros: I loved everything about my job and I was really good at it.
cons: I was passed on a promotion due to being pregnant. It was widely known. I had great numbers and glowing recommendations. I was also told I could not obtain a part-time position within the company because I was over qualified.

summary: I just started so I wont be able to say too much but so far I love it!
pros: They are willing to work with my college schedule. I get paid 12 dollars an hour which is better than most part time jobs. Full benefits after 60 days and vacation time starts immediately.
cons: I have nothing to complain about really. I wish they closed earlier but thats not even a problem. I guess you always have to wear black shoes and pants sucks but not bad.

advice: Treat your employees better help develop them and do not over work them . Chase add job enrichment you have the money to do so!
pros: company as a whole is well organized with their human resources department and employee programs
cons: depends on management can be lazy and not really help you developed No growth unless you want to become a manager . You can also be easily targeted by upper management which hinders you from growth or moving offices . They have hybrid banker position that are over worked and underpaid

advice: Stop the bias and start acting like a global corporation.
pros: You work with the latest technologies and work with highly capable human beings.
cons: Extremely strong East Coast bias.  Even when faced with metrics that prove midwest employees outperformed those from NY & NJ, credit rarely fell upon the midwest teams.  High level managerial positions were not given to Midwestern candidates.  The company valued outside talent with fewer years of experience over its own employees. In IT, weekend only releases made for extremely long hours.

advice: Continue to be collaborative with Managers and their project leads.  Be open to suggestions which drive success.  Be agile in approach and methodology.
pros: JPMorganChase has many large project initiatives which challande the most seasoned Project Managers.  Programs involve both complex business and high Technology in an ever changing environment driven by federal regulations.
cons: Program Resource requirements can easily be underestimated which places extra demands on the project teams.  This can lead to a very stressful situation when deadlines are mandated.

advice: Place more emphasis on obtaining feedback from direct reports and solid 360 performance reviews of the IT Leadership and Management Team - Specifically ED and first band MD's.
pros: Very large Organization with the opportunity for mobility with Excellent benefits package.
cons: After 10 years I found the IT organization lacking sound leadership.  Within the various IT groups I worked within, you work long hours and very hard, most times this is unnecessary and mostly due to misguided leaders in key positions providing poor direction.

advice: I can't say enough good things about senior management. I was proud to work at JPM.
pros: Incredibly strong leadership team, both locally and at senior management levels. There was a deep bench as well - no matter who left, someone as strong, or stronger replaced them in the majority of instances. I liked my team and the division as a whole.
cons: I left for a new opportunity, but if I had to do it again, I probably would have toughed it out and stayed at JPM.

advice: Advices to the big management. Share with the little workers the enormous profits you make. We are an important part of your success.
pros:
Not too pushy.
No work on sunday and holidays.
401K
cons:
Salary is terrible.
Incentives are over-taxed which doesn't allow to compensate poor salaries. 
Rules always changing.
Very hard customers services. A lot of rudness and threat. 
Little opportunities to grow if any.
Management responsabilities not appreciated as no change in the salary.
Possibility to be fired for no reason anytime.
Open longer than other bank on saturday.
No full time position for Teller.
Health benefits not affordable.

pros:
Mobility opportunities
"Own your career" culture... I worked in 3 different LOBs and what I observed is that the most successful employees are those that develop close relationships with management, ask for more work or promotion opportunities, and find ways to take ownership of projects, initiatives, etc.
cons:
Work/Life is what you make of it - seemed like the most successful managers worked A LOT.
Compensation is below industry averages... they can pay less because people are drawn to the brand name.
High turnover in most businesses, especially at junior levels

advice: Get more training to be more personable with your team members. Learning to be a better leader will help motivate your teams to do better and strive for more within the company.
pros: Great benefits, great company to work for in general. Specialist II in Auto finance.
cons: Auto finance Dept is a very demanding and under paid position to work for. Metrics for production are attainable yet can also have its moments when there is no production to pull work from. Tons of favoritism in that Dept.

advice: Please have your managers be involved in their day to day actions in their branches .  It seems like my manager did not exist . She would come in randomly but not earlier than 10am & leave at 6pm sitting the back and hiding . But the rule for bankers was quit different .
pros: Has  good benefits but you feel like each year they will cut down  on something.
cons: their salary is too low but when I started with them their commission payout was good so it would compensate  for the low salary but each year they cut down and make it harder to make money . Just imagine for 1mm dollar investment your pay out is .02%.

advice: Quit giving jobs to foreign contractors and quit taking such huge bonuses for yourselves
pros: Good vacation plan and decent healthcare
cons: More and more IT jobs are being outsourced to both offshore and onshore Indian contractors.  TCS has taken over.  There have been layoffs which will likely continue as the jobs are given to Indian contractors. There is no opportunity for advancement and no new employees coming in, only more contractors.  Employee morale is very bad in some groups.  Raise and bonus were insulting and determined by a Director  2 levels up the org chart who I have never even met.  Everybody gets "meets expectations" on their annual reviews which are a joke.

summary: Overall I really like the firm and I would recommend it to anyone interested in working for a big bank.
advice: I hope the company takes into account how compensation is paid and that team members within the same levels do not have a huge discrepancy.
pros: Great company and great brand. Recognized across the country and expanding their global presence. Great benefits and flexible schedules. Management is great at communicating with their staff.
cons: Really long hours. Expect it to feel like working for Goldman Sachs (well that is if you're working in a growing business).

advice: Adopt a more family friendly atmosphere.  Manage your middle levels of leadership closely as there is much variability between good and truly poor managers.
pros: Opportunity for those who seek it, better than average benefits, solid learning environment with training/education opportunities, career progression at entry levels through mid management can be swift for those who apply themselves
cons: Work life balance is truly terrible.  No real respoect for your outside family.  High demands on time, including travel depending on your position.  Unwieldy and bureaucratic as is typical at large organizations.

summary: Interesting, challenging, awesome, but... Under paid...
advice: None. This is how a company should be ran, I can pick up the phone and speak to the ceo if I wanted too. That's neat! However pay talent with respect, increase salaries based on performance more that just 3%
pros: Advancement easily, gives proper tools to work with, mgmt support 100% when you squeak the wheel. Customer geared where it makes logistical business sense....
cons: Corporate, no control over lending, too cookie cutter. Lost arts of personalized business banking, unless you have a good banker. Turn over rate high.

advice: Its time to re-invest in your most important asset; your employees.
pros: Good wellness program. Generous vacation time, but you will need it.
cons: Going thru restructuring of businesses, attempting to automate interactions with customers. Large scale lay offs across the board have left survivors overworked. Dozens of IT systems that don't inter connect well has created a nightmare management issue. Business has spent so much money settling law suits that little or nothing is left to spend on training and developing employees.

summary: It was a great place with the right people, but the business model was not sustainable due to bleed out of great people.
advice: Seriously listen to the people doing all the heavy lifting (the foot soldiers) and be willing to hire and promote those who deserve it based on performance. Also, the business model of outsource/offshoring has a way of returning and causing headaches for both clients and employees (especially those skilled).
pros: Great networking, mentoring, diversity, and tons of projects if you want it.
cons: Projects dead end pretty often and don't count on worklife balance.

summary: Large company where you can grow in many areas
advice: Improve in communication
pros: Allows you to grow in your career and certain position allow you to work virtually. Always a wide range of professional opportunities.
cons: Certain job are available in certain locations that you are limited to grow unless you relocate.  Progression to next grade ranking is sequential, so if you qualify for a position you can only move up to the next grade level. Must be in that position for a year before moving again

advice: Listen more to the employees.  Most people are content, but things could be better.
pros: Global company has a multitude of opportunities to grow.  Sometimes you have to start near the bottom but there are plenty of opportunities within the Chase.  They are willing to hire people from different backgrounds and give them a chance to start a career within Chase.
cons: Do your research.  Some departments have limited growth, but stick with it.  After 1 year you can be eligible to transfer to a better/different opportunity.

advice: Pay long time employees who have proven their worth a decent salary when being promoted.  Many have left and come back to get their desired salaries.
pros: Benefits, PTO, Work life balance, Career Advancement.  All in all they take good care of their employees in ways other companies do not.
cons: Internal Salary increases are very small even when changing departments and taking on larger projects and responsibilities.  External hires seem to be given better treatment when it comes to salary.

advice: They need to raise compensation to industry standards otherwise the turnaround rate will just keep increasing.
pros: JPMorgan offers great flexible work hours as well as remote telecommuting. They have great technology available for their staff. Many employee discount programs available and perks. Great people work there and its a friendly environment.
cons: Compensation is below average and bonuses are 1 to 2 %.  Many groups are understaffed so it is difficult to keep up with your work. You essentially end up doing the job of five people. So you are simply overworked and underpaid.

summary: An industry leader with a few drawbacks
advice: Policy and procedure needs to be simplified, more does not always equal better. Continue to develop better technology for internal users, not just client facing platforms.
pros: Large stable company, consistent performer. Encourage mobility within the firm. Lots of online training resources available. A very well structured performance evaluation process.
cons: Onerous policy and procedure, average technology solutions. Policy and procedure is very top-down, needs more input from those that actually do the daily work.

advice: The same few FAs complain and are rewarded when there are accounts to be assigned.  If you are not one of these folks you will not receive these transitioned accounts.
pros: Your schedule is as flexible as you need it to be.
cons: A lot of chaff in the wheat.  The management team is weak, but if you can produce they will stay out of your way for the most part.  Most FA's do not know a whole lot about investing, but they can push what the company tells them to push.

summary: This company was an opportunity that I needed at a certain time and I have enjoyed working for such a great company.
pros: There are various pros such as benefits, strong company, career development, 401K matching, and a genuine desire to respond to both customer and employee feedback.
cons: It is very discouraging that the base salary is not competitive with other firms. I feel that the base salary is extremely on the low end and discouraging to longtime employees and those that are strong performers.

advice: Most manager do a pretty good job considering their work load in addition to managing their teams.
pros: Great benefits, employee recognition, constantly make improvements to their systems and processes made on employee and customer feedback.
cons: Odd schedules and having to bid for a new one yearly even if you had a recent change, Very low employee retention rate, low pay compare to competitors, no sales / incentives position- offering products and benefits for free, very difficult to get raises unless doing a lot of extra work / projects for free.

advice:
-Expand program to make internal consulting a longer term program 
-Provide more flexibility to junior staff who are looking to find right fit with in the bank, whether in ops / markets technology or in a client facing role
pros:
-great exposure to strategic planning in operating and technology groups by rotating through different assignments
-technology group assignments very good for programmers
cons:
-Expand program to make internal consulting a longer term program 
-Having a tech / programming background is helpful for markets technology roles

advice: Promote culture by promoting outings for people to socialize outside of a work environment. Other than that, the management was good in my opinion.
pros: Very good experience. The culture was great and everyone was caring to lend a hand. It is a very good bank.
cons: The pay may not be as competitive as you would expect from a big bank. Nonetheless the overall experience was great so if you are looking to learn than this is the place.

advice: Reduce the number of re-orgs. Org announcement are published almost on a weekly basis and it's hard to focus on business priorities when you can't even get to know the person you are working for before it has already moved
pros: There are a bunch of very smart people with very high standards both in terms of business conduct and professionalism
cons: Environment is extremely competitive and business heads spend more time managing up and defending their turf than leading people and making sure clients experience is up to expectations

advice: Continue to invest in technology and then follow up with technology training for any employee that wants to advance their career.
pros: A Challenging environment with a focus on doing the best job for our clients.  So much to learn from managing projects, financial analysis, working well with many other intelligent colleagues.
cons: Sometimes the environment can be very corporate even though senior management strive hard to reduce beauricracy.  Technology can sometimes really hold us back from full potential.

advice: Please revise your policy . It's 2017 !!!!
pros:
Great company!!
Great CEO
Talented folks!
Work life balance is moderate
cons:
Management style: very bad in promoting internally. Long queue to get promoted...
Wrong outdated policy:
If they want to hire an employee, they can't , because they have policies of not to promote anyone from outside, on the other hand, they can't pay the person enough unless they promote the person. Catch 22 situation.
How they would attract, hire or rehire talent???

advice: At the branch level is where the firm makes their revenue. These salaries need to be updated. Stop putting such low value on branch employees. Hire qualified branch managers who can lead a team and make staff feel like they have a voice.
pros: set schedule. Holidays off. Great benefits. Uniform.
cons: The opportunity here is so limited. To make money, to move around internal to different departments, and advancement is non exisitent. Upper management as well as branch managment has very poor leading skills. You will have no voice here.

advice: Get your ducks in a row for remote workers, offer better support and training and the process to obtain lending authority should not take months.
pros: Salary and benefits are excellent,. The people have been pleasant so far.
cons: Very corporate and lacks common sense underwriting. Antiquated loan system that is very difficult to learn. Not prepared for remote workers and lack of communication and instruction. Training was not efficient and process of getting lending authority takes months. It's nearly impossible to get systems help with computer issues.

advice: Provide the pay that matches the job field – and provide regular ideas of next raise timeline along with bonuses. It gives us a little glimmer of hope.
pros: The shift towards becoming a technology company is great.  Depending on the team, you can have great coworkers! Management seems to be open to change.
cons: Processes boggling down on development time. The culture here needs some work, though I see that there is a shift happening.  Hard to move up in ranking positions.

advice: Communication is Key within a team. Metric, understand certain situation that should not count against you
pros:
Benefits: Maternity leave 16 wks
401 K match 
Lots of Paid Time Off - even to get your covid shot and its very flexible 
Great Leadership
Extensive training and support
co-workers are amazing
cons:
Lack of communication- better communication about updates could better improve work flow processes and avoid errors
Metrics expectation is reachable but there are situations where you cannot control and will just ruin all your hard work and can be hard to bounce back from

advice: Private Client Bankers are the eyes and ears for advisors in the branch. Training for most bankers is lacking. The curriculum needs to be ramped up to better educate all bankers on what to send as leads and how to look for client needs and opportunities.
pros: The company culture from a grand view was nice. At the branch level, it gets lost.
cons: Commission is low, work/life balance is non-existent. I spent more time doing things to help the branch operate than I was able to do my actual job.

summary: Great working enviornment and improving, but...
pros: Great working environment for project management teams, increasing push throughout all of the company to promote diversity and inclusion, stable executive leadership, name recognition. Work life balance great since WFH due to the pandemic.
cons: Pay rate for experienced workers is falling well behind the industry standard which is causing a massive exodus, promotion criteria more confusing than before and not nearly as transparent as it is portrayed to be. Strong push to return to office due to real estate pricing reasons rather than productivity reasons.

advice: Your relentless drive for profit is destroying the reputation of the company.  This company is the prime example of the dark side of capitalism.
pros: They do provide some training, and there is a small ammount of leeway to accomplish your own projects.  They provide 4 weeks of vactiaon.
cons: The pay is very low for the industry, and they have a relentless drive for outsourcing and insourcing.  Our manager said in just about every meeting, "we need to ousource more because its cheaper."

advice: give your current employees a better shot to get promoted.  Just treat you current customers with respect and try to keep them and work with them.
pros: Great training, good money and unlimited commissions. Good professional work environment Always looking for employees ideas, thoughts and concerns. Overall good work place.
cons: having 2 preset appointment to open new account everyday. Chase promotes favorites not based on merit. If you hit the goals to get promoted they will say now you have to hit this goal. They string you along

summary: Great company with short-sighted, unsupportive management
pros: The platform of the bank is great. Products, technology, and client support is nothing short of top notch in my opinion.
cons: Direct management is short-sighted when it comes to decision making regarding the business. Turnover is extremely high with very minimum consistency within action plans for the business. Promotions are difficult to come by as well. Promises of career advancement will be made to steer production, only to take them away when the opportunity does come up to keep employee working for the management team.

advice: For corporate operations in particular:  Trying to accomplish different things by moving the same management around to various job titles will not work.  If someone has a history of failure in their position, they should not be given further management opportunities.
pros:
Large, stable company with a good vision
Tons of resources to help do your job properly
cons:
The large company can be intimidating if you aren't ready for it
Very specialized work doesn't leave room for much opportunity in other areas of the bank
Internal mobility is very difficult

advice: Get some integrity.
pros: They do a great job with training you to help you succeed.  Also, they have an amazing support team that makes your job easier.  Great benefits except for healthcare...use to have amazing healthcare recently its not good.
cons: District and Market management have a complete lack of integrity.  Again the is an awesome company but somehow in most area's District and Market management are so detached they have forgotten what its like to run a business or they never knew to begin with

summary: No work-life balance on operations side of business...just a number here.
advice: Pay the people that keep the departments and company moving and in check.  Hire more operations people and get rid of overpaid and lazy traders and salespeople.
pros: Looks great on your resume that you've worked for one of the prestigious big banks.
cons: Low pay considering the importance of the transactions you are a part of.  No rewards for going above and beyond the normal work.  Long hours and low pay, no balance in life.

advice: Career growth, saying mobility is important and standing by it.
pros: the benefits package at the company is competitive and a definite plus. The employees and atmosphere makes work more enjoyable. There are a number of development programs and training's which make it very easy to enhance your skillset.
cons: easy to move laterally but difficult to move upwards, first crack not always given to internal employees. Work, depending on what you're doing, can be cumbersome. HR is slow, communication not always up to par

pros: Some of the smartest and hardest working people I've ever worked with. Expectations are high and that you can keep up in the fast paced environment.
cons:
Low pay despite long hours and high performance (consistently highly rated but compensation never reflected it - main driver of my departure).
Lots of bureaucracy to deal with, sometimes impedes progress and makes decision making harder than it should be

advice: Be more open to moving ideas up the ladder - more efficiency within the system.
pros: Great leadership with a clear direction for the company. Willing to help summer analysts and analysts. Focused on developing talent. Great place to get started with the company.
cons: As true with most jobs in finance, the hours are tough with aggressive goals. Big company, may be hard to get things rolling and started. It's easier to push a boulder off a hill, than to try to roll one up.

summary: Great place to build a book of business.
pros: Great brand and thought leadership. You can really build strong relationships within the branch to facilitate a strong pipeline to grow your book of business. Clients are very comfortable with having their money with JP Morgan-Chase. It makes it much easier to get clients when they already bank with chase.
cons: It's a tough business for the first few years. It takes some time to navigate the environment. But JP Morgan-Chase is a great place to build a client base.

advice: With the vast amount of employee resources available, it would be nice if one of them was a better organizational view to see who across lines of businesses you're role is most similar to.  Just a direct reporting hierarchy is not sufficient.
pros:
--collaborative, round-table culture where everyone who as something to contribute does
--great benefits
--loads of vacation time
--incredible employee support services
cons: --being such a large institution, knowing how you're role fits in to the big picture can become a bit of a daunting task.

pros: Amazing benefits, stability of a Fortune 10 Company, WFH with gradual return to office, great leadership, promote from within. Some of the locations are very nice which is the only up-side of going back to the office.
cons: Outdated and old-school mentality when it comes to culture and work-life balance. For a company so large, I understand the need for standardization but seems that the company thinks employees are absolutely unable to WFH full time and perform (although employee surveys and performance/company earnings say otherwise).

advice: Fight HR, other departments, regulators and for your employees. Your subordinates are watching and hoping you have a spine.
pros: They're always hiring . . . always. That should tell you something right there. There are good people there suffering right along with you.
cons: They will exploit you. If you're a veteran they acknowledge enlisted time in salary considerations and they will take full advantage of any tax rebates you can get them (I had to fill out my own form for being a disabled vet on their behalf). Everyone is constantly leaving and there is no continuity in the process as a result. They're constantly putting lipstick on a pig to appease whoever's looking.

advice: Actually listen to your employees not just say you are going to listen but ACTUALLY listen, your employees are very smart and some do work their butts off for no real gain, while most others have gotten into the mentality of saying why should I go above and beyond it doesn't pay off.
pros: Easy, almost impossible to get fired, great co workers, pretty laid back
cons: Dont get paid what you are worth, like pulling teeth when asking for a raise, micro managing like crazy

summary: Overall Satisfied with position at JPMorgan Chase
advice:
Hire and promote women of color in senior positions within technology and operations.  Develop a retention program for people of color.  

Develop a program to bring engineering onshore.
pros: There is good communication from senior management and the firm makes a concerted effort to allow employees an opportunity for a good work/life balance.
cons: There is a huge disparity of women in color in senior positions within technology and operations.  In addition some of the women are not treated with fairness and respect.

pros: Lots of opportunities to learn and develop yourself in other areas within the same industry. Many networking opportunities and company events. Great employer, great people working there, and great opportunities.
cons: In the beginning there is not much to do. We were left to learn and take time settling in (may be a pro, but I wanted to hit the ground running). There is no pay increase for the first 2 years and many benefits do not kick in until after the first year.

advice: Listen to your bankers, they see things on a daily basis that are often overlooked by employees who aren't spending as much time with core clients.
pros: Got along with every one of my peers and managers, and was also put in a position to succeed. Was given assistance when help was needed, but was also left to do my work.
cons: Although the payout is done monthly for commission, the amount earned per product declined over time, and overall base salary is not very competitive.

summary: A good place to work while it lasted
advice: I guess it is too late for advice, but it would have been nice if there was more focus on the companies survival and less on the bottom line.
pros: Good Benefits and reasonable salary. Opportunity for advancement if you worked hard and earned it. Hired really good employees with a common goal to please the customers.
cons: Huge disconnect between corporate and branches. Towards the end branches were still being told everything was ok when in fact that was a lie.

advice: Acknowledge your talented employees. More praise, more money and quicker advancements.
pros: Your co-workers really keep you alive and kicking. Without them, the benefits are few and far between. The lower tier managers really seem to care for the subordinates but by the time you get to middle to higher management, you'll barely get to hear from them directly let alone witness their presence.
cons: There is a very slow progression for your personal growth and advancement. The ratio between your effort / talent and your compensation is outrageously disporpotionate.

advice: I do not have any advice for the management. If I did, from my experience management has been very responsive to employee feedback and take suggestions from all employees - no matter how junior or senior - into consideration.
pros: J.P. Morgan has an amazing culture, with great employees. The people here have amazing intentions and always put the client first.
cons: I do not have any cons to say, I have had nothing but great experiences while working for the company. Only good things to say.

advice: I think it would be nice to have programs available for those who work at the organization who are receiving secondary education to be trained in other positions when they are completed with their degree.
pros: One of the best reasons to work for JPMorgan Chase was the tuition reimbursement program. It was one of the best in the industry. Also you are rewarded with excellent benefits.
cons: One of the downsides I felt working at JPMorgan Chase is that it felt as if you would be stuck in your position.

advice: The program should have a mandatory role change at least half way through so that everyone can try a different role.
pros: The starting salary is very good for an entry level position. By the time the program is over you have increased your salary by 7k which starting out is really good.
cons: Not a lot of support from the program if you want to switch roles. They make it very difficult and will stick you wherever they can find a spot opposed to where they think you belong.

summary: I was a good place to work. . .
advice: Unfortunately, WaMu is not longer around.  I was not with JPMorgan Chase long enough to provide feedback to leadership other than beware of the greed that was a major cause for WaMu's precarious position and eventual destruction.
pros:
For the most part, WaMu followed the core values 
fair
caring
human
dynamic
driven
lots of opportunties for advancement (until "purchased" by JPMorgan Chase)
cons:
poor operational controls
took on way too much risk
unsound business strategies
very siloed organization
often insufficient resources to complete initiatives (or too many initiatives)

advice: Don't lose sight of the customer as that is your bottom line.  Pay attention to the strong business units in smaller cities - they rock.
pros: Boss didn't micro manage, trusted what you did, the salary was great considering the position, enjoyed the people I worked with.
cons: Really was no direction if you had quesitons as your boss was 2 time zones away.  Folks working within headquarters doing the same job were always paid more and selected for projects as they didn't have to pay travel fees.

advice: Listen to all your employees and what they suggest in order to make the workplace better, theres a lot of that not being done and in some departments theres nothing but a revolving door.
pros:
Great Company Overall
Great Benefits
Great Banking Benefits for employees
Overall, its a good company to work for, lots of people working there, lots of opportunities to move to  a different position
cons:
Very hard to move up, fairly easy to move laterally
Managers tend to favor old friends for promotions and incentives.

pros: Great Team and Managements. I guess it all depends of the branch you're located and the people you work with but in my experience I had great managers who coached me really well and they were very understanding and friendly. As part of the team you learn a lot and have fun as well.
cons: The Branch I work for was a very busy branch and it was difficult to get things done as expected. We needed a better time management  to work more efficiently and prioritize.

advice: Take the time to evaluate skills from aquiring company - many would be beneficial to your vision
pros:
Good management usage of aquiring company resources
Communication was good at the working team levle - informed of plans, challenges and roadblocks
Working cross multiple locations and time zones is a strength
cons:
Senior management not as effective in leveraging resources and treat people sometimes as number - not focused on the people/relationships and very bottom line / profit first oriented

Some areas were not as effective in leveraging skills and knowledge of aquiring company

advice: The bank is well run, as has been proven throughout the financial crisis. Systems could be improved to facilitate better deals and risk management in derivs.
pros: Great bank, smart people, presumably even better after financial crisis. Infrastructure is good and the work is interesting / challenging. Comp is ok.
cons: Hours can be long and work / life balance may not be as good as in other banks (pretty much average I suppose). Comp could be better at HFs or a few other banks.

summary: Looks good on your resume, but not a good work environment
advice: Communicate large scale issues with employees so they are not blind sided by upcoming changes. Stop operating like a cost center in a client service LOB, they do not mix
pros: Name recognition, experience with a top firm, respected in the industry, paid for OT even though salaried.
cons: Very poor work environment (won't even supply office supplies like pens!), poor communication, below average pay for position, and VERY political, forced performance rankings so even good performers get shunned by the system in place.

summary: Great benefits and great people but be prepared for a lot of bureaucracy
advice:
Invest in technology, foster greater communication and cooperation between LOB's. Embrace 
firm wide solutions for common problems instead of allowing each LOB to have their own versions of common solutions (CRM etc.)
pros: Great benefits, 401K Match, Pension Plan, One of the most stable banks
cons:
Bureaucracy, Sometimes slow to react to changing market conditions. A lot of regulations and audit work. 

Technology can be very advanced in some areas like mobile technologies but very outdated in others (punch cards and mainframes)

advice: Need to recognize and reward good hardworking employees.  Need to learn how to trust their employees.  Need to stop enforcing stupid rules and regulations such as when employees are allowed to take vacation days.

cons: Company doesn't recognize good hardworking employees.  There's no work and life balance here.  They constantly expect you to stay late till 8pm and be back in the office as early as 7am.

summary: Terrible pay, great benefits, incompetent middle management.
advice: Focus more on what frontline people are telling you and less on how they are saying it.  Consider putting a stop to the practice of forcing mandatory overtime and refusing to pay for it.

cons: The work is drudgery, and the pay is bad.  Promotions are offered only to meek, mild-mannered folks who will always say "yes."   There is a lot of talk about process improvement, but it's like turning a battleship with a frozen rudder.

cons:

- very penny-wise pound-foolish

summary: Managers Need How to Treat Employees Training

Jamie Dimond really need to do something about they way the local managers treat the employees.  Diversity is very scares in leadership. summary: Cutting Heads to build new HQ

pros: The brand is second to none. You know u work for the best bank. Sr levels are smart and work harder than anyone.
cons: Lack of respect for talent. Who you know matters more than what skills you have. Political and bureaucratic. Too many hoops and views to get anything done.

advice: great company and structure. make sure that employees are heard so they stop leaving to other banks. this seems to be the biggest epidemic
pros: Company has a great reputation, a lot of career opportunities, good incentive plan, products sell themselves. Like to promote internally

Large scale platform exposure
Interest in new technology
cons:
Non-Technical managers in technical lead roles
Large gaps between IT and Business
PMO core can be  weak
Difficult to challenge status quo

advice: I don't know. I understand the need for quality control but they pile on so much work and demand so many files per day that people are being rushed and making mistakes.
pros: Management is ok. They understand the issues facing not only the underwriters but they are grossly understaffed
cons: You work at Chase? If so LQR if not LQR  -  They audit a lot of files and when you make a mistake it's they treat it like a major major issue and it the whole moral there is horrible

summary: Challenging- you'll be honed to be the best person in very critical times
advice: Be more employee oriented,
pros: Number one is Salary, they are well known for compensating their employees, next is the chance to be knowledgeable in the banking system, lastly is mobility to explore different work streams within the company.
cons: The shift can become quite stressful because there is no guarantee that you will be assigned in the morning, most especially if you are under WHEM. Also, there is little work life balance  because of the amount of workload assigned.

advice: The management is a joke here.  Extreme, micromanaging where you can't even taking emergency calls at your desk. You must practically be outside the building to take a call. You are told to work 50 - 70 hours a week which is not even realistic for this type of job. If you hate yourself work here. Oh, you get no warnings they just fire you.
pros: There are no pro's working for this company.
cons: They rotate your shift every week. It can  be during the morning of dawn or at midnight. They call the job help desk, but you are not doing IT related work. You only get a 30 minute lunch and two fifteen minute breaks.

summary: Decent benefits and opportunities, but little work/life balance
advice: Work on making flexible work arrangements available...especially for busy parents. Also, think about adjusting call center metrics downward so that customers can be taken care of in fewer calls with higher satisfaction instead of needing to rush through calls.
pros: Benefits package good, decent pay, a few chances for advancement, fairly clear expectations from management.
cons: Lots of corporate red tape and strict rules that sometimes get in the way of really doing business efficiently. No opportunity for flexible work schedule. Mandatory overtime almost every week.

advice: Management can push harder to support employees in their transitions from one role to the next.  Good reviews and positive feedback so that those employees can go further in the company.
pros: I gained a lot of knowledge and experience at the company in the area of finance.   I was able to work in different roles and learn multiple tasks.
cons: Room for growth could be better.  It seems that employees remain in roles longer than they should, especially when they are more than qualified to move on.

advice: Consider loosening up a little and let employees be more themselves, clients like it more when we are more human.
pros: Excellent benefits, team environment, ethical company, strong client focus to always do the right thing, great compensation for strong performers, great individual and team recognition opportunites
cons: very sterile and corporate environment most of the time, constrained to one office location most of the time, big company with lots of great employees sometimes difficult to stand out, most important decisions are made off-site.

summary: Great company overall however, your experience there may vary greatly depending on your department.
pros: Great exposure!! Because the bank is so large, there is a lot of opportunity to have experience in different areas. You can move around LOB relatively easily.
cons: If you are hired into a smaller department your growth opportunities are often limited. There are many small departments within the bank that, because of their size, there are very few opportunities to move from lower level staff to an officer.  Smaller departments typically offer promotions once a position opens up.

summary: Performance driven yet relaxed atmosphere...they will take care of you
advice: Focus on training lower level managers better.
pros: Good compensation, good training and realistic expectations of their employees. Upper management is very open to feedback and will work with you if you prove yourself to be a competent worker. Very progressive environment with lots of opportunities for networking.
cons: Lower level managers are not always the cream of the crop. Hours and repetitive work can be taxing. May not be the ideal long term career choice for every one.

summary: Good Company if you want to be a retail banker
advice: provide more opportunity to branch into other departments and lines of business at JPM.
pros: If you work hard you can make some good money. They also give the opportunity for other roles in retail banking. If you love retail banking, it would be a good company to work for.
cons: Terrible Culture. This isnt a function of JPM though. Retail bankin in general has a terrible culture. You have to deal with ridiculous situations often because you deal with the public.

advice:
Stop promoting people who lack management skills
Get with the times...people CAN actually be productive when they work from home, maybe MORE productive!
pros:
Opportunity to move around to other positions internally for many 
Decent benefits and PTO
Work/life balance better than many places
cons:
Leadership is not great, too many promoted that aren't qualified to manage
Salaries stagnate quickly as merit increases are small, if you even get one
Lack of culture, open seating, lack of flexibility for work from home
Work/life balance not as good as it was

summary: Be prepared to work your life away. No work life balance. No job security. Just the buddy system.
advice: Hows about some value added management instead of just "yes" men? You would do better to actually do your jobs instead of just trying to kiss up to the guy in front of you.
pros: Decent pay. But that's it.
cons: You will live, eat and sleep JP Morgan. No job security. Management has no clue. Understaffed, outsourced and off shored. Terrible place to work. No work life balance. Advancement based on who you know instead of what kind of work you do. Look at how many people have DIED while working there. A heart attack waiting to happen. Best thing I ever did was leave.

summary: Why you should not work for JP Morgan Chase
pros: Its a big bank and they will do whatever they can to appease the customer. The commission potential is mid level. The best thing about working for Chase is the retirement planning and the pension.
cons: The salary is quite low and the hours are long. The bank doesn't really care too much about the employee experience. They will work you and not reward you at all. There is very very little room for advancement. They treat you like a number and not a person.

summary: Great Culture, but not much opportunity to advance
advice: The benefits plan needs a overhaul. I switched to my spouse’s plan because it was better coverage and 1/2 out of pocket.
pros: Some of the best people I’ve ever worked for and with. Good salary and bonus structure. Great work life balance. They promote a culture where you are expected to explore new roles frequently.
cons: Benefits are terrible. Those in higher paying jobs pay significantly more than others. Very easy to make lateral moves but challenging to promote.

advice: consider listening to your employees and stop covering up issues instead of fixing them . stop being a biys club look at actual talent versus who you know
pros:
Big company 
great reputation
great marketing 
good benefits
lots of locations
cons: company is very political and a huge boys club. Management can be incompetent and still nothing is done till too much damage has been done. instead of fixing issues they just try to cover up issues and customers are the ones that suffer

summary: great company with no engineering culture
pros: Great work life balance. friendly and nice people to work with. Benefits are decent. pay is below average. Company culture is amazing. People really care and work hard regardless of pay and title.
cons: bureaucracy everywhere. extreme corporate culture. the complete opposite of startup culture. Best in finance but technology is not the core function and they make sure engineers feel that way. No autonomy poor product and decision making. Engineers don't run engineering teams. The only way to move up is management.

advice: My job is stressful--I believe everyone in my dept is probably underpaid. Because it's hard to find people for this job, some bad employees get to stick around. Then we pick up their slack.
pros: Great benefits, opportunities for promotion, support, established, great reputation, good pay, great maternity leave and even paternity leave. Plenty of vacation time.
cons: It's a big corporation so it can be tough to get things done efficiently. In our department you hear a lot of "it's how we've always done it."

summary: My experience at Chase was great love the challenge.
advice: The management was great I think Chase had the best of the best as their Management team they all had the same general goal.
pros: Diversity, Overall great company to work for benefits are great. Coworker was  also great just and overall environment you did not mind to to. Great chance for advancement.
cons: My only downside to working for Chase was when the company relocated to Lewisville, Tx and my commute went from 10 minutes to 1 hour plus. Then came the layoff.

summary: Chase is an excellent employer. The company cares for its employees and we have one of the best CEOs in the world.
pros:
A firm built on integrity, trust, and genuine care for its people.

Strong values and commitment to innovation.

A solid team and some of the most loyal and hardworking people around.
cons: It's a huge company and it can sometimes be difficult to navigate your career and relocate in other countries unless you network effectively and have people guiding you on getting the information you need.

advice: Look for ways to limit the administrative burden that falls on the analysts, as this is the main reason for the high turnover rates in some teams.
pros: Overall, the team is extremely motivated, which contributes to an interesting atmosphere to work in. There are excellent opportunities to network, and learn about a variety of topics in finance and economics from some of the most capable individuals in the industry.
cons: Work can become very repetitive and administrative due to the heavy regulatory burden that the industry is subject to.

summary: Decent pay and benefits. Frustrating management.
advice: Lighten up on all of the conference calls. Follow-through with branches when improvements are promised.
pros: The pay and benefits are good. And their are a lot of opportunities to advance within the company.
cons: Dealing with the corporate side of Chase can be very frustrating. They make you sit through a lot of meaningless conference calls that could have been emails. They also have a habit of promising improvements and then not delivering. My own branch has been waiting on a new TCR for months now.

pros: Office environment, strong brand, warm call list, looks great on resume, help obtain finra licenses, great potential earnings. Great 401k and pension options plus access to great health care.
cons: Stagnant branch locations that don't allow new money to come in, client list have been worked for years, no upward or lateral movement, cubical style offices(no privacy to conduct business), have to hop through to many hoops to get anything done, lack of freedom, micro managed, and treated like a tool.

advice: Listen to the the great and tenured employees, because when they're leaving in droves

cons:

pros: JPMorgan is a strong firm in the financial services industry. They operate in many cities making relocation possible for personal reasons. Benefits are in line with the industry for the most part.
cons: Just like all large firms what team you are on will dictate your experience. I enjoyed multiple roles within the IB. The culture of the private bank wasn't quite as relaxed. Work life balance was non existent a few years ago but getting better.

summary: My experience with this company has been great I have learned so much and so many areas of opportunity to grow
pros: Limitless lines of businesses  throughout the company, company takes care of their employees and is willing to help them grow and develop
cons: Pay isn't very competitive against its major competition. Pay within the company is the same, at times you can have a tenured employee and a newly-hired employee getting paid around the same amount just because of the position

pros:
Very stable job. I usually have the same tasks each day so I know what I need to get done. Co-workers are awesome. 

Good benefits besides medical.
cons:
No room for advancement. Chained to desk. No room for creativity or to do other tasks not related to your desk. 

Health benefits are awful if you go to the doctor more than the average person. Wish there was an option for a non- high deductible plan. 

Salary could be more competitive with other companies in the industry.

advice: Get management trained; stop being bias; and treat all people the same.

cons: Overall Chase is a good company; but the Executive Office in Lewisville is a real mess. If you want to work 4-6 months out of a year and the rest getting paid for being on LOA then that is the place to go. Management caters to the staff and they do whatever they want. Morale is low. A real mess in this department

advice: Ask for feedback from staff while they are employed as far as improvements that can be made from the top.
pros:
The culture; I found it to be professional and respectful

Zero tolerance for gossip and other such behaviors that can wreck havoc on office morale over time

Trained managers in management positions;  not random individuals who lack required managerial skills 

An environment that encourages new ideas, creative insight, trying new approach, and welcomes fresh ideas

Flexible work schedules
cons: Felt distant from upper management

advice: Be more helpful with your employees, instead of telling them what wrong they do. I would suggest you help them to suceed. Management, be more available, your employee sucess is yours as well..
pros: The benefits are great, they have a variety of schedules.
cons: The trainings should be more in classroom and not by yourself. I feel in a classroom, if you have any questions you can be helped with a trainer. I do believe that managers that work in a call center should be more involvement with employees.

summary: Unless you like getting yelled at constantly don't work here.
advice: Always have your tellers back, don't give them crap for pleasing a racist customer.
pros:
Benefits
Vacation time 
Paid time off
Sunday's off
They provide uniform
cons:
The customers, depending where you're at customers tend to be annoying. You get yelled at for any little thing, and most of the issues you can't solve because they need back office to solve it. 
Training is terrible.
Deal with racist people, and depending on your manager you might just have to suck it up and smile.

advice:
-pay people more if they move to a job that deserves it
- it should be easier to get a VP title within the company, dont hire so many external candidates as VP who arnt qualified
pros:

-work from home on occasion
cons:

-bonus for IT employees in IB fairly low (~8% of base) for associates

pros: For this position the work life balance is great, and the benefits are pretty good.
cons: It is a huge company and the bureaucracy is often times completely maddening. It makes it incredibly difficult to get things done with any type of speed. Additionally, no one will ever care about you personally or professionally. You are just another number slaving away and there is no real career guidance or help. Opportunities exist to move up, but no one will help you to do so. Raises are non-existent.

summary: Great place to launch your career
advice: Encourage risk taking & entrepreneurial endeavors within a large company. Have more comprehensive 360 reviews with managers, peers, and colleagues.
pros:
1. Had the chance to meet Jamie Dimon at a talk he gave to the interns, which made a significant impact on my view of my career path, the economy, and humanity. 
2. Great training programs for recent college graduates
cons: Interacted directly with senior director of my group & he failed to acknowledge my name after 3 months

advice: I wish the company invests more for hiring good branch managers.
pros: Work gets easier every year. Higher commission for solid performers. No sales pressure. Employee Benefits. Reasonable company policies. Great National Sales Achiever Conference meeting. Commission sharing system with banking partners. Strong sales support from the company
cons: Rapid changes on products, systems, and other working environment. Absence of true leadership in the retail branch. It is really hard to meet a liable branch manager due to low salary for management team.

pros: The friendships I made with some but that is about it!
cons: Management does whatever they can to benefit  themselves. When it comes down to doing the right thing for the customer or benefiting Chase you are told to do what helps Chase NOT the customer. This was one of the most negative environments I ever worked in. They eliminated my position and after being with them for 6years just let me go;  didn't help with finding another job etc. The same with everyone else in my department.

advice: Stop reducing our incentives. In the many years I’ve been here you almost always reduce the amount we can earn on categories. Increase all bankers base pay And stop putting caps on the dollar amount we can earn from a single client
pros: You can make a lot of money in pvcs each month and good mobility
cons: They monitor how many calls you make, you receive, emails, appointments and your performance better be good or they will review what I mentioned earlier.

summary: I think they are a fair employer, they have great benefits and stability.
advice: Keep doing what you are doing.  I was laid off and felt there could have been more assistance in finding an internal position.  I am not a financial person, so that is why there were limited positionsavailable  I would be qualified for.  My career outplacement service was excellent.
pros: good benefits; lots of perks, very qualitied employee base
cons: Very large, different companies, so to speak (Retail, Investment Banking, etc.)

summary: I learned how to take criticism, and how to be a better team player.
advice: Workers needed to be supported! There were many times I felt frustrated!!! There was to many employees gossiping about each other's!!
pros: We worked in groups, I was comfortable asking for help. Training was excellent, I gain knowledge in each area I worked in.
cons: I worked on 3rd shift, I was exhausted, never learn how to balance work and life. The lead and supervision did not pay enough attention to what was going on the production floor!!

summary: Robust economies of scope and scale; however, pay and promotion from within needs to be looked at.
advice: Stop the lip-service and really show some appreciation around value-added initiatives and those who aspire to grow within the firm.
pros: Benefits | Experience | Networking  | Bank Holidays
cons: Tons of lip service from middle and senior management - genuine action is needed around supporting and nuturing career aspirations.  More importantly, salary compared to what the market offers is terribly low considering Chase is a fortune 500 corporation.

advice: Pay for talent, recognize it, relentlessly promote it, I saw a person promoted after being written up by HR for discriminating behavior, every one of their associates are posting out trying desperately to get away from them yet management and HR turns a blind eye, when you have some of the best talent to pull from and you chose not to and you chose to not pay, I feel this company has severe issues
pros: Relaxed atmosphere, job is not high pressure
cons: Low pay, no transparency and ideas are usually knocked down

summary: Great company, just make sure which branch you know if your branch is good ahead of time
pros: Excellent company, very forward compared to other banks. Their controls are great, with great credit products and freedom to hit your numbers
cons: If you are at a great branch in a great area, you will do well. However, if you are in a area with no many wealthy clients, you will struggle. Management should disclose this ahead when hiring you and telling you how much you are gonna make.

summary: Rewarding summer experience, but did not appropriately foster career development
advice: Praises for providing some of the most direct and candid feedback about the direction of the organization and the goals of leadership
pros: Very talented senior management, great place to work. Enjoyed the work culture, proud to be a part of the team. Highest quality professionals
cons: Not the most accomodative to facilitating the long term career goals of the up and coming undergrad work force in my particular experience/location. I believe this was an isolated experience

advice: Opportunities to advance come with time.
pros: Employee  Benefits are out standing.
cons: At any time Management will write up or fire an employee for a reason that the majority of others are doing.  If you have a Linkedin Profile you are not allowed to have one skill listed on it or you can be written up and fired because of it.  It is against their policy for you to "Share" a sharable Chase Post on Linkedin.  They write up employees for Audits for a misplaced receipt that was filed 2 years prior after the branch has passed several audits.  Stressful work environment.  All Incentives are just about taken away or pay for them is pennies.

summary: Great Place to Work and Advance
advice:
Apply 360 leadership "talk to walk" -- 
Better HR staff HR in Markets; there is 1 HR person for every 250 markets need more HR support and assistance
pros: Excellent Benefits, 401k, pension plan, PTO, Sick leave, personal leave, volunteer leave lots of career opportunities and mobility
cons: Some of the senior managers have not adapted to current trends in employment such as flexible work arrangements and remote work arrangements.

summary: Big companies have their perks and their drawbacks
advice: Let your managers manage, stop micromanaging and let the people that know the business lead the business.
pros: Good benefits and pay. A recent change in upper management will hopefully change the morale in the office from distain to hope to contentment.
cons: Morale is very low among its employees. Management says that their employees are important to them in the same breath they say mobility is really only prevalent if you're in upper management. Work/life balance is nonexistent. Employees are disposable and interchangeable as you can be picked up to join a new project with another department without warning, which as a positive, exposes you to new areas and management styles.

summary: Growth creates changes that bring on the good and the bad
advice: Give employees (who will be effected) advanced notice of changes, involve them in how changes will be made and the implementation of said changes.
pros: A large employer who is still taking every opportunity to grow and expand leaves plenty of opportunity for new and existing employees. Very employee and relationship focused.
cons: With such quick growth, a lot of rapid changes that can mess up ones daily flow and be difficult adjustment for seasoned employees.

summary: Good company, good management, not so good of a team or advancement opportunities.
pros: Large firm with lots of name recognition. Great place to start your career, compensation was good relative to the industry. Benefits were pretty good as well.
cons: Not necessarily a ton of lateral advancement opportunities. Everyone is incredibly specialised. There is also a lot of bureaucracy so things always need approval from others and can take much longer than expected or reasonable to accomplish. Stacked ranking system wasn't always fair and was fairly political.

summary: Low Pay, Old School, Restrictive Growth
pros:
+ Company name on your resume.
+ Co-workers are generally intelligent and pleasant.
cons:
+ Low-salary
+ Working from home can be risky for companies. I get that. But, if I'm in an approved group for access to various platforms, I shouldn't have to spend most of my days wondering "what will frustrate me today?"
+ Management is okay. But, there's definitely a lack of respect for your time and if you think a meeting might end on time...well, you're in for a surprise. Meetings, meetings, meetings.

summary: After 5 yrs working for the investment bank I left to restart my career, they weren't going to teach me a new tech skill
pros: Investment Bank Technology pays well, and if you play the political games bonuses could be outstanding.
cons:
Working for the technology arm of an investment bank breeds a kind of competitive behavior in tech people that is counter productive.  We we not on the same team, each person was looking out for number one.
Training was sometimes hard to get despite being required

summary: Horribly toxic, sexist, and stuck in the past.
advice: Clean house (which will never happen) and get with the times. It's not the 80s anymore.
pros: Looks good on your resume
cons: This is the absolute worst place I have ever worked. It's a good ole boys club where you only get ahead by being fed relationships/accounts. You get no help, no support, and then are made to think you're the problem. Classic gaslighting. Non inclusive, incompetent management, toxic culture, outdated notions of office hierarchy, "face time", work/life balance, flexibility, etc. ... I'm just so relieved to never step foot in that place again. I cringe to even think about my years there, that's how bad it was.

summary: Lots of mobility and growth opportunities
pros: With such a large company you have lots of opportunity to move around. Great place to start a career and figure out what you want to do. The culture is fairly young and encourages work-life balance.
cons: If you are hourly you are expected to work long hours without necessarily being compensated for your time.  Bureaucracy can be a very large issue and dealing with their many legacy systems can be very frustrating.

summary: For a bank, not a bad place to work
advice: I would consider implementing 360 degree reviews; rely on hiring more undergrads and fewer MBA students, and clean up the JPM intranet.
pros: In my department at least, everyone was highly competent and willingly part of the team.  JPM is also one of the strongest banks around, and is not at risk of going under.
cons: There was noticeable tension between finance (where I worked) and the business unit we supported, I believe this is common in the bank.

summary: Increasing focus on technology and decreasing personal interaction for clients. Cost cutting and planning lay offs.
advice: Doesn't seem like employee satisfaction is a priority.
pros: They offer typical benefits. 3 weeks vacation to start and a 5% 401(k) match(match is only made once a year).
cons: If you're not working in one of their HQ areas the opportunity for growth is very limited. There is a clear shift in company direction; it appears to be focusing more on technology development and decreasing physical branch transactions.

advice: Get rid of the idiots and promote mobility across the bank. There are a lot of smart people who want to advance into different areas but cant because there are idiots who keep them back.
pros: Great brand recognition. Tries to promote a good work enviroment. Located in a nice area and acquisition of the Bear building has its perks
cons: Fake mobility -- they make it sound like you can be mobile but fairly static. A lot of crazy managers who need to leave.

advice: Jamie Dimon is a excellent leader however he should review hiring and retention policies.  Senior IT management needs to realize that current employees are over-worked as they are not hiring at the levels to replace those that leave for better opportunities.
pros: A large diverse company with plenty of avenues/career paths to take
cons: Shortsighted on the benefits of a widespread workforce.  Focuses on having to have the majority of technical positions located in Ohio.  Have given up talented people if they won't relocate there.

summary: challenging work / life balance but prepared me with the building blocks needed in the financial services industry
advice: do a better job establishing mentor / mentee relationships for individuals at all levels.  make them feel like they have someone that is looking out for their professional and personal growth
pros:
Brand
senior management effectiveness
opportunities for advancement
surrounded by intelligent, thoughtful and driven colleagues
skillset acceleration due to velocity of opportunities
cons:
long hours
large corporate job that was very NY centric
hierachy made it very difficult to build a true mentor/mentee relationship

summary: Hard work with no room for anything outside the firm.
advice: More efficiency. Please just hire some more people or at least get the work on my desk sooner.
pros: The pay is high, and you get good exit opps. Saw some people get into top hedge funds and the like. Good enough culture compared to what I've heard from friends at other firms.
cons: Only work, no room for anything out side work. I was in investment banking and it was absolutely brutal. Working 100 hour weeks wasn't uncommon.

pros: Best team related experience I've ever had. The company provides proper training and opportunities to help you grow in many ways.
cons: depending on locality, leadership could use some improvement but when you voice that to your managers, they listen. pros:

Information and resources are at your fingertips so you can learn a lot.
cons:
My job as a Transaction Processing Specialist was very repetitive.
The company is too concerned about maximizing output from employees so even if the employee turnover is very high they do not get replacements and the ones staying get burnt out with too much workload.

pros: Benefits (if hourly), Worklife-balance (if exempt), 4w vacation upfront(if exempt or >5years if not). Career Growth until you hit Assoc.

cons: There are no real cons from my perspective. All I can think of is that they are not located in Philadelphia. Currently, they are not that fond of overtime and are paying less bonuses.

advice: Within sales and trading there needs to be a better way to place analysts on desks that they actually like. Even when people wanted to trade positions management was so rigid and tough to deal with.

cons: Easy to get stuck in a bad group with terrible management and bad pay. No internal mobility. Internal job website is a joke.

summary: Good ole boy network and lots of back stabbing

Office politics are a major pain. If you are not a politician, you will not do well here. 
Chicago culture after merger with Bank One completely ruined this company's work environment.

summary: Intense work environment with lots of opportunity to learn and gain exposure.

summary: Poor Salary No Room for growth - DMS Department at Chase HR Dept Umbrella
advice: They should stop choosing their favorites and also stop being so unprofessional. Management should also give the opportunity to internal candidates to move around within the department.

cons:

Poor salaries
Management 
Inexperienced management

Management does not care about employees

summary: Fulfilling and Chanllenging, I miss working for Chase

pros: Close knit workplace, team atmosphere with little office drama compared to my current place of employment.  Advancement for those who want it, security for those who perform.

advice: The only advice I would have is to keep up the great work. I think management was doing great.

summary: Hope, I would hope that Senior Mgt really give those a chance that are trying to move upward within the company
advice: Diversify......The corporate world should be a rainbow of influences.   So many times you hear the company preach about how everyone is encouraged to apply and yet, those that are hired look and smell like them only.
pros: Working Mom have great Benefits 12weeks of pay while on maternity leave is great.
cons: Not able to climb the corporate ladder.  So many positions are giving to outsides friends.

summary: WaMu is the biggest bank failure in history

The Managment Team is open minded, able to communicate to you professional...... and also understand the balance with work life and personal life.
cons: Upper Level Managment aka The senior management your rarely see.... Senior Managment has no idea on how to run a branch efficently

summary: Working with other systems in the bank.

cons: Company getting too big to effectively manage. Also, given size, you need astronomical annual growth in your numbers to show growth. Too many managers acting like Jamie and trying to be bigshots without a clue of what they are doing.

summary: Okay place for entry level advancement

large company with many position open at all times
good work/life balance

pros: Great systems & training in NYC
cons: You might be plugged into a branch that doesn't have enough activity, deposits, or professional staffing to help you be successful.

Provide more recognition to technology contributions.
Provide realistic career path for technology staff

Merit and performance really do matter a lot

advice: My advice would be to have a more uniform treatment of employees across all lines of business, regardless of it's effect on the bottom line as support services are necessary to keep the engine moving.

pros: Exposure to great banking standards, constant and current training, constant feedback.

Company does not pay young college/masters graduates competitively compared to peers.

advice: Pay more attention to the rank and file. Clean house at the top of the Asset Management business.

summary: Great place to work as a new grad, room to grow your career

cons: Endless trainings, lower base pay comparing to the competitors, micromanaging but it depends on the manager you have and your market director.

jobTitle: Global Finance and Business Management Analyst

cons: In the current job market other companies are paying 10-15% more, though that sacrifice is likely because you are working at the top bank.

summary: WaMu on its Last Leg as JPMorgan Chase Takes Over... Good Riddance!
advice: Learn from your mistakes... You poorly managed the company, its employees, and its reputation, and look what happened.  Improve the quality and frequency of leadership communication to keep employees informed.

Lack of understanding and appreciation for work support groups provide by Marketing and other senior leaders.

summary: Was a great place to work, sad to see the compnay go

cons: Over the past few years the company became consenus driven and mid level employees were not empoowered to make decisions, instead approvals often required upper level managment..

summary: Creative Thinkers & Innovators Need Not Apply
advice: Essential to find a place for the creative and innovative thinkers instead of only having room for the 'doers' who execute and do not question the orders they are given.
pros: JPMorgan is a large global company with continued financial stability in an unstable financial marketplace.
cons: Very little tolerance for creative ideas and entrepreneurial initiative that do not adhere to approved corporate standards.  Over emphasis on process and reporting and less on quality results and innovative ideas.

summary: Good people work there but company is too big that your voice is not heard, everything is standarized

pros: Good benefits and you leave for home and you dont have to do work at home

cons: The annual raises didn't cover how much the price of benefits went up.

pros: With the rising cost of benefits, JP Morgan's co-insurance program is one of the better ones I have seen.  You only pay 10% (no deductible required) if you see your primary care doctor.

cons: Many people say the pay is not the best. Realistically speaking we cant have it all. It's either the compensation or a comfortable environment.

pros: Got off early on Fridays due to volume of work

advice:
Demonstrates\ “team player” behavior view, individual success as imperative to group success.
be direct, straightforward, honest and polite.
pros:

cons: If you're looking to work for this company, I have some bad news for you... Thanks to unscrupulous lending practices, WaMu is no more.

summary: They pay well for a reason.

cons: Call center cubicle atmosphere. Long hours. Sedentary. Onboard training focused too much on the history of JP Morgan (the guy and the company). I think the casual dress code has been modified. Work-life balance was meh.

cons: they need to get rid of the old legacy people.  they are just collecting a pay check and talk about when it was Chase Manhatten bank

summary: A great corporate structure learning opportunity, if you can make it here you can make it anywhere
advice: Excess, greed and entitlement are never eternally granted opportunities, you may be back to square one when least expected.  Remember how you equate the lowest man in the company as someday you may need to reach out for his compasion.

Awesome benefits
Nice kept up with facilities
Friendly atmospheres
Variety of hours and shifts
