advice: Realign your focus.
pros: Company is financially stable, however, the current conditions can only continue to be profitable for a period of time.
cons: Company has grown extensively over the past 10 years.  As a result, the company's culture was gradually lost.  The employees are no longer any priority.  It is not uncommon for employees to focus on their own advancement (this is sole motivation).  The team concept is very rare.

pros: Overall, JPMorgan Chase is committed to the technology organization, which is fantastic for a non-technology company.  There are also a variety of opportunities available in different locations, technologies and business groups.  Also, as a large company, it's not hard to get the right resources and right tools to do the job.
cons: With all the lawsuits and regulations, the bureaucracy is stifling. Most of the focus is on not getting sued, rather than making client happy.

advice: If you move someone up to be a supervisor or lead, make sure they have good work ethics and have the personality to respect the people they will be "supervising".
pros: There is a lot of chance to learn to software and also chances to be creative in software development.
cons: Some employees that have been there for a lot of years tend to be lazy and get away with not doing very much. This brings down the morale.

pros: A good amount of money to spend, when you can get your hands on it.
cons: So bureaucratic it's not even funny. It runs more like a sweat shop. It's all about execution and no time for strategy or planning. The hiring practices are so inconsistent and the quality of hires is low. It's all about volume. The place is riddled with under performers but it's so big that it's easy to fly under the radar, and they do.

pros: Excellent colleagues. We had a great time working together. The company was mostly respectful of employees during a very difficult time. Everyone always pulled together to make things work. Great culture of support, fun, and of course hard work.
cons: Sad to see it end the way it did. I would have loved to have stayed on had it been possible. Working at Chase is just not the same. Much more corporate and less friendly. For that, I had to go.

summary: Great place to work if your lazy
advice: Stop playing scared. Too much animosity among co-workers. Fix your pay scale. Equal work for equal pay. If someone can't keep up, they shouldn't make MORE than those around them.
pros: Not that Chase pays you a lot of money, but they over paid you for the work that you did do.
cons: Always afraid of getting sued. Minorities rule this place. The best person for the job doesn't get the job. They have to fill the quota first.

summary: Company is too large to summarize; Depends largely on which team you are in
advice: Hire more senior management that is actually competent and doesn't just talk tough
pros:
Lots of resources
Easy to reach out to other teams
Supposedly better culture than peer financial firms
cons:
Lots of red-tape; takes forever to find and get requests approved
Your enjoyment depends largely on which team you are placed into (which for me was random because I joined fresh out of college as an analyst)

advice: District managers need to appreciate their branch managers more!  My branch manager was the best manager I have ever had in all my years of working!
pros: Based on customer service, their main focus is not sales for the tellers.
cons: Time off is a little hard because they go by seniority.   My husband had military orders and there is not a Chase at the new location.  I am very saddened to see my career end with Chase.

summary: Great for learning the industry, bad for monetary growth..
advice: Review your talent and reward those people that are true stakeholders that impact your LOB! Don't let good talent leave if you can manage!
pros: It's a global company that allows you to access every type of business.  If you want to learn it, the resources are there for you.
cons: If you don't know a significant person or negotiate your pay high when you come in, you become stagnant in your career and pay.

advice: Give some opportunity to the people who have been grateful and proud to be a part of the Chase community.
pros: JP Morgan chase is a great company to work for.  They have excellent benefits an great opportunities for advancement. The have a diversified culture and care very much about their employees.
cons: Management can be intimidating at times.  There are some Managers who work their, who don't even know who they are managing are how to solve issues.

pros: Great Financial Company. Good remuneration & benefits. Depending on the location, the jobs vary. In Houston, Tx, pretty much support roles for all levels of  Investment Banking and Trading applications, related to Front, Middle, Back office Trading. Easy going atmosphere.
cons:
One would get bored doing repetitive tasks. 
Most of the classroom training  are offered in India for employees there. 
But very recently, they have enhanced the training program, for online, self paced learning.

advice: Reward the people that count, do the work, put in the extra time, not the ones who do not threaten you.
pros: PROFESSIONAL work place   Good upward mobility and great benefits
cons:
After all the mergers (MHT, Chemical, Chase. JPMORGAN, Bear Stearns...Lot's of Dead Wood stays on while the good got cut.
Too much PC mind altering BS   They should focus more on helping people think, not telling them what to think.

summary: No back support closing down to many departments no warnings.
advice: Need to scale to all branches so that everyone is on the same page and employees know what's going on day to day.
pros: Full benefits including medical, dental, life insurance, 401K and other benefits which made for good job security.  I'm sure that's why people stay there.
cons: They were closing down to many branches and departments without warning employees which made for lousy back support when you needed help nobody was there.

summary: It wasn't what I expexectwd it to be. They promise all these wonderful things and room for advancement and what not.
pros: You make good friends while you're in training. The training is the best part about it because they do help you out at the beginning.
cons: You're very controlled in everything you do. You can't go to the restroom because you're only allotted so much time on breaks. Managers rarely there to help so you get this desperation feeling because you don't know everything.

summary: Big Bank cares for only the Big Wigs!
advice: Open your eyes and ears for many employees are manipulating incentive program with false comments and yet you are allowing because it makes you look good and your ultimate goal is annual bonus.  I find that to be an integrity issue
pros: Clientele is continuous so potential to close business very good if your a sales oriented individual with profiling skills
cons: company doesn't care for their employees!  They care only about the big wigs.  They have an incentive program that has many loop holes.  Policy and Procedure are very vague and will target investigation on one individual when so many are breaking policies.

advice: Promote from within. There always seemed to be a hesitation of promoting/compensating an employee, which could cause tension
pros: Fantastic company to work for. Forward thinking, ready to adapt and try new things if the risk is worth it.
cons: At times it can be a typical "Big corporate" enterprise. Even with their flexibility there can be a mile of red tape. Some of their systems are a little outdated, and their health insurance wasn't as good as it could have been.

advice: Get rid of the managers as they don't want to do anything. They complain to one another and collect their base salary
pros: Chase as a company is a great place to work. Offer Great benefits and chase is a good company to work for other than retail banking.
cons: Retail banking managers treat you like piece of dirt. They dont do anything and critize you for their work that they fail to do. Work more and not get compensated for.

advice: The work environment and culture is in a transition phase and every day the outlook for the firm is getting better. Keep up the good work.
pros: Excellent team based approach makes it easier to provide top notch service for even the most complicated clients. The firm is large enough to get experience in many different areas.
cons: There is a lot of competition from previous employees. The firm needs to be more appreciative to employees that are dedicated to the firm.

advice: Value your people and career advancement more.
pros: Stable job, some flexibility, you are not micro managed.  4 weeks of vacation time plus personal and sick days.  The technology is advanced and Chase has a lot of resources to help you succeed.
cons: Sometimes it can be long hours, hard to advance to other positions.  They keep eliminating jobs in the branch.  Sometimes you do not have a say in the staffing or partners of your branch.

advice: Stop nepotism. Value those employees who are not only producers but so doing the right thing for all parties involved.
pros: Great compensation. Interesting connections with investors,  business partnerships, and homeowners. My direct manager was great at providing guidance drawing on his extensive knowledge and experience plus allowed space for me to effectively do my job.
cons: Division management could be petty at times. Upper management was slow to make decisions and much less knowledge than my direct manager.

summary: Some good, more and more getting bad
advice: A lot. I'm tired of just thinking of it.  I hope they listen to the lower level employees as the VPs and decision makers thinks that the people underneath are happy but mostly they are not.
pros: Good benefits with wide variety of options in medical, dental plus the MRA funding.
cons: Depending on the line of business, the corporate sector had become toxic environment. No more flexibility and people that work hard never even get a pat on your back.  Some but not all of employees that had been there for years had become relaxed and the energy and enthusiasm of everyone is literally just fake.

summary: Many changes that doesn't make sense.
pros: A lot of opportunities within a growing company. Co-workers are great and improvements in technology are very satisfying. Consumer friendly products make it easy to sell and reach goals. Constant training about new products or enhancements.
cons: Too many practices and rules changing all the time. Doesn't provide enough stability to associates and in the end the customer feels it. Not the best pay in the industry for all the work performed and the hours. Understaffed branches.

advice: Keep doing what you are doing, what you are doing is really working, keep doing it, profits are rolling in, larger than other banks.  global
pros: Quality of life, pay, educated people, great benefits, marketing, technology is key and keeps getting updated, great place
cons: I can not  think of any, all is well at JP.  It is a great place to work.  They know what they are doing, keep doing it and it will work out

summary: It's a grind but if you can stand out there is upward mobility.
pros: Office culture is to produce results. If you aren't at the top management will be asking why and you will not advance. This is a pro for the top and a con for the under performers. You also get licenses which is beneficial for future opportunities.
cons: You are just a number and a piece of a massive machine. Everything takes a lot more time than you would expect.

pros: Great career opportunity for a college graduate. You are a contributing member to deal teams right from the get-go and become extremely well-versed in corporate finance, the latter of which is an incredibly valuable life skill. And those who excel in this environment are very well rewarded.
cons: Very challenging to manage work / life balance, although significant efforts are being made to improve the spread of workload. Also the environment can be stressful at times, so be prepared!

pros: The culture at JP Morgan is great. They promote work-life balance but also emphasize the importance of efficiency and hard work. Most of the people I have met are genuine and are willing to help whenever they can. There are also a ton of networking opportunities.
cons: It is a very hierarchical structure as are most corporations of this size, but this can cause you to be stuck with responsibilities that don't feel very meaningful.

summary: Beware of low educated managers in IT and nepotism.
advice: The nepotism in the data center was so bad, I had to live through it for over 10 years after Chase merger with Chemical Bank.  They don't recognize you for your education and knowledge just you ability to become a spy for management.
pros: good starting pay and good benifits
cons: if you don't play their games , you do not advance. Most of the managers in IT were just high school grads. They got their positions because of friendships. Lots of OT given out to the spy's as rewards. Beware of constant data center moves and outsourcing to India  to save  money.

advice: incentivize advisors to do more production by actually moving them to better territories.  Otherwise, every abled employee will reach their apex, get frustrated, and then look elsewhere.
pros: Lots of firm recognition in banking sector.
cons: Lack of progression and obvious ceiling once you've "tapped" regional book of business.  Also force you to work with bankers who tend to me lacking not only in intelligence but overall tend to be people no one really wants to trust with their money.

advice: Consider hiring and promoting people of color in every discipline of the organization for more equality.
pros: Great employment opportunities in a variety of locations and disciplines of the business .  Wonderful training opportunities to help employees hone their skills.  Great leaders in the business which has allowed the organization to become one of the best financial institutions in the world.
cons: There were not enough people of color in senior level positions.

advice: Advance the careers of people who improve the business.
pros: Will help advance your career in the future - it is a well respected company
cons: Poor management and company values. Good work is not valued; you are expected work a lot, whether or not you actually need to. Efficiency is not rewarded - if you do things well and quickly or improve processes, you are punished, as it makes your manager look bad if you are not working 10 hour days.

advice: When performing layoffs understand the real impact to the area not just the bottom line.  The Florence site performed at the same or higher performance rate as other sites nationwide. The quality level was higher than that of the other sites.
pros: Salary, environment, advancement potential, learning potential, all great.
cons: I only had one con. That was that they expected me to travel for 2 to 4 weeks at a time. As a single parent that was difficult.

advice:
-Listen to associates' issues and concerns
-Be better communicators
-Stand up against the "status quo" and bureaucracy
pros:
-Challenging work
-Good co-workers/colleagues
-Full benefits a plus
-Opportunities for growth
cons:
-Some departments: dealing with bureaucracy and red tape
-Compliance courses (following laws and regulations) can be a drag and kind of bs
-Management is not the best (personally, and I believe they don't care about my 
 concerns at work); not good at listening and communicating with associates
-Stressful work environment sometimes (during peak periods)

advice: Allow for more flexibility with your employees. These days most parents are working parents it's just the economy we live in and things do come up like illnesses.
pros: Steady work and opportunity for overtime. Many opportunities for advancement within the company if you work hard. Benefits were okay.
cons: Very little flexibility for families even if you use a sick day that is marked against you. Always sales goals to meet, usually are very realistic but can still be stressful.

advice: Train management instead of hiring friends and buddies. Create a better way to be diverse, hiring a few black spokespeople will not constitute diversity, when your African American and other  employees of color are being treated poorly and  disrespected when they speak up.
pros: Benefits are great! Plenty of vacation time for work life balance.
cons: This company has turnovers and bad management. You will not get hired based off experience or education, if you have a buddy in high places -You’re hired! No opportunities for growth within certain divisions. Merit raises are a joke. If you’re hired downtown Phoenix expect to dedicate $600+ of your earnings to parking fees.

advice: Increase salaries.  I know I'm underpaid for my industry.
pros: Culture, people, leadership, mobility opportunities.... The list can go on.  I started my career here and (unlike many in my generation) plan to finish it here too.
cons: Anticipate long hours and high demands.  The people who work here are the best in the industry, so they will have high expectations of their coworkers.

advice: Great management makes great team , learn your staff and their job. Listen to their concerns and interact with them. You're staff want's to feel appreciated and understood.
pros: During certain times of the year we have team building get together a where the upper management is involved with the different depts.
cons: Upper management isn't aware of the daily conflicts we face in each department, not enough interaction with staff, not enough listening

advice: If you are closing sites and locations, be upfront about it.
pros: Great benefits and opportunities if you are willing to relocate. The company has longevity and will be around for some time, but I am doubtful that the Springfield site will make it past the new push for a "Global Location Strategy"
cons: Local leadership is very political and operates in cliques.  There is a lot of secrecy from senior leadership and little involvement in business strategy from the ranks.

advice: Work on better tone in management communications to employees.  Also, communicate to connect with employee morale.
pros: JP Morgan Chase is overall a great place to work even though there is a disconnect between very senior management and their organization.  Excellent benefits.
cons: Downside is that pay is not on par with other similar sized companies.  Senior management shouldn't be the only ones getting paid top dollar while pennies are being pinched with everyone else.

advice: Develop current staff rather than bringing in new staff.
pros: If you like building relationship with clients and partners it will be a great fit.  You must be self driven and always hold your self accountable to making your cold calls, follow up calls, and always looking for financial solutions for clients.
cons: If you are not supported by a great team of partners it is difficult to build book alone, and have to find partners who are just as driven.

advice: Pay management more. They are your voice in this multi trillion dollar corporation. They and their employees are how you make your money. Appreciate them more not only monetarily but also in support
pros: Non-Management has unbeatable benefits, very competitive salary, great concentration on employee satisfaction
cons: Management Level has great benefits. Doesn't make up for the slavery salary you receive, the 65 hour weeks with no overtime, lack of support, denial of unemployment benefits when your position is changed or eliminated

advice: Keep up the great work.
pros: Great people. Love the atmosphere and architecture of JPMorgan.  Very proper and everyone respects one another :) Jeans for the teams who reach 100% or more productivity. Love the seasonal events and team spirit week activities.
cons: I have nothing bad to say about working at JPMorgan.  Culture promotes efficiency.  I guess the only negative thing was having some individuals being a bit domineering and it gets on everyones nerves.

summary: A big company with a lot of opportunities
advice: Perhaps a career development department would be something useful
pros: A lot of room for career development,  there are a lot of positions you can consider. The benefits are great, the coworkers are awesome. Vacation and PTO are awesome. They start you with 3 weeks of vacation.
cons: Once you are in, the pay increase is at a small rate. Sometimes it is hard to be noticed because it is a large corporation.

advice: please make sure you pay attention to your young analysts because they are the future of your company, take them seriously.
pros: go into it with an open mind and you will be rewarded. It is a big company but you should question all aspects of your job
cons: it is a big company, you can get lost in the shuffle so do things to make yourself standout, hard to get promoted, will stay at one job for a while

jobTitle: Vice President - Business Systems Analyst/Delivery Manager
advice: Location was gripe to many on the team due to move to an mostly undesirable location for most on the team.
pros: Benefit Packages are good. They allowed working remotely after proven reliability and productivity. Internal and external teams were great to work with.
cons: There is a lot of red tape for releases and much of that is for good reason. Others seem excessive. One role was not filled for many months which was critical in assisting my role.

advice: Make sure your team leads are inform of your business as usual activities
pros:
Great benefits though it didn't apply to me because I was a temp.
Guaranteed 40 hours a week and was paid every week because I was with him.
Manage to live up to their contract agreement of a year ago I was assigned to me at the beginning of my interview.
cons:
Not too professional as I expected.
A lot of vulgar language  was use.
A lot of layoffs.

summary: Great Culture, Great Place to Work
pros: If you are a self-starter and at the right branch location with the right demographic of clients, you are sure to be successful in your role. There is a lot of room for career advancement. I like that the culture has moved more in the direction of taking care of client's needs first and not just selling a product.
cons: There is hardly any room for advancement or transitioning from the retail side to corporate.

summary: Great Pay, Benefits... but lousy politics within groups
advice: Need to tighten yearly review process to create transparency and should be based on fellow peer reviews as well and not based  solely on manager review.
pros:
Reputed #1 Financial Company.
Great Pay, Benefits
cons: Depending on the group you work, there is a lot of favoritism and politics. People sucking up to managers are promoted and get to keep jobs. Qualified and deserving people who do not do politics are let go.

summary: A great place to work and advance.
advice: Communication is the key. Upper management does not communicate with team managers, leads and employees well. There's always miscommunication. Learn how to work together well.
pros: Great to employees, encourages to advance quickly, willing to work with you with schedule adherence, great team managers. Great coworkers, food days often, decent pay, over time available almost every day.
cons: Attendance is number one priority, dealing with nasty customers over the phone blaming one for declines and yelling(call center). Long shifts.

summary: I greatly enjoyed working for JP Morgan
advice: More communication. Everyone is so busy that people forget to talk to each other and just email
pros: Great experience, great culture, and a lot of opportunity to meet very smart individuals. The company hosts a lot of events for the employees and ensures they are happy in the environment
cons: Almost no one in the company takes a lunch break. Food is eaten at the desk which is challenging since you do not get a break to re-focus

advice: It's all about who you know. I've been there 8 years, and little to no advancement.  Very very bad experience and the main reason why I want to leave.
pros: The benefits are amazing the pay is wonderful health insurance is one of the best in town. They even have a pension!
cons: Favoritism, hard work is not enough. It's all about who you know. I've been there 8 years, and little to no advancement. I would mention they give nice pay raises though.

advice: Please allow some autonomy and allow your leaders to lead but also have the appropriate red flags in Human Resources to ensure fairness and consistency.
pros: Sound company with great leadership at the top. Benefits are good and they offer a match on 401K and provide a pension.
cons: As with many large companies, they seem to lose sight of particulars within groups and try and place everything in one neat box. The mortgage default group is a wreck.

summary: email came out to management; Raise the rating b/c we cant get any one in here.
advice: None; you can't tell them anything!
pros:
Lots of good benefits. 
Lots of Holidays and Vacation time.
Any you get to take a lunch.
cons: Absolutely no work-life balance.  Only top 2% in your group will get raise, lower 10% gets laid off. that's why they keep on hiring.  Spreadsheet oriented, no consideration of the human factor.  Management ideals are antiquated. they cannot think outside the box. mainly because "that's the we always done it" Philosophy  Working hours are skewed from normal bank hours so it looks like they pay more but is a shift diff for really unhealthy hours.

advice: Work with Middle Management to improve their ranks.
pros: JPMC has world class people and products. You will learn a lot no matter where you work in the company, and you can move to other positions from time to time. Top leadership has good vision and communicates frequently.
cons: Many businesses run in a high pressure mode, offering little development or encouragement except for the very top performers. There is a tendency to either micromanage or ignore most employees. Middle management tends to communicate poorly.

advice: Reduce the levels of pointless management and hold individuals accountable for their results not for the results of the people they manage... This hierarchical model is like a huge expensive telephone game.
pros:
You can make Good Money
There is Career Potential if you hang in there long enough
There is no shortage of Available resources
cons:
The legal and compliance business units were very disorganized and Lacked thoughtful leadership!

They would commission massively expensive software projects and quickly throw them away.

advice: more focus on teaching managers to manage and on rewarding different work styles and competencies; pay attention to the career paths for employees, particularly mid-career moves
pros: many well meaning employees dedicated to the work; strong work ethic and high caliber of work; some really exceptional people; highly respected firm with lots of access to outside resources.
cons: can be highly political and require lots of self-advocating/promotion; long hours and emphasis on responding to emails quickly at all times of the day

advice: Learn to listen to your employees with honesty and sincerity and not just because it's good for your financial gains. You need to practice what you preach and not use "Diversity and Inclusion" as a publicity stunt or a "camouflage" to cover-up greed and pure capitalistic principles. Promote positive social change. It's good for your "KARMA".
pros: Tuition Reimbursement, learning opportunities, and exposure to cutting-edge technology.
cons: Working overtime without pay, many managers and executives have racist mentality, career advancement is based on "who you know" and not on merits and performance, blatant display of "favoritism" and "cronyism", management is full of hypocrisy and lip-service for publicity stunts without really enforcing them internally.

summary: A good company with reliable managment.
advice:
Most all of the management staff was excellent at their job.
My only advice would be to be sure not to become micromanagers and let the programmers do their work.
pros:
They work as a cohesive team solving problems and finding solutions.
They have some impressive managers that do a great job getting blockers resolved.
cons:
The top executives where skeptical of the new hires being lazy when the pandemic made us go virtual.
Did not appreciate being doubted as being lazy.

summary: Great until you turn 50 years old
advice: Don't discount older employees they offer a lot of value, don't think of them as a number.  You have driven out the close working unit in favor of the bottom dollar.  Upper management is more worried about getting ahead and their bonus and not worried about the employee.
pros: Benefits, pay, work from home and nothing else
cons: Long Hours, short sided upper management, Overall kind of like a government agency takes too long to get anything done.

summary: Great benefits and pay, subpar experience
advice: Tell the CEO to stop running  his mouth to the wall street journal about how everyone needs to be back in the office. People are getting sick, and leaving. higher compensation can’t account for EVERYTHING
pros:
Great health insurance & benefits
Stable
Opportunities to learn
cons:
Not Covid safe / Return to Office pressure HUGE 
Endless meetings (like 6 hours a day sometimes)
Pressure to work overtime at no additional compensation
Internal toolchain, many tech skills you learn won’t transfer

advice: Make sure you come in at the proper level, because it takes forever to get promoted here.
pros: There is a great work/life balance there. Some of the people are really great.
cons: some of the people who work there have been there for 10+ years and never want to try or do anything new/different. The online teams and work is so 10 years ago and it's almost too hard to change. WAY too many layers and jobs that aren't needed and incredibly inefficient

advice: don't copy me on every email, 300/day is too many.  Get off the Blackberry.
pros: Managers get 4 weeks vacation per year, but you're lucky if you get to take them.  Full-time employees get $5000/yr toward college tuition costs, but you may not have time to attend class.
cons: Having meetings to schedule meetings and then having meetings to discuss what was discussed in a previous meeting without any progress being made.

summary: Good Company, but politics hinders its progress
advice: Focus on being transparent with management and tech devs, because Chase is large a lot of information get lost in the ether
pros:
The technology is usually up to date, with an encouragement to move their platforms to the next level.
Work-life balance can be good if managed correctly.
Decent documentation
cons:
Politics and micromanaging hinder the progression for development with constant changes in team structuring and philosophies. 
Can easily be swamped with work, with sometimes working on weekends, or overnight.

advice: Identify best practices in culture and communication, then apply them across the organization for a consistent approach.
pros: JPMorgan Chase is one of the best major banks to work for. They have a very disciplined system that drives results and performance.
cons: The company is bureaucratic and slow-moving at times. There are issues with communication breakdowns, and silo behavior across business lines. Every business does not have a consistent leadership style and approach, some are much better than others.

advice: Treat your team members with respect and actually try investing in them more. The attitude at the leadership needs to change to more of a servant leader.
pros: Great benefits and a wealth of experience
cons: The culture not pleasant. Managers dont really have an interest in your future nor do they know how to help you get there. Also when HR investigates cases of harassment they are looking for ways to protect the company not the employees who are being harassed.

advice: Flatten organization structure opening communication thus eliminating constraints put in by some middle managers who are more concerned with their kingdoms then the well being of the organization.
pros: Great benefits, including tuition assistance, vacation, stock options and bonus.  Excellent and safe working conditions with many advancement opportunities across the nation.
cons: Very competitive work environment that is high stress.  Work life balance needs to improve as employees put in extra hours to meet high demands of management.

summary: The only thing you can count on is change.
advice: Invest in the current talent at all levels. Grow your talents skills in all areas not just the firm wide canned training.
pros: Amazing group of people. Leadership is accessible. Opportunities to expand your scope for some roles.
cons: Change is constant. From leadership, to organization to criteria for promotion. Despite teams wanting training to grow professionally, opportunities or programs don’t exist. They tout wanting to retain talent but do nothing to help it.

summary: Poor management that has their favorites
pros: Decent benefits, thats about it.
cons: Management has their favorites and if your not one of them you can forget any chance at anything. Large building with over 10,000 employees and only 8,000 parking spaces. Typically you drive around for long periods of time to find somewhere to park and if your late get written up. If you work past 4pm forget about the cafe and can't leave due to the mass quantity of people in the location.

summary: Every team is different, but leadership has no idea what's going on under them
pros:
- benefits
- team mobility
- training on some topics
cons:
- inflexible remote work
- VPs are just promoted willy-nilly and most shouldn't be managers
- so much turnover it's almost impossible to get work done
- total lack of communication (and no, this was an issue before going remote)
- so much money available that when a project SHOULD fail, it will fail 3 times and still be thrown to another team as their problem

advice: Try to plan better with respect to movement of employments. Please examine carefully the trend of managers bringing in their cronies from previous companies. Particularly when these cronies are not superstars.
pros: I work with energetic colleagues. Always a new challenge. Technical support is excellent. I like the ability to work from home.
cons: The office in which I work is not cleaned regularly. Too big and so you and your ideas can get lost. Not enough activities to encourage networking. Too much politics.

advice: Communicate more to your subordinates - give them feedback and meet with them more to discuss your progress.
pros: Opportunities for advancement - one word: Mobility.  The company prides itself on finding new and challenging opportunities for its employees if they wish to transition somewhere else.
cons: Layers of management - obviously with a company this large there are going to be tons of layers of management - sometimes you may not get all the information from your manager.

advice: The company was acquired by the FDIC during a series of events. Unfortunately Executive management did not work to sell the company sooner.
pros: Opportunities for advancement provided and encouraged. When ideas for improvement were identified by employees management supported efforts to implement them if the right justifications were provided.
cons: Large company many different channels, increases inconsistencies between departments and lines of business. Resistance from some lines of business to implement best practices unless required by executive management.

advice: rating system still using curve based which is not fare. WFH policy is too loose and hard to manage. HR need to enforce performance evaluation standard.
pros: big Bank,every good internal trainings, easy to find a new position internally. Good brand name, a lot of employee WFH a lot. job security is high.
cons: firm culture is every bureaucratic, does not promote excellency. turn over rate in some group is very high. JPM salary is not as competitive as MS or GS.

summary: One of the best companies I have ever worked for!
advice: Less favoritism. Give people a chance who deserve to move up. Not just because they've been there 20 yrs.
pros: Great pay. Awesome benefits. Company takes care of you in many ways. Great collection contest. Very rewarding. Free tickets to the diamond back games. Discounts all over the place. Not to mention their lucrative 401k plan.
cons: No upward mobility. Everyone in recovery has been there for a century and doesn't plan to go anywhere.

advice: Karma baby.  Karma.
pros: Benefits are comparable to other banks, salary can be good when factoriing in bonus, large and stable (as banks go) company.  I guess if you are just out of college and don't know better or desperate for a job then this is a fine place to start.
cons: No regard for employees, HR looks for ways to get rid of employees not retain them, a New York "I'm untouchable" company attitude, customer service? What's that?, who cares if the customer closes their account, we have new accounts opening each day to offset it, upper management reeks of dishonesty and shady business practices.  High stress goals and expectations.

advice: Have a centralized career plan for each individual employee. Relocating to branches and changing management can slow down the career progress for an individual.
pros: It is a great place to work with a lot of opportunity. I would recommend working here.
cons: You need to manage your own career path. Many people get lucky and get advanced because of right place right time. Or you can be in my situation and be stuck in the same position for years.

advice: I have customers that tell me the branch is a ghost town.
pros: The monthly bonus is good and you can make some good money. Chase also has great banking products and easy to use online.
cons: They are cutting staff at the branch to make room for technology at the branch. In this role they want you to make calls and set appointments but it's hard to do that when you are the only banker and you need to work the lobby.

summary: Nice place to work with great benefits
advice: As a respected firm, employee compensation can be increased across the firm, not just for executive pay. Need to have more career-related incentives for all career streams.
pros: Challenging work with a lot of learning opportunities. Fast-paced & competitive work environment for novices and experienced folks alike.
cons: Considering its size, there is more bureaucracy to deal with as compared to smaller size firms. Difficult to get professional certifications paid for even if they are job related.

advice: no advice just positive vibes that is all I have to say about that. consider staggering hours.
pros: It's been a great roller coaster rise wouldn't trade a minute of it. Great people in a great space. Not a bad place to start a career
cons: no rest for the wicked. I'll sleep when I am dead though. Beware turning into a sheep. Always do your best and you will be noticed. Promotes from within

advice: Have a clear vision of where you want the team to go in and execute. Hire people that will help with execution and pay good employees so they want to stay.
pros: Great to work for, lots of vacation time, very flexible with regards to schedule
cons: Not very competitive with pay in relation to comparable companies. Hard to move up because there is a cap on raise when changing departments. As far as technology, they are behind.

advice: Work toward better integrating the HR functions between the business units so that employees have a better opportunity to transition to another part of the company to learn new skills.
pros: Solid compensation, great benefits, well run company. The company is very streamlined and rewards employees that truly are working for something higher.
cons: Anytime you work for a company this size, red tape will be involved. I noticed that it was rather difficult to transition to other businesses within the company.

advice: Keep doing what they're doing. JP Morgan is on top of the world for a reason, I don't see any need to switch that up.
pros: I had a great experience interning with JP Morgan last summer. Learned a ton, definitely a great spot for anyone interested in investment banking.
cons: Lots of work. I'm sure it's not like the old days where they worked interns to death (literally), but it was the largest workload I've ever had.

pros: Above average salary, excellent benefits package (affordable insurance at a bargain price, with an MRA to offset out of pocket expenses).
cons: Promises, promises. Incentives and advancement opportunities primarily pop up when the company is in danger of losing you to a competitor. Customer satisfaction is all yours, but policies severely hinder your ability to actually be helpful. Micromanagement is excessive. The culture is based on negative reinforcement. It's often difficult to take vacation time in more than one or half day increments.

summary: Great place to start a career
advice: Engage in the work, that way if you need to make substantial changes to the policy or procedure there is a working knowledge built into decision making.
pros: Office culture is pleasant and friendly. Company is big enough that there are opportunities throughout the business for growth and advancement.
cons: Due to the size of the business salaries tend to be on the lower end of the market. also, bureaucracy can be frustrating and cause issues with efficiency.

advice: Spend less time looking for the APAC cheapest source of labor and bring things near shore or back to US.
pros: Great Financial backing to perform project efforts.  Good structured governance of efforts. Diamonds no BS view on getting things done make life easier to innovate.
cons: Don't come here if you don't want to work hard.  When you no longer provide value or your more expensive then an up and comer, they part ways in a fair way.

advice: Provide more networking events for bankers and staff. Create better workshops to develop homogeneous practices and consistency of service.
pros: Training is best-in-class. Hours are set and provides for a full work/life balance. The company is heading in a direction that I personally feel is a healthy balance of corporate agenda, customer satisfaction, and employee satisfaction.
cons: Some branches are not an adequate environment for aspiring professionals. Due to the size of the company, some things take too long to implement.

advice: Listen to employee's when they tell you that they are being bullied, harassed, belittled and disrespected by supervisors.  Look into why good workers are terminated when slackers continue to cheat and lie on their time sheets.  And supervisor go along with it by signing off on the attendance.
pros: The benefits and the hours. Night shift
cons: Treatment.  Treat all employee's the same especially the one's that are dedicated, on time and willing to get the job done.

advice: -Management depends on what role you get placed in. Not much advice to provide.
pros:
-You get exposure to various roles within finance.
-Provided with intense training as well as several networking events.
-The culture is great, most people I have encountered are friendly and willing to help.
-Benefits and compensation are pretty good.
cons: -You don't really get much say as to what role you will be placed in other then submitting a preference survey which doesn't guarantee anything.

summary: Being a bank teller your the first face a customer sees when walking through the door.
pros: It's a wonderful experience to get the opportunity to help out at other branches when needed because you get to meet other people within your district and build connections.
cons: Depending on your manager and fellow coworkers some tasks can be a little challenging to perform. There's always room to better our communication skills and come through with a clear agenda of everyone's job responsibility.

pros:
-A lot of opportunities to learn the internals of financial systems and applications (System Architecture, Codebase and etc)
- Interaction with desk/traders in a high paced environment
- Good opportunity for mobility in other technical teams over different lines of businesses
cons:
- More time is spent with meetings and support rather than developing
- Bureaucracy with simple processes and pushing changes to production
- Disconnect with management and developers regarding features and requirements (i.e. overworking technical team with last minute requirements)

pros: Chase offers lots of support groups, webinars, and email materials to keep the employees engaged. Many organizations offer Fireside chats, corporate engagements, and fun activities to connect the employees.
cons: With the news from the WHO informing that pandemic numbers are declining, Chase is enforcing rapid return-to-office mandates and business as usual. As a new person to the company during pandemic times, it is hard to build a connection and get acclimated to the new environment much less the new culture.

advice: You are doing a decent job in a dying industry. High priced advice and management is not the wave of the future.
pros: Good flow of leads from bankers. Decent base salary and bonus structure.  Good software program (CFA) to help customers with planning process
cons: Horrific compliance/establish new account process. Basically a sales job. High fees for managed accounts. Hard to honestly recommend to customers that they agree to 2% annual expenses between management and mutual fund fees.

summary: Ok for silicon valley, but aim for FAANG still
advice: Fix your existing systems before trying to add new things. Add more engineering roles below managers like Junior Engineer. Let employees choose if they want to work in the office or remote (hybrid). Invest in culture and building a place of psychological safety down to the team level
pros: Work life balance for tech teams. Not much responsibility or pressure. Work day consistently ends at 4pm.
cons: None to horrible documentation. Internal tools and systems rarely work. Engineering work is 95% emailing and messaging people how to fix their existing work. Professional development is very political. Culture is a work in progress

advice: There should be a greater focus on promoting and mobility from within as opposed to hiring from the outside.  Granted its anecdotal, but there in my experience when i would interview for a role there were lots of external candidates even though I'm sure there are plenty or qualified ones at the firm.
pros: Lots of resources to help with investments/markets knowledge.  People are always happy to grab a coffee and chat about their roles and any advice they might have.  Good educational opportunities (they host a CFA class and will give some money towards classes)
cons: Large bureaucracy where it is hard to differentiate yourself or escalate issues/projects.

summary: Stay away from their call centers, they will micro manage
advice: THey should spend more time, focusing on employees who have the educational experience and work experience to promote employees within.
pros: There are a lot of opportunities and they are located all across the US. They also give a generous amount of Paid time off between vacation and sick days.
cons: SEems like you're a little fish in a big sea. Advancing career for those qualified should be easier.

advice: Great place to work for
pros:
Global scale, world class talent and our commitment to diversity shape a culture of leadership within JPMorgan Chase.
 

JPMorgan Chase has a presence in more than 50 locations worldwide and offers an exciting variety of career opportunities globally. Apply for jobs, explore different career paths, create job search agents for email notifications of available positions and learn more about all of our lines of business, as you consider joining our exceptional team.
cons: Challenging and encouraging working atm.

advice: Removing support staff and reorganizing so that their work falls on engineers is responsible for reducing productivity.  It may cut costs this year, but in the long run hiring more costly engineers is more expensive.
pros: They are trying to use modern tools and technology.
cons:
Some of their systems are old.
Removed BA & QA roles, while SE's are capable of doing the work of these positions, they are also expected to produce at the same level.

summary: good to start somewhere, not good to stay
pros: paid time off, benefits, networking, client interaction, volunteer opportunities, hours, paid holidays, financial knowledge
cons: terrible corporate ladder, short staffed all the time, bad compensation plan, unrealistic expectations, they want you to do more work for not any more money, they will hire people off the street and pay them more than you . they don't give raises and if they do its pennys. the training program is terrible. very high pressure for no return

advice: Corrective action swift and early might of kept the company around.
pros: WaMu did offer great work life balance and there was a strong sense of camaraderie within teams, especially toward the end.
cons: Work between teams was strained at times.  Senior levels promoted an evertyhing is fine atmoshpere.  Values were talked about but not consistantly applied which resulted in an atomosphere of each manager was in charge of their domanin and the variances were great.

summary: Great benefits, but poor work life balance
pros: 16 week parental leave, More than a month of PTO, 5% 401k matching, and a number of other benefits are great.
cons: The PTO is more like flex time. As an exempt employee, the work never leaves. You have to work twice as hard the next week to catch up if you take a week off. Especially since the pandemic, fast-paced environment pushes us to work after hours since we are in meetings all day.

summary: J.P. Morgan - good pay, poor choice to cut employer 401k match
advice: seek out input from all levels of employees at the firm, those actually performing the grunt work may have valuable input.
pros: Salary and bonus for last year was good considering the economic environment the firm was operating in, cannot complain about the employee benefits.
cons: Being at the bottom of the totem pole (in an entry level role) I do not get much, if any, input on issues.

advice: Stop pushing everyone to the office, start sharing the enormous company profits with the workers.
pros: It's big so some very nice people around and as with all banks, interesting challenges to modernize and be competitive.
cons: It's big so some frustratingly obtuse people around who enjoy using the bureaucracy to their advantage of doing very little -- people who create and maintain blockers, build large excel sheet solutions to track the mess and never work to kill the bureaucracy.

summary: WaMu was a great place to work.
advice: No advice.  WaMu is no longer independent company.  JP Morgan Chase has now completed its incorporation of WaMu.  Too bad.
pros: I moved from Microsoft to WaMu.  The pace was slower, but for me there were more chances for advancement.
cons: The economy and some poor strategic decisions caused the firm to be handed to JP MOrgan Chase by the FDIC.  Chase is a much less capable organization overall.

advice: Your people are your best asset.  There has been a deep knowledge dump in recent history that may cause headaches down the line.
pros: The peolpe work hard and are driven.  There is a sense of prestige for working for this company so morale tends to be high.
cons: There is seems to be inconsistency in upper level strategic planning which cause confusion to trickle down to the mid-level management

advice: Make sure to inform staff of the future workplace model.  Let employees know what will stay in the states and what will be overseas so that they can prepare, accordingly.
pros: Management is open for suggestions and believes in workplace "transparency."  If you show talent and eagerness to learn then you will be rewarded.
cons: Work hours have been extended due to staff downsizing and as many positions are being off-shored in an effort to reduce costs.

advice: Stop creating layers - there are good mid-level leaders that could be excellent promotion candidates, but I see upper management blindly creating layers where they don't have to be there (by either hiring externally or moving managers laterally).
pros:
Premium industry reputation
Relatively stable employment for the finance industry
Reasonable hours
Well organized orgtree
Easy to make lateral transitions
cons:
Bonuses dependent on manager's political standing
Surprising number of incompetent people and people not willing to help out
Work can be repetitive

advice: Management should truly develop their people. The morale is horrible in the building. Chase does some shady things in certain areas.
pros: They offer great benefits such as medical, dental and vision. 401K has a 5% match, PTO and holiday pay.
cons: Management does not have best interest at heart. I believe that if you are great asset to the department, they do everything that they can to keep you there and not allow you to be promoted.

pros: Given high amount of responsibility. Can be paid well depending on your group and business line. Exposure to senior management. Two year analyst program allows you see work in different department and explore different business lines.
cons: Your experience is dependent on your team or department. As usual IB is flush with cash and you get what ever you need. In other departments computers were at least 5-6 year old. The team changes vastly depending on departments.

advice: Offer good raises for people being promoted within the company
pros: Good benefits, being a big company there is lots of room for advancement. They value the custome alot. Alot training to improve customer servive both internal and external.
cons: Although there is room for growth career wise. The pay is not good and as you move up your salary does not move with you so much. They pay more to someone coming from outside that somebody being promoted within.

summary: Valuable time spent at the firm
pros:
Good pay. Good work/life balance. 
Internal mobility supported
Decent benefits from what I can tell compared to others.
Good retirement matching plan.
cons:
J.P. Morgan is a very, very large firm - unsurprisingly, there is big firm bureaucracy.
Sometimes it seems the balance between documenting processes and doing other "busy work" kind of paperwork occupies an inordinate amount of time compared to getting to the core tasks at hand.

summary: Prepares you for the real world
pros: You are very well compensated. It's a serious company, and if you have the drive, you can succeed here. There are plenty oppurtunities of growth here, you will go far with this company.
cons: Upper management in my department had very little knowledge of what was actually done.Also, when being trained, if you are new to the field, the associates don't keep that in mind, and assume you know all about internal systems etc.

advice: Management may need a  better understanding the daily responsibilities and work of the employees.
pros: The job has great benefits.  There is a strong sense of being part of a team. There are a lot of opportunities to take on extra responsibilities if desired.
cons: The office environment is constantly changing due to frequent changes in lower and upper management.   This can be a Pro or Con depending on the person.

summary: Overall good experience for entry level positions. Would recommend to others. Adds a lot of value to the resume.
advice: Involve the junior analysts in meetings and other communication with the client and give them more responsibility.
pros: good exposure to variety of projects and lines of business. Good rotational program for entry level analysts. Good benefits package.
cons: corporate politics a bit more than other companies. Criteria to succeed is not clearly defined and is harder than other places.

jobTitle: Chase Private Client Banker/Small Business Specialist/Manager
summary: Great Benefits - but you are just a number
pros: Best benefits and paid time off, meet a lot of interesting people and get to know them on sometimes a daily basis.
cons: Chase is such a huge corporation that everyone is considered easily replaceable and no matter how good you do, they want more. Company directive changes frequently and as whole the company is extremely restrictive. Neither the employee or customer experience is a priority.

advice: Back off a little bit and trust your employees
pros: Chase has great benefits for bank tellers but they have really cut back other incentives for new accounts and credit cards
cons: Managers need to let employees work and develop on their own a little bit rather than following every step they take. Stop running on skeleton crews as well, certain locations get busy and need more employees to make sure all customers are well taken care off

summary: Just as political as you would expect
advice: Trying caring about your employees a little instead of treating them like the numbers that you see them as.
pros:
-One of the most stable companies you can work for
-Very large infrastructure using many different technologies
-Good training opportunities
-Allows telecommuting
cons:
-Just average compensation
-Very little opportunity for upward mobility
-Upper management can be very unethical towards lower employees to reach their own goals and deadlines

advice: None - only been there 7 months but I'm loving it so far.
pros: Unlimited Opportunity.  Management is interested in my success, provides me the tools that I need to succeed, and then basically gets out of my way so I can get to work.  Great company, amazing name recognition and respect in the market place.  Aggressive pricing so I can win deals.
cons: Somewhat negative perception (hopefully only temporary) due to losing $2B recently.

summary: It was a great experience while it lasted.
advice: Ignoring risk and lending out to anybody regardless of whether they can repay the loan isn't really a good business model.
pros: I truly enjoyed my time at WaMu.  I loved my team and the people I worked with, learned a lot,  was challenged by the work I did and liked the company's culture.
cons: Getting shut down by the FDIC and being devoured by JPMorgan was kind of a downer.

advice: Set clear goals for employees.  Improve the culture/work environment to make it feel more inclusive.  Reward individualism and creativity.
pros: Excellent source to build relationships with high network clients.  Good compensation plan.
cons: Company's management lacks clear direction and managerial skillset.  The message is forever changing based on what they think clients want at the given moment.  Too political.  Not the place to be creative and an individual.

summary: do not want to do review
pros: it is not too many good reasons to work at Chase. it's good a place to start your career without any education. Base salary is very low. You have to work a lot to get some money from commission
cons: Base salary is very low. You have to work a lot to get some money from commission. it is not too many good reasons to work at Chase. it's good a place to start your career without any education.

summary: There was plenty of opportunity and diversity.
advice: Listen to the workers a little more. The people in the trenches know what needs to be done sometime.
pros: There are a lot of good people working there. They were always willing to lend a helping hand. Plenty of opportunity to learn new things.
cons: The biggest down side was that management kept cutting back resources, but still wanted everybody to still get the jib done and work a minim 50 hours a week.

advice: Spend a day or two working cases, then go back and re-write the entire procedure manual.
pros: Good benefits.  Job security, as it would be illegal for the company to offshore this particular function.
cons: Line managers have never actually done the work.  They spend all their time coming up with policies and procedures to govern those of us who have, and most of what they produce is nonsense.  Highly paranoid on the subject of risk.

advice: Listen, acknowledge and praise your employees when you make that nice bonus. The CEO took all our bonuses away but yet paid himself over $20M.
pros: Benefits, Open door policy, schedule, nice raises if you're a top performer.
cons: Only 10% of the site are noticed. I was a top performer and the staff would call me by first name. I heard so much grief of people not be appreciated or helped when needed. A lot of politics.

summary: Chase has been a great company to work for that allows multiple opportunities of growth.
advice: The C in Chase stands for the ever changing environment that Chase is a part of.  They should always find other reasonable avenues to attain quality people who support them.
pros: Open door policy to speak with upper management, ability to navigate your own team to reach expected goals.
cons: Recognition of strong employees within their field and finding a way to retain them for future growth

summary: My experience with JP Morgan Chase was very rewarding.
advice: I think it is great to offer monthly bonuses dependent upon performance.
pros: I enjoy a job that presents challenges, just as in everyday life.  My experiences in the work place have allowed me the opportunity excel in areas that I consider strengths, such as attention to detail and my ability to communicate with others.
cons: There was no opportunity for promotion once the company made the decision to close and relocate.

summary: Executive Senior Management Opportunities For Woman And Minorities
advice: Management needs to ensure diversity is included in all Executive Senior Management job opportunities during interviews and selecting candidates for positions with real interest to ensure stock holders return and opportunities for real talent.
pros: Excellent Training, Development and Support to accomplish profitability for the companies bottom line.
cons: Need more opportunities for woman and minorities to advance to Executive Senior Management roles.  They are still an old boy network which impacts overall profitability.

advice: Review company policies and should be implemented equally and fairly across all line of business.
pros: Good salary, not so much benefits, but for some its enough.  You'll learn a lot .  It has nice working place and it is a company who listens to his people with regards to its benefits. Unlimited drinks :)
cons: For some functions, needs a lot of process improvement and strategy. Process must have system in order to be effective and efficient.

advice: None....They have an established history of ignoring wisdom.
pros: The company provides industry leading products. It is easy to provide customers multiple access points from which they can manage their finances.
cons: The management is under such pressure to increase sales and market share that they often resort to ethically "grey" areas to make sales and meet their sales goals. Customers are told they are required to take products that are optional. There is no long term relationship perspective towards customers.

summary: Profitable company with good career mobility for high performers.
advice: Leaders seem to be getting tunnel vision with their new site location strategy, which leads to low morale and fear of lost jobs in the 18 non-hub areas (300+ areas across 800+ offices).
pros: Good work-life balance even at exempt levels.  Lots of Locations + Many Employees = Good amount of networking opportunities.
cons: As with any large firm, bureaucracy runs rampant in some parts of the organization.  Too many silos.

advice: I can't believe I was here for 5 years....It is better almost everywhere else. It is a robust bank/business though but at the expense of talent retention due to the stated cons. (Retail Space) It could be vastly different in other areas of the bank.
pros: Allowed me to develop my communication skills and have better dialogue when gauging different people.
cons:
No Flexibility
Low Compensation
Micro-Management
Scripted sales pitches that make you sound like a machine
Sales "huddles" that are repetitive and do absolutely nothing

summary: Godo place to once you have experience
advice: Show recognition to employees
pros: Great benefits, enormous company, great environment. Good place to start, or end, I wouldn't say to stay your entire career
cons: For entry level positions salary is low. As an applications developer, you learn quickly their technology stack and soon enough you will be one of the main developers of your team. Your pay rate will not change much.

jobTitle: Assistant Vice President Site TeM Operations Manager
advice:
Promote team work and a casual friend work atmospher as it is easy to get burned out
Clear, concise, and direct communication with an open door policy at all levels of management
pros:
Challenging 
Always different and changing sceneries 
Work with people
Assisting and training others to excel
cons:
Long hours
Sometimes you really want to help a family out, but the scenario is just to outside the box and risk level
Consistently changing regulations that are not very clear and directional

advice: Must be able to adapt to change, there are many last minute schedule changes due to auditing, training, vacations, assisting other locations.  Taking vacation or time off is sometimes a challenge.
pros: Able to work without a micro manager, great staff, goals are reasonable, comfortable environment, pleasant customers, excellent benefits.
cons: The hours can be long, staff shortage, too many back office duties, many have to be get done before and after closing hours making the day very long.

advice: Continue to work hard to identify and hire the right employees for the positions. What's been done in the past won't always set you up for future success.
pros: The benefits are definitely one of the top things on my list! They put emphasis on appropriate compensation. Great customer and employee focus.
cons: I see the main opportunity as being the current state of excessive regulatory oversight. It impacts both the customer experience and at times creates an adversarial climate.

summary: A great company to work for
pros: A healthy competition amongst peers definitely motivates employees to do better. The culture is really great as hard working, high performing employees get recognized. Growth opportunity is definitely higher compared to peer companies.
cons: The middle management is out of touch with their employees and business. And work politics is so prevalent that it hinders from employees working harder because your promotion is kind of based on how close you are to the middle management.

summary: Assist affluent clients utilize the power of Chase with their entire relationship.
advice: I am fortunate to have a great manager. Most aren't quite as competent.
pros: Existing book of business, and branch with traffic. Strong team goal oriented, with recognition. Technology, and systems are consistent and easy to use.
cons: Commission structure has been consistently reduced over the years. Some retail/customer facing elements are difficult to manage. Everyone is stack ranked and there is constant pressure to perform.

advice: If I had a ready-to-use recipe for the management's success that I could package into 20 words, I would be working in management consulting or so!
pros: Overall, a positive experience in the Digital Banking organization (Chase.com). Team culture and dynamics are great.  Great benefits. Good work life balance.
cons: Technology, organizational culture, and methodologies are all decidedly showing their age. Sometimes, goals just don't make sense, but are pursued anyway because "the business" wants so.

summary: Chase Bank is overall good to work for
advice:
Work from home and other liabilities are must for Chase
Look-up the cons and do something to improve
pros:
Benefits are very good.
Pay is very good if you negotiate very well before joining
cons:
Salary is not increased every year as expected
Career growth is not very easy. They hire managers from outside instead of giving an opportunity to an existing team member 
Insurance cost is too high

advice: Stay connected with employees as to all company wide info and news occurring.
pros: Very professional, up and coming on the frontier of technology and HR practices.  Strong operation for most part across the company with enterprise-wide support of employees. Excellent benefits and resources. Much to learn from good talent that kept employees reaching to be best with pay for performance philosophy.
cons: As any large organization, much bureaucracy and can be a tough environment to work in.

summary: Decent employer not considering poor pay
pros: Open minded management, pretty flat hierarchy, good career development opportunity and plenty space for personal career advancement. Not bad in terms of work life balance. Flexible work hours and good job mobility
cons: Poor salary, esp. for someone working there long long time. A high workforce turnover. In past 7 years I have seen a couple of really bad managers including one of my former bosses. They were rude and incompetent, yelling at ppl in public.

pros: Compensation is premium for my location.  This firm is on the cutting edge where new technologies and development methods are concerned.
cons: To work here one must be prepared for change which can occur rapidly and unexpectedly.  The learning curve is steep so perseverance is required.  It will not be easy to gain the exposure needed to rise as a star performer.  Political awareness will be a necessity.

advice: You should appreciate the employees that work hard, not only the bankers that make a lot of pvc or points based on code of conduct violations
pros: It's a stable company, they offer good benefits but lately,  I would say the last 3 years the employee experience is going down
cons: You don't feel appreciated from upper management,  I work so hard, 6 months without a manager and I don't get a promotion to branch manager yet

pros: Great Benefits, flexible with taking time off.
cons: Lots of managers that have no experience in the field they're managing. The company feels too big with too many people. Very bureaucratic and impersonal. No one really has a firm grasp on what's going on or is knowledgeable enough to answer questions. They won't help you work on a career path, uncompetitive salary, you'll learn a lot of internal systems that will be useless experience if you apply somewhere else.

advice: Take better care of your employees. Other than health benefits there are no incentives to be an employee at Chase.
pros: I have been trained how to talk down anow angry customer and research complicated situations.
cons: Too much stress. Too much pressure on employees. Not enough back up from management or corporate. I feel like a puppet on a string. I don't get paid enough to have so many medical problems attributing to all the worry associated with my position.

advice:
Strive for inclusiveness (the head and the heart of leadership). Tendency to source feedback from the same constituents or by email alone.

pros:
Strong 401k match - 100% of 5% + 3% of your salary for 1 to 9 years of service.

Time off - start with 4 weeks vacation
cons:
Work/Life balance can be a challange

Runs lean in terms of staffing. Poor metric design to determine needs.

Procedures and guidelines change daily.

pros: Decent pay and opportunity to make more if you work in a rich community

advice: Go back to school and study the proper methods of motivation and management.  Try to change the company from within to view the employee as their most valuable resource.

advice: They should listen more to their employees and be more open to change.
pros: The pay was good. Manager worked well with you as far as time off.
cons: Poor communication between managers and employees.  Employees overworked with no compensation.  No concern for the quality of work and all they cared about is their matrix.  No balance between work and personal life.  Too much paper work to get anything done.  Witch hunts were common.

pros: There are many opportunities at JPMorgan & Chase that people can pursue. I've seen rank and file staff climb the ranks to become Operations Managers. It really depends on how well one is able to own their own career and development.
cons: There's a lot of competition out there. The company hires great people and it's not easy to get ahead because there are many other employees who are getting better every day.

advice: Take care of your top performers, otherwise keep losing them and wasting time on new trainees
pros: If you want to step into the banking world, I think Chase is a good start. You will learn how tue banking world works.
cons: They don’t appreciate the employees who have been with the company for a long time and their experience. They loose great talent because of not taking care of their top performers .

advice: No advice needed,  company does not exist any longer as an entity.  It is now a part of Chase Bank
pros: Benefits,  corporate culture was superior, a willingness to train employess,  co workers were very competant, knowledgeable and easy to get along with
cons: corporate leadership was not looking at the big picture or focussed on the needs of the employees.  When the company went down employees were left holding the bag

advice: If you focus on making your team feel happy and supported you can avoid frequent turn arounds.
pros: The company offers great benefits and PTO. The teams that I have been working with are phenomenal but there is a ton of competition within the markets
cons: It seems as if there is room for growth and promotion but you receive a lot of resistance from upper management. There is hardly any support to move forward

summary: Review of a position at JPMorgan Chase for a professional with 5-7 years of experience.
advice: Focus on building your core to be strong and smart. There is a serious lack of respect for selected senior management that do you have the technical skill set and are not acting as resources. Promote change.
pros: Reputable company, job security and location
cons: No mobility for superstars, incompetent managers, lack of resources, subpar quality of people, terrible tuition reimbursement programs,

summary: The company tanked for a reason
advice: Should spend more time reviewing viable and effective strategies rather than playing politics.  Also, there should be greater control over internal growth, which occurred too quickly and resulted in a highly disorganized structure.
pros: A lot of vacation days, sick leave, and holidays.
cons: HIghly political work environment, little recognition nor reward for hard work, poor upper management, highly disorganized, and basically ineffective.  As the results speak for themselves in 2009.

advice: Listen to your employees more - take input.  Keep them better informed about company actions or though process.  It often was a vaccum of information that left people guessing a lot.
pros:
Many different things to get involved in
Good amount of vacation time
Can learn a lot in a short period of time
cons:
New York focused culture - Chicago appears to be viewed as a second class citizen
Very competitive culture that doesn't always lend itself to teamwork

advice: There's a reason our mgt is fighting FINRA every other day, thats becuase we to often dont do the right thing for our customers.
pros: The benefits are the main reason to work here, hours are not that bad, but those are reall the only reason to work here.
cons: Turnover is high and their concerned about one thing, making money.  You are much better of finding the same job at another company.

summary: Great company, but good things only last so long!!
advice: great job on recognizing talents and promoting form witin. Your best staff was from day one hires, great PACE mamangement training program as wekk
pros: Compensation structure was amazing, full range of products and services, and the ability to run each branch as your own business
