advice: Work on updating technology, make career paths more defined, hire better people in back offices, make a better incentive plan, start competing more with other banks(even if deposits aren't needed).
pros: Encouraging culture, vast reach to relocate, decent benefits
cons: Old technology, have to move around a lot to move up, terrible incentive plan, not competitive on consumer side, back offices cause more client issues than they resolve

advice: Stop micro managing your employees and treating them like little kids. If you can't trust your employees don't hire them
pros: It is a good company with a lot of great products to offer to customers.
cons: The management is horrible. They micro manage everything and treat you like you are in middle school. From corporate all the way down to branch managers

summary: If you are looking for instructional design opportunity, keep looking elsewhere
advice: Organize your priorities and communicate better when changes will affect people's jobs.
pros: Benefits, good cafeteria, four weeks vacation, flexible work schedule
cons: Instructional designers are treated as training developers. Mortgage Banking is one of the worse environments I've worked in a long time. Management is very disfunctional and employees are disconnected. There is no team work and no room for creativity or innovation.

summary: Good Company to Work For But Can Be Better
advice: Stop lowballing the mortgage banking/servicing employees. To kept talent, you have to pay for it.
pros:
Plenty of job opportunities to move around and advance your career.
Working for a reputable bank looks good on your resume.
cons:
Typical workplace politics at times. 
A lot of the department don't communicate with each other. 
Can get lost in the shuffle due to business need.

advice: The common message for any grievance is "that's just the way it is".  When you know a majority of employees are unhappy but refuse to do anything, talent is going to go where they are appreciated.
pros:
Much lower stress
Lots of people to work/learn from
Stable company
Pretty hard to get terminated after your 90 days.
cons:
Health Insurance
Internal Promotion very difficult and convoluted
Slow to adopt technology
Merit compensation has a glass ceiling.

advice: Maintain a constant loop of communication with not only your managers but also those that grind for you. Loyalty and respect is yours if you exercise this more often.
pros: Diversity, leadership, military friendly, challenges
cons: Some managers are promoted too quickly and cannot manage talented associates instead treat them as a threat. This should be an opportunity to develop them and move them up the ranks to strengthen the business unit.

summary: Great experience to build a book of business. The company has a great investment philosophy and investment expertise.
advice: Train the bankers to form better habits while profiling, and make sure the branch manager holds licensed bankers accountable for setting weekly appointments for Financial Advisors.
pros: Easy access to prospects with money who already have relationships with the company.
cons: Integration can be a challenge, and you have luck of the draw with your bankers for referrals.

pros: A technology professional with a strong record of success providing on-going application support for global systems ensuring that business requirements are met. Strengths include maximizing global system accessibility, performance and communication levels, making sure that applications and systems run efficiently to support global trades, batch runs, transaction processing, account activity management and processing for mortgages, money markets, CD’s and other customer driven requirements.
cons: not available. not available. not available

advice: Minimize obstacles where possible. Listen to the lower-level or younger generation of employees.
pros: Plenty of opportunity to work in many different areas and lines of business.  Good chances for mobility and promotions.  Great benefits and networking opportunities.
cons: Sometimes it can feel easy to get lost or unnoticed in such a large company.  Can be political, lots of red tape and hurdles to get things done.

summary: Good company with a great reputation and pride
advice:
Consider strategic reduction in work force to make the firm more nimble and fast
Better training needed for managers
pros:
Brand
Good leadership and strategic business planning
Great execution and cares about internal employee
Great for internal career mobility
cons:
Fast paced - sometimes crazy pace - everything needs to be done NOW
Work-life balance could be challenging
Too many cooks in the kitchen - bloated  organization that slows down the pace

summary: Good Entry-Level Job Out of College
advice: Higher Pay for personal bankers.  Create more programs for people to move across the organization (consumer banking to auto finance or investments), rather than only "up the ladder" in a branch or district.
pros:
Great Colleagues
Strong shift from hard sales to customer service
Good training and learning opportunities
cons:
Hours, bank is open from 9am-8pm M-Fri and 4pm on Saturday
Hard to get time off
Customer Service (dealing with the public)

advice: Layoffs and advancements need to be really looked at hard. Some if not most employees would rather take a hit to the income and increase incentives vs a full out layoff.
pros: Great people to work with and some of the upper management is fair. Casual environment.
cons: Production expectations are very challenging. The Mortgage division has too many changes to the operating systems. Job security and poor. Advancement is challenging.

advice: Reward those who have shown loyalty and dedication, and place those who are knowledgeable in the right roles.
pros: The pay and benefits are great! Great teams and lots of opportunity to advance your career.
cons: Some managers don't care for you name until they need your help. Advancement is hard unless you're with the "in crowd."

pros: very strong leadership, very diverse, lots of opportunity to get involved with side projects, very challenging in a 'push your limits' kind of way, real focus on career development
cons: can be scattered and unfocused, you will definitely work hard, very challenging due to constant management shuffling, so many resources available but not a lot of guidance

pros: Structured, Disciplined company.  Regulatory Controls and Risk Avoidance policies are in place.  A lot of talented resources. Career mobility is encouraged.
cons: Extremely political, especially at higher levels. Forced distribution is strictly followed during performance evaluations, despite the rhetoric of it being a "simple guideline". Work-life balance in technology organizations is non-existent.

summary: Great environment to work and grow.
pros: JPMC is a great company for learning and developing a career. The company is huge and the possibilities are vast. They focus on mobility. Flexible work hours.
cons: As all banks, excess in regulations makes the environment extremely complex and difficult to navigate properly. Long learning curve, management changes take a lot of time.

summary: All depends on your direct manager
advice: Employees matter.
pros: All the perks of working in big company: free access to NYC museums, 401(k) match, bonuses, internal mobility, etc.
cons: Very uneven culture, you are at the mercy of your direct manager, if you have a good one, great, if not, a nightmare.

advice: Micromanagement can be improve
pros: a lot of opportunities to pursue within the company. Trains you to develop sales skills and how to handle tough situation.  Good incentive programs, discounts, retirement plans and health insurance for part time. Everyone you meet at a chase branch is friendly.
cons: Must be able to work and stand long work days.

advice: More attention to the development of youth. More opportunities and transparency regarding compensation would be nice. Clearer guides to promotion requirements.
pros: Good mobility and development of young employees. Good benefits of working at a large bulge bracket and prestige that comes with job.
cons: Hierarchy decently rigid. Difficult to advance faster than the set promotion schedules. Politics of company annoying to navigate through.

pros: Training program was good. Fellow bankers were very helpful while in the branch. Hour were good, with rotating days off.
cons: The  bank loaded the branch with too many bankers.  Never had my own desk due to the number of bankers.  This made reaching goals vey difficult at a location with limited new people moving into the neighborhood.

advice: Better organization and planning.
pros: Volume of work was constant and heavy, requiring talent and skill. Most supervisors on hand were very helpful and understanding.
cons: The high volume of work also created unrealistic expectations and oftentimes the inability to meet certain quotas produced the need for overtime. Individually, the supervisors were mostly competent and nice. Collectively, however, management and organization had issues.

advice: Spend better so that people do not have to lose their jobs due to poor management
pros: Great Pay and Professional Atmosphere. Large company so lots of movement available
cons: Training not the greatest but as is the case with most large companies. They try hard to fill this gap but not at the simplest level - actual job training.

advice: Try to remember staff members are not numbers on a spreadsheet, treat as humans with life ups and downs.
pros:
Meet some great people. Nice work environment.
Can be challenging and rewarding.
cons:
Some very nasty politics in high level management in practice. Treat people as 'resources' - numbers on a spreadsheet.
EOY review & force ranking is soul destroying on both side, reviewer and reviewee.

pros:
Managers are great at helping you get past any roadblocks and try to support you in various ways.

Resources, if available, are very helpful on completing projects outside of their current scope.
cons:
Attempting to get additional resources to help out on projects can be difficult.

Multiple online training lessons can take up some time out of your day.

advice: Put the customer first. To much "put them on the back burner we have to much to handle right now" makes the job harder than it should be. Staff appropriately, make customers happy.
pros: Pay and benefits were above board, a lot of nice people to work with.
cons: The company was very disorganized when it came to efficiency, communication and customer relations.

summary: Great Place to start off career
advice: Focus on making leaders and allowing greater career mobility instead of tagging someone to a particular type of product/asset class/function
pros: Great learning experience combined with immense exposure. International coverage and clientele base depending on the type of role
cons: Difficult to figure the best career path because of too many options, some favoritism exists too

pros: Individual incentive plan. You can make a lot of money if you have the right set of skills and work harder than others.
cons: Incentive plan is getting worse year over year. There are very limited amount of managers who knows how to help you to develop your career path. Others are......"???"  HR...they are super powerful...

summary: If you find right manager, its a very good company to work for.
pros: it has flexible work hours, recognition for what you are doing. This is true for most part, but depends on your boss and department.
cons: its a big company, with bureaucracy. You have to learn to navigate it and use it to your advantage.

summary: An average place with an average culture
pros: If you are employed in a money-making department, chances are you will receive an above-average treatment and entertain an upward career evolution trajectory.
cons: If you are not employed in a money-making line of business. chances are you will be better off looking for opportunities elsewhere. The same holds true if you prefer more compact, personable and better-than-average environments.

pros: Great benefits, fantastic commitment to training.
cons: While there is a lot of talk of time management, employees are left to fend for themselves to meet aggressive timelines of a fast-paced, corporate structure. While we are encouraged to take time off, it's rare to see management acknowledge unrealistic time constraints and put more emphasis on get-the-job-done and less on get-it-right-the-first-time.

advice: Reduce the 15 layers of management to 3 or 4 that you can actually reach
pros: Direct management is great.  Colleagues are great. Benefits are very good as well.
cons: Higher management is completely disconnected from what you do on a day to day basis.  They try to BS their own sales people by making our payout a mystery calculation.

advice: I can't say I have any advice really. Things are as they are for better and worse.
pros: Free-thinking, everyone is approachable, open communication, feel valued. Corporate life is a lot worse in a lot of other places.
cons: Things move at the speed of bureaucracy, tons of work can get done and end up meaning nothing, innovation is punished by bureaucratic hurdles

summary: Great benefits and very competitive salary
advice: Make it a priority (scorecard item) for your managers to develop their staff.  Managers show up to 360 review sessions unprepared.
pros: Opportunities to work on large budget international projects.  Internal job opportunities - possible to apply for jobs in different departments.
cons: Fellow employees getting laid off due to operational efficiencies or role getting sourced oversea location.

advice: implement positive reinforcement to encourage more referrals for the tellers; have management involved and step in to support tellers as needed.
pros: Great training provided on an off-site location; company provides uniform annually (don't have to purchase clothes to adhere to dress code); flexible in terms of work-life balance; good retirement benefits.
cons: Low morale amongst the team; no incentive to meet goals; politics within management

advice: Listen to the employees and treat them all the same playing favorites is mot professional. Managers throw their weight and higher management play favorites also.
pros: Good pay,, day shift 7am -3:30p
cons: People are messy and in you business always.  On the production floor people are loud and lazy. Co-workers do not respect each other.

pros: Great benefits( 401K, Vacation, Sick time and personal days) great working environment. Managers are there to support you and help you grow within the company.
cons: 100% call interaction with customers. Sometimes it can be frustrating, but if you have worked in a call center before, you should know that you have to shake it off and let it go.

summary: Stressful but lot of opportunities for career growth
advice: Define the clear guidelines for growth and metrics that are used to measure performance for promotions and help employess realistically achieve those.
pros: Lot to learn and opportunities and exposure to develop leadership skills.  You are challenged most of the time.
cons: There is no work life balance.  Employees are rewarded based on the willingness to be available 24/7

advice: Consider growth an opportunity to get employee communication right.
pros: Chase has made many improvements since converting from Washington Mutual including benefits, work life balance, fairness in hiring, promoting, etc.
cons: Chase is a really large bank and has the same issues WaMu had in communicating with employees. It's frustrating to hear about company changes in the news instead of through management channels.

summary: Used to be a great place to work
advice: Make career mobility central to the employee experience.
pros: Offers the possibility of a varied career across different product areas and businesses.  Smart, talented people.
cons: The culture is risk- and innovation-averse.  Career mobility, while great in theory, can be challenging in practice.  The longer you stay there, the greater the possibility of a compensation imbalance.

advice: Make the same opportunities available for TSS employees as those for other divisions in the firm, make benefits similiar in all divisions
pros: Easy to take time off, prestige of the company, relatively secure role, financially strong, interaction with a lot of different teams
cons: limited opportunites for advancement in TSS, difficult to move from TSS to IB & Private Bank, terrible benefits, management not competent

advice: Out of that 24 billion dollar profit for 2015, after that 27 million that Mr. Dimon decided to pay himself how about a raise bigger than nickels and dimes after a 4 year freeze on raises.
pros: You can make good money if you have business development skills.
cons: Terrible management. Constantly short you on commissions. No opportunity for job growth that results in a raise.

summary: Big company bureaucracy, but good perks
advice: get on the same page so employees do not get conflicting information
pros: Above average compensation, generous benefits, flex scheduling, career opportunities. JPMC is the most stable of the big banks so job security is not on the forefront of the employees minds.
cons: Big corporate monstrosity. It takes a long time for the slightest changes to be implemented.

summary: Great company to be a part of
pros: Great company to work for, great benefits. Good pay and the people are very passionate. I would work here again but had to leave due to change in where I was living at the time.
cons: Long hours. The management is difficult to deal with sometimes. You will want to work in a very cut throat environment.

summary: My overall experience was very poor
advice: People in management positions should have a four year degree.   Education is the key to a successful company.
pros: I really do not have any good reasons to work at Chase Bank.
cons: When I worked at Easton many comments were made by people that were uncalled for and grounds for termination.  Many employees made comments about other people that were offensive.  Some employees were late to work and never reprimanded and others were. Many people were promoted due to affirmative action not because they were qualified.

summary: Good benefits, poor pay, broken promises
pros: Full time or part time, it doesn't matter the benefits are the same. It's a good job for someone single or looking to work in a bank
cons: Pay is little, too many responsibilities with little incentives, too much competition within a single location, they're cutting down staff and soon will be able to replace most people with machines

summary: Extremely satisfied with my employment at JP Morgan
advice: Socialize and mingle more often with new and entry level employees.
pros:
Top tier finance work experience at one of the most prestigious Investment Banks in the world. 
Outstanding compensation and benefits.
Encouragement by management to develop a new hire's career with the firm.
Good raises and bonuses.
cons:
Long hours.
Unorganized training programs.
Lack of training as new hire.

advice: Fight for higher pay. Don't be afraid to be in your employees  corner. Help with career progression.
pros: Good people, learned a lot of systems. Opportunity to host and lead lots of meetings. Lots of visibility to senior leadership.
cons: Bad growth. Below average pay. They don't post salary ranges. How else to know if it's a lateral or promotion.

advice: To invest on their people with inhouse training available for employees
pros: The Pros for this company are workplace environment, compensation and benefits package available for the employees, retirement package, world class facilities.
cons: The Cons for this company is lack of inhouse upskill training for their employees in which they can improve and masyer their skills in doing their job.

summary: Great company if you like structure and bureaucracy
advice: Cut the fat, use resources more affectively, and don't get any bigger!
pros: Job mobility, opportunity to learn a lot, work with some great people
cons:
Way too big and bureaucratic   
I question how some people are employed / should be employed
Some parts of the company hit a ceiling very quickly

summary: Overall , it was a good experience
advice: None
pros: I like the work hours, the training, and the team of people I worked with (both employee and management).
cons: Part of my job was to collect from people that were going through some major hardships, i.e. loss of home , loss of a love one, and/or personal despair. That made it difficult to process my job.

summary: My experience here has been amazing so far!
pros: You work with people who are as smart as you. I love how we work as a team here rather than compete with each other all the time.
cons: The work hours can be long sometimes. The work can be boring too at times but i think JPMorgan is a fun place to work at nonetheless!

summary: Good job out of college, horrendous hours
advice: Care about people
pros: Learning / experience, get paid well and can live in NYC. Lots of mobility available to move to different divisions abroad, etc.
cons: Brutal work hours and very negative culture (like all of IB across the street). Relatively anti-intellectual culture. Fair amount of painful rote tasks. Again, not limited to JPM, just all of IB.

summary: Good if you can endure till you get to the top
advice: Please increase the base pay. Cost of living is more than what is earned. People are staying at home and making more than those working.
pros:
Great employee benefits
Get enough vacation hours and sick hours
cons: Average base pay, could do better there since we are the assistant branch managers in short.

pros:
*Long term employment
*Great benefits from day 1
*paid time off and sick time from day 1
cons:
*limited opportunities for upward mobility
*Politics between the higher ups
*Older leadership that refuse to retire and want to run depts like its the 90's
*Tend to pay less for same role than other banks and companies
*Raises consist of 30-75 cents an hour

advice: After all that has happened, I am speechless.
pros: Amazing culture that promoted strong collaboration across work groups. Egos were check at the door. Had the opportunity to work along side some of the brightest and dedicated individuals in my career
cons: Short sightedness of senior management and all along telling everyone that everything was fine

advice: Too many project managers checking off the tasks and measuring the folks doing the work.
pros:
Great career opportunies
Very meaningful and interesting projects
Some highly competent people
cons:
You will constantly work nights and weekends.
A friend of mine works until 8 or 9 pm each night and about every other weekend during the year supporting implementations. 
Absolutely no work/family balance

advice: Put together a real training program. Side by sides are limited to the experience of the person you're matched up with. Essentially, each successive associate will at best be slightly worse than the one before them.
pros: Great Learning Opportunity with some really good people.
cons: Entry Level with limited growth- The only way up is out.

pros: Out of many banks I worked for Chase has been the best in the retail section for promotions and employee development. Those who complain that they cannot move up are just not the right fit or think it should be handed to them. Take charge of your own future!
cons: work/life balance nonexistent in retail banking

advice: Karma will bite you in the back sooner or later
pros: Great  benefits and great benefits
cons: Upper Management Staff are ruthless.  They have no empathy towards staff under neath them.  They are a numbers company.  As long as they have their jobs, that is all that matters.  It is a cut-throat environment.

summary: One of the best companies to work for
advice: Thank you to the CEO of Chase for giving all your employees an extra week vacation!
pros: Excellent training, easy promotions, great staff, a lot of support, In 2014 the CEO gave everyone an extra week vacation.
cons: A very stressful environment, may not be for everyone working in a call center

advice: Review policies regarding human management at the Lake Mary  camp .
pros: Good leadership at the higher echelons management , poor management at the satellite camps, i,e Lake Mary /heath row. cases of favoritism and racism  .are common place in this location
cons: Good 401k  for weeks paid vacation for staff 5 years in employment.

summary: I've had a positive experience with the opportunity to work in multiple divisions
advice: Focus on the branches. These are the people meeting with clients.  If they are not happy and motivated it impacts our reputation.
pros: Mobility, intellectual capital, strong company, mostly good leadership
cons: Raises have been on hold for the most part, fair share of politics, branch environment needs to improve

advice: Dimon came in from Bank One and really cut costs / made co much leaner...
pros: Comp in DE was fair on the Analyst level (in the 40s), however at Associate levels was below avg, especially for Associates managing a number of people (in the 50s)
cons: My direct manager made YE promises that were not kept. Mostly around Comp.

jobTitle: Licensed Relationship Banker - Small Business Specialist
pros: Good commission incentives.  If you are a top producer you can make good money.
cons: Very low salaries compared to competitive firms. Higher upside though if you can produce. Bank keeps reducing staff to cut costs. Very little resources to help service clients and deal with complex issues. Less time to focus on building your book of business.

advice: Focus cultivating middle management as much as you do on the kids in the analyst program.
pros: Exposure to senior management. Ability to work on global projects. Exposure to clients on a daily basis. Good atmosphere, if motivated.
cons: The clicks are real so learn to network and build relationships otherwise, it'll be hard to move up.

pros: It is a large corporation, and respected industry wide.  While salary is often low, they have various incentive programs that you can actually earn much more.
cons: It is often very difficult to transition to other lines of business within the corporation.  It often feels like entirely different entities.  IT is often a micro-management environment.

summary: Good, stable company employing a lot of intelligent people.
advice: Keep up the good work.
pros: Large, stable company with good opportunities for internal movement.  Many hard-working, smart people work there.  Pays extremely well depending on the specific position.
cons: High level of bureaucracy sometimes makes decision making slower.  Large hierarchy makes it difficult for upper management to hear employee concerns.

advice: Listen to the staff who are in the field with the actual customer.  They are the ones who get the feedback from the customers.
pros: Chase is very good to their employees. One of the best places to work.
cons: Lost the focus on the quality of service to our clients. Everything was driven by quantity vs quality.

summary: Supported the UAT testing for business which included end to end regression testing  and executed test plans and scripts
advice: It's always an opportunity to learn and also share your experiences with others.
pros: Ability to learn the business functionality since I was in HR most of my career.
cons: The annual compensation was very low for the position I held (Business Analyst)

advice: Be more hands on in continued development. Consoder lowering the commission payout grid for new hires
pros: Flexibility in daily schedule. No micromanagement. Extensive source of referrals to build your book of business and gain experience
cons: Tough to make monthly commission payouts early on. Little to no continued training. Bankers not always motivated to refer business

advice: in order to be successful you must have an open mind and take risks.
pros: Obviously with a large company there are great benefits and plenty of room to climb the ladder.
cons: Communication and competetive products often lack as a large company. Technology was a little behind times, but JP had just jumped into this market.

advice: Work on lining up your compensations for the position.
pros: Benefits!  They have great health benefits, life insurance policies, tuition assistance, pension(noone offers pensions anymore), just great great benefits no lie
cons: It comes with all the challenges of a call center.  After alot of hardwork and dedication your reviews come down to alot of subjective matter.

summary: Solid firm, intense environment with talented individuals.  Solid management and decent support.
pros: Had good support and access to great research, modeling tools, and a team of hardworking and dedicated workers to give a competitive edge.
cons: I felt at times that the smaller firms were easier to maneuver to bring innovative ideas to market with less management meetings to gain approval.

advice: More training. More in depth planning and better tools.
pros: Good learning experience. Small base salary. Great client base to work from due to partnership with the bank.
cons: Zero opportunity to actually advise. More of a sales role than an actual advisory role. It is easy to starve.

summary: What you would expect from a Big Bank Corporate Job
advice: Promote and pay adjust your current employees that want to work there instead of paying more for external options that are just looking for the next best thing.
pros: Great exposure to the finance world, good benefits, 401k match, many career path options.
cons: Big company mentality.  Constant change in the executive ranks.

advice: Get rid of uniforms!!!!
pros: Great benefits for part time. No sales quota. Great environment to work. Paid time sick off . Ok pay , ability to go to school at the same time
cons: The only downfall O can think of is the fact that you have to wear a uniform. And tellers are being replaced with machines .

advice: I would suggest that management not over staff when the work load increases. This appears to contribute to layoffs when the work load becomes stable.
pros: Excellent pay and training. Opportunities for advancement.
cons: The company is known for laying off employees. Many of my friends and coworkers have been laid off particularly in the Mortgage Department.

summary: Nice atmosphere, hard work pays off
pros: Team oriented, high base pay, high bonuses. Long workweeks, usually up to 100 hours per week. Nice colleagues who are helpfull and cooperative
cons: Superiors might not always be availabe for asking questions, or for discussing some issues. Working 100 +- per week might lead to a burn out or problems regarding social life

pros: I have nothing but great things to say about Chase. Such a great company, very flexible and through out all the years I worked there, I've met wonderful people, learned and grow so much in my career.
cons: Managers should look for inside talent before interviewing new candidates, there is so much potential within you own branches.

pros: the networking opportunities are good but only benefit certain lines of business
cons: The bank just gives meaningless titles with no real rewards. From all the business and companies it has acquired the firm is failing to streamline things thus making the working environment a headache. The hours are unreasonable and your schedule is dictated by the business.

jobTitle: Vice President Banker Private Wealth Management
summary: Great Company.  It is a true meritocracy.  Work hard and you will be rewarded.  Learn to work the J.P. Morgan way.
advice: Keep up the strong work!
pros: Compensation, opportunity for promotion, meritocracy, great brand and history.
cons: In the news for good and bad often as they have a bulls eye on their back being such a large company.

advice: Need to improve communication between employees and management
pros:
Getting to know the other companies inside and out
The types of dealing they have with other companies 
There are many events for networking
cons:
Its all work and no play when you are at work
Advancement placement for the company is quite difficult 
Finding out information is not easy as it should be

advice: Look at whole body of work when evaluating personnel. You can't get it right all the time but at least take a deep look
pros: Best in class name recognition. Fast paced culture and high ceiling of learning. Colleagues are smart and driven
cons: Politics and maneuvering play a part even in the lower levels. Could have better focus on development of people

pros: The benefits are awesome as well as great pay, flexible with scheduling once you have been there a little while, and loved my co-workers/team leaders.
cons: The only real cons I have is that there needs to be some more training as far as taking calls for partners and specific procedures, and the calls tend to be very repetitive.

summary: Great place to learn and grow
pros: Great work atmosphere, intelligent colleagues and emphasis on training and career development. Interesting work with lots of different career paths to pursue. Pursuit of further education and licensing encouraged and paid for.
cons: Lower pay than you might expect especially in the entry level positions. It's a really large company and it can be intimidating at times.

pros: JP Morgan Chase is a great name to have on your resume and decent place to begin career. It is a great place to learn how to stand out as a top performer among others.
cons: Contractors are definitely treated differently and are not given similar opportunities - because of culture, it is very difficult to be made a full time employee.

advice: Still the best work culture compared to other IBs. Asking for references from business for a tech reviews is counter intuitive and makes it harder to retain bright tech talent.
pros: Flexible work environment, opportunities for internal mobility and great people to work with (technology and business alike).
cons: Not the most competitive pay and hard to get a promotion.

pros: Good benefits, monthly incentives depending on your branch location.
cons: Company is very controlling in what to say and do. Monitor your social media, advancement to become a manager and going to call center, bank brings a lot of people from out of town for promotion. Bank makes rules One Size Fits All, and it doesn't work.

pros: Benefits are great & the vacation time is unlike most you would get coming in to a new company. Upon starting you receive 3 weeks of paid vacation.
cons: Company is not supportive of employees. Sometimes very hard to find other opportunities within your department or within another department. Pay seems to be well below what it should be.

pros: Working with great colleagues and having decent benefits made this position a good fit for me. Although I was here for less than one year, it was a positive experience.
cons: The technology was quite outdated and the disparate systems could make the job challenging at times. Overall, I found the job quite enjoyable although my commute was a bear.

pros: Listens to employee needs, fosters a collaborative environment, keeping up to date with current trends, employees were treated as if we are all business partners who have a responsibility to care for the business and I personally feel like I am held with a high regard.
cons: Our facilities in our location (Philippines) needs upgrading. That's it.

advice: Give finance function the respect and compensation that it deserves!!
pros:
- Ability to leverage brand name to get a much better job after a few years
- Benefits are decent
cons:

summary: The worst place I have ever worked
advice: You need to rethink everything.
pros: Just the benefits package and nothing more.
cons: I don't even know where to begin ranting about the Chase Wholesale Lockbox. The job creates an environment where people hate one another, sabotage one another for favoritism status, wish ill upon their bosses and even cry during lunches and breaks, it is simply disgusting. The process and quality and productivity expectations change so rapidly that it is impossible to settle into your job. The quality and productivity expectations are unrealistic based upon how random the work is day-to-day, so unrealistic that it is impossible to advance your salary (this is probably on purpose so the bank can make more money). Favoritism is absolutely out of control, from certain shifts getting all the easiest work to one screw-up employee getting fired, to another screw-up employee getting a new function. The team-leads also would take easy work from one person and hand it off to someone else who was closer to them, screwing up productivity for anyone who got stuck with the hard stuff. Work was not distributed in a fair manner even though all openers had the same expectations. Only openers can receive errors, mail-sorters, who typically make all the mistakes, are exempt. The over-time is also out of control. Working third shift and 10-14 hours a day, 5 days a week, it is impossible to have a social-life while working this job. Work-life balance simply does not exist and over-time pay is quite poor due to a lousy starting wage. The company seemed to have a habit of raising expectations right before bonus payouts and salary increases as if to keep the wages low. Any errors you make last a year and keep you for advancing. Management also tried to force people to switch shifts and take a pay decrease by threatening to draw names from a hat if they didn't get people to switch shifts. Management threatened to fire an entire new hire group weeks after starting the job due to failed expectations on quality. At this time, work was supposed to be checked before leaving the building, but errors were still getting out. The person who was supposed to check the work but let the errors out got employee of the month for their efforts. The department later removed the quality check process while then also increasing productivity and quality standards. Anyone who makes more than 6 errors in a year is fired. Simply put, it was the worst job I have worked to date. This department is crooked in so many ways, you cannot pick one thing.. I have never seen lower morale at any other company I have ever worked for. Avoid lockbox like the plague.
